candidates.name: alsa-lib 'linear' rate converter (pcm_rate_linear.c linear_expand/linear_shrink behind plug)
candidates.where: libasound.so.2.0.0 (alsa-lib 1.2.15), internal rate plugin that plug inserts when the app rate has no codec row (36 kHz measured; before patches/0074 also 22.05/24/32 kHz)
candidates.apps: any SDL1/SDL2 app whose rate is outside 8k/11.025k/16k/22.05k/24k/32k/44.1k/48k/96k (e.g. 36 kHz), plus any not-yet-rebooted board without 0074
candidates.heat: MEASURED: ~1.85 us per output frame (~590 cycles), about 8% of a core at a 44.1 kHz output (artifacts/audio/first-principles-2026-09-27/REPORT.md sec.3); 36 kHz mono arm path cost 2.66 us/sample = 9.56% of a core, 22.05 kHz mono via linear 4.31-4.50 us/sample = 9.5-9.9% (raw/tone-h2-sinf.txt)
candidates.pathology: alsa-lib's generic sample path converts through per-sample label-dispatched get/put macros with per-channel area stepping; ~590 cycles for what is two multiplies and an add per channel. Integer-only, so the cost is dispatch/addressing overhead, not math
candidates.replacement: An external ALSA rate plugin (libasound_module_rate_s31lin.so, selected by defaults.pcm.rate_converter in the lean /usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf we already ship) implementing snd_pcm_rate_ops convert_s16 for interleaved S16 with the same integer interpolation arithmetic as linear (same pitch/weight fixed point, same input_frames/output_frames rounding); alternatively copy-patch linear_expand/linear_shrink bodies in libasound by full-body signature
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED ~20-40 cycles/frame vs 590 -> recovers ~7% of a core per converted 44.1 kHz stream; 0 for native-rate apps
candidates.exactness: bit-identical output samples and identical frame accounting (input_frames/output_frames, period sizes, delay) versus alsa-lib linear for every pitch; drop-in only if selected through the same plugin API so plug's negotiation is unchanged

candidates.name: alsa-lib route plugin mono->stereo (snd_pcm_route_convert1_one) and plug-chain area copies (snd1_pcm_areas_copy/write_areas)

candidates.est_gain: INFERRED ~100 of 110 cycles/frame -> ~1.3-1.5% of a core per 44.1 kHz mono stream
candidates.exactness: exact: identical sample duplication (ttable 1.0 weights), identical frame counts and period geometry seen by the app

candidates.name: ALSA SNDRV_PCM_IOCTL_SYNC_PTR on every avail/hwsync (no status/control mmap on riscv)
candidates.where: libasound hw plugin sync_ptr1/snd_pcm_hw_hwsync -> kernel sound/core pcm_native.c snd_pcm_sync_ptr, snd_pcm_stream_lock_irq, ioctl entry (flash)
candidates.apps: every audio app; worst for 512-frame-period SDL apps

candidates.pathology: upstream pcm_native.c only allows the status/control page mmap on x86/PPC/Alpha, so alsa-lib falls back to a trapping ioctl for every pointer query; each is a trap plus flash-resident entry code on a board where a syscall costs microseconds
candidates.replacement: Allow the coherent status/control mmap on this SoC (a single shared, coherent L1 D-cache across harts, big-ideas.md:31/53) so alsa-lib reads hw_ptr/appl_ptr from shared memory; if patching sound core stays forbidden, an own loadable helper exposing a read-only status page plus an s31fp interposition of the hw plugin's sync path. Previously closed as 'kernel policy' (frame-path-plan.md:32-38), so this is an owner ruling
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED 0.5-4% of a core depending on period size (bounded by the measured ioctl shares above)
candidates.exactness: identical hw_ptr/appl_ptr/avail_min/state values as the ioctl returns; ordering guaranteed by the same memory barriers alsa-lib uses on x86

candidates.name: musl float libm evaluated in soft double: sinf/cosf/sincosf/tanf
candidates.where: libc.so exports sinf/cosf/sincosf/tanf (-> __sindf/__cosdf/__rem_pio2f with __adddf3/__subdf3/__extendsfdf2); callers: tiopex AngleVectors/R_RotateBmodel/R_EntityParticles (11 sincosf sites), OpenTyrian (imports sincosf), any per-sample synth
candidates.apps: sdlquake/tiopex, tyr-glquake, OpenTyrian game logic, audio test clients, X desktop toys
candidates.heat: MEASURED: one sinf ~9 us (~3000 cycles) on the board, 40-50% of a core at 48 kHz when called per sample (first-principles REPORT sec.3, raw/tone-h2-sinf.txt); QEMU icount per call (this survey, build/cloud/probes/wide-census/icount-sysroot.txt): sinf 2104, cosf 2049, sincosf 4024, tanf 2789 vs musl's float-only atanf 74, fmodf 81; software-Quake libm bodies 0.91% of CPU0 (perf-review-2026-09-23.md:100, not split float/double)
candidates.pathology: the FPU is single precision but musl computes the float API in double_t, so every sinf is ~8 soft-double helper calls plus a double polynomial
candidates.replacement: FPU implementation: Cody-Waite reduction and float-float (fmadd.s exact FMA) polynomial giving ~2^-40 relative error, then a Ziv rounding test; when the float result is provably the same as musl's (i.e. correctly rounded and musl's is too) return it, otherwise tail-call libc's sinf. Unary float functions have 2^32 inputs, so equality with musl can be verified exhaustively on the host (answers the roadmap's A5 deferral for the unary cases)
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED ~60-150 instructions per call vs 2000-4000 (15-30x per call); app-level ~0.3-0.8% of CPU0 on software Quake; large for per-sample float synths
candidates.exactness: bit-identical to musl for all 2^32 inputs (exhaustive host check), same fflags; delegate when frm != RNE; W7 in the narrow roadmap only speeds these ~2.5x via v2 helpers

candidates.where: kernel riscv_timer/tick_program_event -> sbi_set_timer (flash c0027e48 per perf-review:110) -> OpenSBI
candidates.apps: all (every timer reprogram)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: M-mode firmware 1.3% (prof9), 1.6% (prof8), 1.1% (tgpfs2) of all samples, contents unresolved (no OpenSBI symbols in the tree)
candidates.pathology: no Sstc, so each clockevent program is a trap to M-mode; also any emulated CSR or misaligned access (the S31 core traps unaligned halfword reads, S31_hosted_transport.md:132) lands here

candidates.exactness: same event times within timer resolution

result.coverage_notes:
What I searched, and where each number comes from. MEASURED means it is taken from a cited repo file or from a QEMU run in this survey. INFERRED means reasoned from those.

Profiles read and re-resolved:
- GLQuake/QuakeSpasm h1s: prof8 and prof9 PROFILE.txt. For prof9 I re-resolved the library symbols with my own resolver, build/cloud/probes/wide-census/res.py; memset 0.69% matches the recorded 0.7%.
- kfast prof10a/b/c, prof/prof1 and fs1, and tyrquake tgprof/tgp14/tgp16/tgpfs2 (tgpfs2.prof.txt).
- The phase5 qsr instruction-count tables and the present-prof lvdesk/glxgears notes (gl-plan-2026-09-25.md:770-790).
- Doom kernel /proc/profile (frame-path-plan.md:136-138).
- Windowed prboom pcsample (worklog-2026-09-19.md:292-300).
- OpenTyrian audio-thread pcsample (worklog 09-20).
- The TyrQuake SDL2 h1s (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:976-992).
- The 48 kHz audio shares (audio-48k-plan:200-265).
- The perf-review T1.7 libc/libm shares.
- The first-principles audio report (artifacts/audio/first-principles-2026-09-27).
- The accel-plan copy table and the current-state read/copy_to_user measurement.

Caveat on the re-resolution: re-resolving prof8, prof10a/c, prof1, fs1 and tgp* against the nm files in the tree gave implausible symbols (libasound snd_seq_*, libc regex/ptsname_r/log2f). The nm files and maps do not match those captures (different builds, overlapping PIE maps). I used only their curated PROFILE.txt/prof.txt tables and discarded the rest.

QEMU instruction counts are in build/cloud/probes/wide-census/icount-sysroot.txt (source ic.c). They were taken on the cloud QEMU sysroot's upstream musl 1.2.5, not the board libc 352e9417. They are instruction counts only; QEMU has no timing model. The getenv figure (3493) is inflated by QEMU's host environment and is not used.

Disassembly of toolchain libc 6041b2cd (libc.dis) was used for:
- the soft-double call inventory of each libm function;
- memset/strlen/sqrtf (sqrtf is already a single fsqrt.s);
- the mutex paths.

It is NOT byte-identical to the board libc. The toolchain libc also carries xesploop (esp.lp) in 55 places, including __addtf3/__subtf3/__multf3 and the dynamic linker. The overlay binaries' arch tags show no xesploop, so the board libc is probably built without it; this was not verified. It would be a correctness issue, not a speed one, if it held.

tiopex-quake.dbg disassembly gave the helper call-site census: long double in CalcSurfaceExtents, sincosf x11, atan2 x5, sin x8, __muldf3 106 sites.

Already covered or excluded, so not repeated as new work:
- the libgcc soft-double helpers, fused chains, OPL, floor/ceil/trunc and placement;
- 64-bit libgcc division, killed in the roadmap because libgcc already uses divu (the kernel's generic __div64_32 is a different routine and is listed);
- SDL_MixAudio for OpenTyrian/tiopex, killed in the roadmap;
- memcpy/memchr/memcmp/strcmp/memmove and clocks, shipped in v3;
- the double libm set, which is W7 (listed only to place its heat).

First-party code found hot but out of scope for a preload, to fix at source:
- lvdesk xshm_request copy+hash, 2.8-3.1% of GL samples;
- lvdesk double poll, about 1.3% of the machine (perf-ideas-sweep #7);
- xlite XShmPutImage extra flush, about 2.8% (perf-ideas-sweep #8);
- TinyGL/libGL internals;
- s31route's own write batching.

Could not reach:
- The kernel tree (linux-71-port) is not checked out, so the kernel candidates marked INFERRED rest on upstream knowledge.
- No prboom binary or function-level profile exists (the W0b gap).
- No libSDL, libSDL_mixer, libasound or libz binaries were in the repo (nm only for some), and I did not fetch upstream sources.
- No OpenSBI symbol map, so the 1.1-1.6% M-mode share is unresolved.
- No profile of a PNG/zlib, fontconfig or desktop-client workload.
- OpenTyrian's game thread (25% of a core) was never profiled.

Scratch is only under build/cloud/probes/wide-census/. No tracked files were modified and no board tools were run.

candidates.name: __clock_gettime inside musl (timed waits, timespec_get, clock, ftime)
candidates.where: board libc.so (musl, board build 352e9417; toolchain copy is not byte-identical): __timedwait/__timedwait_cp (src/thread/__timedwait.c:42), timespec_get.c:8, clock.c:8, ftime.c:7. These calls bind inside libc, so s31clk's exported clock_gettime/gettimeofday/time never sees them
candidates.apps: SDL2 timer thread (SDL_timer.c:202 calls SDL_SemWaitTimeout, which calls sem_timedwait), SDL2 SDL_CondWaitTimeout (syscond.c:107), SDL1 SDL_SemWaitTimeout and SDL_CondWaitTimeout (libSDL-1.2 imports sem_timedwait and pthread_cond_timedwait, from artifacts/gl/glquake/nm/libSDL-1.2.so.0.11.4.nm), and any app calling clock() or timespec_get
candidates.heat: Coverage gap MEASURED structurally under QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-syscall/clkcov-strace.txt). A preload answered every exported clock entry without a syscall. Even so, sem_timedwait and pthread_cond_timedwait each still issued 1 clock_gettime64(REALTIME) syscall, and timespec_get and clock() one each. Per-call cost MEASURED on the board (artifacts/s31fp-vdso/clock-board-full.txt): syscall clock_gettime64 2514 ns on CPU0 and 3049 ns on CPU1, against vDSO 429-564 ns. Call rates on the board are unmeasured
candidates.pathology: Each timed wait traps once just to turn an absolute deadline into a relative one. The kernel text for that trap runs XIP from flash. SDL has already read the clock through the vDSO to build that deadline, so every timed wait pays for two clock reads, and one of them is a trap
candidates.replacement: (a) Copy-patch __clock_gettime's entry in libc's text (it is an XIP cramfs page, so this is a private COW page costing 4 KiB of RAM) into a jump to the s31clk vDSO adapter. That covers every internal user at once. Or (b), better, copy-patch __timedwait_cp to issue FUTEX_WAIT_BITSET|FUTEX_CLOCK_REALTIME (or MONOTONIC) with the absolute deadline, as glibc does. Then no clock read happens at all
candidates.est_gain: About 2.0-2.6 us saved per timed wait or clock() call (MEASURED per-call delta). The total is small unless an app waits with a timeout at a high rate (INFERRED <0.1% for current games)
candidates.exactness: The same kernel timekeeper data is read, so values are identical. EINVAL for a bad clock id and the ETIMEDOUT/EINTR returns of __timedwait must be kept. The absolute-bitset variant changes where the deadline is computed (kernel instead of user), which can only make the timeout more accurate. Cancellation-point behaviour of __timedwait_cp must be kept

candidates.name: SDL 1.2 timer thread SDL_Delay(1) poll loop
candidates.where: libSDL-1.2.so.0.11.4 (SDL 1.2.15), src/timer/unix/SDL_systimer.c:197-206 RunTimer: while(timer_alive){ if(SDL_timer_running) SDL_ThreadedTimerCheck(); SDL_Delay(1); }
candidates.apps: Any SDL1 app that initialises SDL_INIT_TIMER. The sdlbench canary does. prboom, TyrQuake/tiopex and OpenTyrian do not (perf-review C88)
candidates.heat: MEASURED on a synthetic frame (docs/sdlbench-results-2026-09-13.md:79-80): SDL1 indexed frame 54.415 ms with timers against 20.833 ms without, median of 5. For the current game set it is 0 (no timer init)
candidates.pathology: About 1000 nanosleep(1 ms) wakeups per second even with no timer registered. Each one is a hrtimer arm (an SBI ecall, since there is no Sstc), a timer IRQ, a context switch at 57-157 us, and a wake. On one or two harts that competes directly with the game
candidates.replacement: Interpose SDL_Delay. RunTimer reaches it through the PLT, so the preload can catch it (INFERRED: SDL1 builds with -fvisibility=hidden and DECLSPEC API symbols, and this needs checking on the board binary). When the caller is RunTimer (identified by return address inside libSDL's RunTimer range) and no timer is armed, block on a condvar signalled by interposed SDL_SetTimer/SDL_AddTimer. Otherwise use clock_nanosleep(TIMER_ABSTIME) to the earliest deadline
candidates.est_gain: Up to 2.6x on the synthetic timer case (MEASURED gap). 0 for today's games
candidates.exactness: Timer callbacks must fire no later than they do now, keeping SDL1's 10 ms TIMER_RESOLUTION rounding and the callback-on-timer-thread semantics. SDL_Delay for every other caller passes through unchanged

candidates.name: mallocng mmap/munmap churn on malloc/free of 4 KB-128 KB blocks
candidates.where: libc.so mallocng (board libc has __libc_malloc_impl@0x21172, alloc_slot, __malloc_alloc_meta: artifacts/gl/glquake/nm/libc.so.nm). Cause: single-slot groups are unmapped on the last free (free.c:148), and MMAP_THRESHOLD is 131052
candidates.apps: Any client that allocates and frees a mid-size buffer per frame or per request (candidates: xlite/ximage buffers, libpng rows in lvdesk thumbnails, SDL surface conversion, SDL_mixer chunks, TinyGL). No per-app count exists
candidates.heat: Pathology MEASURED under QEMU on upstream musl 1.2.5 (build/cloud/probes/wide-syscall/mchurn-result.txt): a malloc(n)+memset+free loop costs exactly 2 syscalls (mmap2+munmap) per iteration for n = 4000, 20000, 65536 and 131000, even with 1-8 live same-size objects. For 8192 the churn went away with 1 or 8 live objects but not with 3. Board rates are unmeasured. Tangential MEASURED costs: under GLQuake the function-call IPIs (TLB shootdowns) are 121/148 per s (current-state GLQuake churn table), and kernel memset (page zeroing) shows in the paging/mm bucket
candidates.pathology: Every cycle costs two syscalls (1.5 us entry floor each, mm code largely in XIP flash), n/4096 zero-fill page faults, and a cross-hart TLB shootdown IPI on munmap when the process has threads on both harts
candidates.replacement: Add an exact malloc shim to the preload: a bounded per-size-class cache of recently freed mid-size blocks, for example at most 2 per class and at most 256 KB total, trimmed on a timer or on a memory-pressure signal, and passed through to musl otherwise. Alternatively a copy-patch of mallocng's okay_to_free/bounce heuristic so single-slot groups for classes above 4 KB are kept one generation
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured. Each avoided cycle saves 2 syscalls plus faults plus an IPI. It only matters if a hot app is shown to churn, so the first step is to extend rootfs/syscount.c to count mmap/munmap/madvise per app
candidates.exactness: malloc/calloc/realloc/free/malloc_usable_size/aligned_alloc/posix_memalign must interpose consistently. calloc must zero reused blocks, since fresh mmap memory is zero and reused memory is not. RSS trades against the 15.4 MB budget, so the cache must be tiny and self-trimming

candidates.name: XLITE ring doorbell: eventfd write + ppoll + eventfd read per XSync
candidates.where: xlite/xlite.c:535-600 (xlite_ring_bell, xlite_ring_read_more: read(efd_in), then poll(p,2,1000)) and lvdesk/xshim.c out_try (server bell)
candidates.apps: Every X client through xlite: prboom, tiopex-quake, QuakeSpasm, SDL1/SDL2 apps, GL clients
candidates.heat: MEASURED: ppoll (the wait for lvdesk's reply) is 1.8% of Quake's main thread, about 1.05 ms per frame (perf-review-2026-09-23.md:166, 481). Cross-hart crossing about 165 us, two per XSync (C94 evidence). Futex/eventfd is 0.095% of CPU0 (C26 refuted as a CPU sink)
candidates.pathology: Both directions pay an eventfd syscall plus a sleep/wake. eventfd wakes are not WF_SYNC wakes (X2-23), and the reply usually arrives within a few hundred us, often from the other hart
candidates.replacement: Spin-then-sleep (C44). The waiter publishes a 'spinning' word and polls the ring head for about 100-300 us by rdtime (45 ns per read, MEASURED). The writer skips the eventfd write when the peer is spinning. A futex on a ring word (one syscall to wait, one to wake) replaces eventfd + poll + drain read
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED (C44 review estimate): Quake +0.3-2%, Doom +1-5%, bounded by the measured 1.8% ppoll share and CPU0 idle
candidates.exactness: Protocol ordering must stay exactly as it is (sig acknowledged before looking, xring.h). The HUP/conn-lost detection via the socket's POLLRDHUP must be kept while spinning

candidates.name: XSync round trip per SDL frame (GetInputFocus)
candidates.where: xlite/xlite.c:963-980 XSync = GetInputFocus + blocking reply; SDL1 XShmPutImage + XSync every frame (SDL_x11image)
candidates.apps: SDL1 apps (prboom, tiopex-quake, QuakeSpasm); SDL2 X11 similar
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 2.2 X-socket syscalls per frame before the ring (frame-path-plan.md:25-29). ppoll is 1.8% of Quake's main thread. Late present +13% on Doom showed that the wait sits on the critical path
candidates.pathology: Every frame blocks the game on a cross-process round trip, which is two scheduler hops at 57-157 us per switch plus about 300 us of wake
candidates.replacement: XLITE_NOSYNCWAIT (perf-review T2.4, not yet written): XSync flushes and records shm_seq, and the wait is deferred to the next XShmPutImage on that buffer, where it is required. That keeps back-pressure through a presented-counter handshake
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ceiling +2.5% absolute on Quake from the ppoll share. Review range 0.5-6% Quake and 2-13% Doom, with disputed magnitude
candidates.exactness: The SHM buffer must not be reused before the server consumed it (flicker was seen with MIT-SHM adoption). The deferred wait must give the same visible frames. X error delivery timing moves later

candidates.name: select(fd+1, {xlite efd}, 0,0, {0,0}) in SDL1 X11_Pending on every SDL_PumpEvents
candidates.where: libSDL-1.2.so.0.11.4 src/video/x11/SDL_x11events.c:906-930 (X11_Pending); xlite XConnectionNumber returns the ring eventfd (xlite_req.c:2190)
candidates.apps: All SDL1 X11 apps (prboom, tiopex-quake, QuakeSpasm, OpenTyrian)
candidates.heat: Count INFERRED from source: SDL_PollEvent pumps on every call, so at least one zero-timeout select per frame, plus one per event. Per-call cost unmeasured (1.5 us syscall floor MEASURED; do_select/eventfd_poll path cost unknown)
candidates.pathology: A trap into XIP kernel text to ask a question whose answer is already in shared memory (the ring's sig/used words)
candidates.replacement: Preload select(): when nfds-1 is exactly the xlite ring eventfd, it is the only fd set, and the timeout is zero, answer from the ring through an exported xlite query (dlsym, e.g. xlite_ring_pending) with no syscall. Pass through for every other case
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED <0.1% per app. Low priority, cheap
candidates.exactness: Readiness must equal what eventfd would report: counter>0, or ring bytes pending, or closed. The fd_set contents and return value must be identical. Only the zero-timeout single-fd form is short-circuited

candidates.name: hrtimer (re)programming by SBI ecall for every nanosleep/SDL_Delay/poll timeout
candidates.where: linux-71-port drivers/clocksource/timer-riscv.c:48-65 (no Sstc, so sbi_set_timer) and :149-157 (stop ecall, then event_handler); OpenSBI esp32s31.c:166-196
candidates.apps: All sleepers: SDL_Delay (SDL1/2 nanosleep), usleep, poll timeouts, lvdesk, audio threads, plus the kernel's own hrtimers
candidates.heat: MEASURED: M-mode firmware is 1.6% of samples in GLQuake (artifacts/gl/glquake/prof8/PROFILE.txt) and 1.1% in tyr-glquake (tyrquake/raw/tgpfs2.prof.txt). riscv-timer runs 391 IRQ/s on CPU0, with 417 hrtimer events/s under GLQuake (current-state.md GLQuake churn table). sched/tick/timer bucket 8.6-9.9%
candidates.pathology: Each timer arm, and each timer IRQ's stop, is a trap into M-mode through firmware on a hart whose kernel text is in flash
candidates.replacement: C16/X1-38: a clockevent driver of our own that programs a SYSTIMER comparator from S-mode (driver owned by us, not a mature-driver patch), and drops the redundant stop-ecall per IRQ
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED 0.3-1% of CPU0 (C16 estimate). The HRTICK-off arm measured +1.3%, inside noise (current-state.md:222-232)
candidates.exactness: Clockevent semantics (oneshot, min delta, SMP per-CPU comparators) must stay the same. The timer must not fire later than it does today

candidates.name: Per-process timer slack for SDL_Delay/usleep/poll sleepers
candidates.where: prctl(PR_SET_TIMERSLACK) from the s31fp constructor. Current slack is 50 us everywhere, s31-bt 0 (current-state.md:219)
candidates.apps: Games and desktop clients that sleep (SDL_Delay in OpenTyrian service_wait_delay, SDL1/2 audio fallbacks, lvdesk poll)
candidates.heat: Unmeasured split. hrtimer_wakeup (sleepers) is one of the sources of the 417 hrtimer events/s MEASURED under GLQuake
candidates.pathology: Distinct expiries for sleepers that tolerate ms-level jitter each cost a timer IRQ plus ecalls (see the hrtimer candidate)
candidates.replacement: Default a larger slack (e.g. 500 us-1 ms) for non-RT threads of preloaded apps, behind an env toggle. Leave SCHED_FIFO/audio threads at 0
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured. Likely <0.5%. Runtime toggle, so it is a cheap A/B
candidates.exactness: Only lateness changes, and POSIX allows it. SDL_Delay still waits at least the requested time. Audio-period threads must be excluded to avoid underruns

candidates.name: Coprocessor (PIE/HWLoop) save/restore ecall on every user-involved context switch
candidates.where: linux-71-port arch/riscv/kernel/esp32s31-ext.c:59-86 (hook always on); OpenSBI s31_coproc_save/restore 0x40380918/0x403809a8
candidates.apps: All, per switch
candidates.heat: MEASURED 477 context switches/s under GLQuake (current-state.md:215) and up to 804/s at busiest. C17 estimates 2-12 us per user switch. All M-mode 1.06-1.6% of samples
candidates.pathology: An M-mode ecall on every switch between user tasks, even when neither task has touched PIE/HWLoop state
candidates.replacement: Lazy ownership: trap on first use, so switches between PIE-free tasks skip the ecall. This pairs with PIE-free string routing, since s31str already routes the lent CPU to scalar
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED 0.1-0.6% of a core (C17)
candidates.exactness: PIE/HWLoop register state per task must be preserved bit-exactly. The earlier hook-off attempt crashed bluetoothd in libc (current-state.md:5926-5947), so the lazy trap must cover musl's xespv routines

candidates.name: libc-internal PIE string calls (xespv memcpy/strcmp/memchr) trap-migrating off CPU1
candidates.where: board libc.so: __riscv32_xespv_memcpy64 plus xespv strcmp/memchr/memcmp/memrchr, reached by internal calls (stdio, qsort, realloc, printf_core) that s31str's exported-symbol interposition cannot catch
candidates.apps: Any preloaded process whose thread runs on the lent CPU (hart0, no PIE)
candidates.heat: MEASURED 924 PIE bounces per boot (smp-finish-plan via C17). wget 0 in 2 s. Per-app counts unmeasured (gl campaign asked for them)
candidates.pathology: Each bounce is an illegal-instruction trap, then migration to the PIE hart, then re-execution. It is a hidden syscall-like cost of about 165 us or more (INFERRED from the cross-hart crossing)
candidates.replacement: Copy-patch the entry of libc's internal xespv routines (a COW page of XIP text) to jump to s31str's rseq cpu_id dispatcher (PIE on CPU1, scalar on CPU0)
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED small overall (<0.5%). It removes a tail event
candidates.exactness: Byte results are identical (s31str already proven: 1.3M calls, 0 mismatches under QEMU). Migration between the check and the call is non-atomic, as in s31str, and falls back to the existing trap handler

candidates.name: Wait/wake kernel spine (futex, eventfd, do_select) executing from XIP flash
candidates.where: System.map: futex_* c00705ca-c0073c4a, eventfd_write c010194a in flash (C26); try_to_wake_up/__schedule already in RAM
candidates.apps: All threaded/IPC apps: SDL audio thread, TinyGL MT worker futexes (gl/tinygl/source/s31_thr.c:126-130), xlite ring, lvdesk
candidates.heat: MEASURED: same-hart futex round trip 491 us, cross-hart 871-889 us (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:1549). kernel syscall/fs/net bucket 1.1-1.3% (GL profiles). Futex+eventfd CPU share 0.095% of CPU0 (C26 refuted as a CPU sink)
candidates.pathology: The wake path mostly waits on I-cache refills from 80 MHz flash. The C23 prelock showed the 16 KB I-cache is already the working set
candidates.replacement: Put kernel/futex/*.o and fs/eventfd.o (8-10 KB) into .text..fast, measured with pingpong -p (private) under same-boot A/B/A. Note the SHARED-futex bias in pingpong (perf-plan:1150)
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED -10-25% per futex round trip by analogy with softirq.o (675 to 542 us). CPU share is small; the latency is what matters
candidates.exactness: No semantic change, text placement only. The C23 lesson applies: any RAM text displaces cache, so it must be measured

candidates.name: gettimeofday/clock_gettime vDSO path itself (PLT, then preload, then vDSO generic code)
candidates.where: rootfs/s31fp/v3/s31clk.c:24-60 calling __vdso_clock_gettime64 (470 bytes, artifacts/s31fp-vdso/kernel-inspect.txt)
candidates.apps: SDL1 SDL_GetTicks (gettimeofday; libSDL imports gettimeofday, not clock_gettime), SDL2 SDL_GetTicks64 (clock_gettime MONOTONIC_RAW, SDL_systimer.c:58-140), lvdesk main loop (2 per poll iteration, lvdesk.c:15860-15865), tiopex Sys_DoubleTime
candidates.heat: MEASURED cost: vDSO 429-564 ns per call against raw rdtime 45-47 ns (clock-board-full.txt). Rates: lvdesk about 200 clock calls/s (current-state.md:3567). Game rates unmeasured
candidates.pathology: About 10x the cost of the counter read, from the generic dispatch, the seqcount on a PSRAM vvar page, 64-bit mult/shift on rv32, and two indirect calls
candidates.replacement: Inline MONOTONIC/RAW/REALTIME reader in the preload: map the vvar data once, seqcount loop, rdtimeh/rdtime/rdtimeh, mult/shift, with the kernel formulas copied exactly
candidates.est_gain: About 0.3-0.4 us per call. At the measured rates this is <0.01% of CPU. Only worth doing for apps that hammer clocks
candidates.exactness: Must match the kernel's vdso_calc_ns exactly (mult/shift, cycle_last, masks, clock-mode checks) and fall back when vdso_clock_mode is NONE. It depends on a private kernel ABI (vvar layout), which is fragile across kernels

candidates.name: __divdi3 / __udivdi3 / __moddi3 / __umoddi3 (libgcc 64-bit integer division)
candidates.where: Local static copies in libSDL-1.2.so.0.11.4 (__divdi3 0x43296, 0x31a bytes; __moddi3 0x435b0; __udivdi3 0x43952; __umoddi3 0x43c2e) and board libc.so (0x66614..); likely also statically linked into apps
candidates.apps: SDL1 SDL_GetTicks (suseconds_t is int64 on rv32 musl, so (now.tv_usec-start.tv_usec)/1000 is a 64-bit division); prboom FixedDiv ((int64)a<<16)/b (INFERRED from source, binary not in repo); any time or fixed-point code
candidates.heat: MEASURED under QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-syscall/ticks-result.txt): SDL1 GetTicks arithmetic is 94 instructions per call against 35 with 32-bit math, so +59 per call for __divdi3. Hot-path heat unmeasured (prboom FixedDiv not profiled here)
candidates.pathology: libgcc's generic udivmoddi4 uses table/loop clz and __udiv_qrnnd_c emulation even when both operands fit 32 bits. The S31 has Zbb clz and a hardware divu
candidates.replacement: Full-body signature match (same machinery as sigs3.h) and replacement with a version that has a 32-bit fast path (n_hi==0 && d_hi==0 gives divu/remu), a Zbb clz normalisation and a 2-step Knuth D for the rest
candidates.est_gain: About 60 instructions per SDL_GetTicks, negligible there. Potentially material for Doom if FixedDiv is hot (unmeasured)
candidates.exactness: Quotient and remainder must be bit-identical, including sign rules, INT64_MIN/-1 (libgcc wraps) and divide-by-zero (libgcc does not trap; RISC-V divu by 0 returns all ones, and that must match whatever libgcc returns)

candidates.name: sched_getcpu / getcpu
candidates.where: musl sched_getcpu makes the getcpu syscall (QEMU strace, clkcov-strace.txt). The kernel vDSO's __vdso_getcpu is only a 10-byte ecall trampoline (kernel-inspect.txt)
candidates.apps: None of the inspected nm import sets (SDL1/SDL2/libasound/libGL/quakespasm/tyr-glquake/lvdesk) import sched_getcpu. Future CPU-aware code would, and s31str already has rseq
candidates.heat: unmeasured (no importer found)
candidates.pathology: A trap to learn a value the rseq area already holds, since s31str registers rseq per thread
candidates.replacement: Interpose sched_getcpu to return rseq->cpu_id when registered, and pass through otherwise
candidates.est_gain: About 1.5 us per call (MEASURED syscall floor). Zero today
candidates.exactness: Same value semantics (racy snapshot either way). Must fall back when rseq is not registered for the thread

candidates.name: CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID / CLOCK_PROCESS_CPUTIME_ID (and musl clock())

result.coverage_notes:
What I searched: docs/current-state.md (syscall-cost sections 1189-1230, 3542-3576, 6035-6100, the GLQuake tick/timer attribution at 199-232, idle wakeups at 5040-5070), perf-review-2026-09-23 (the table and all 95 candidate verdicts in artifacts/perf-review-2026-09-23/*.json, grepped for syscall/futex/vdso/poll/yield/SYNC_PTR/rseq/ecall), perf-plan (futex/pingpong), frame-path-plan (syscount results), sdlbench-results (futex and SDL timer arms), s31fp-handoff, gl-performance-campaign, artifacts/s31fp-vdso (board clock costs), artifacts/gl/{glquake/prof8,tyrquake/raw} h1s profiles, the nm import sets of the board's libSDL-1.2, libSDL2, libasound, libGL, quakespasm, tyr-glquake and lvdesk, a disassembly of rootfs/tiopex-quake.dbg, xlite/xlite.c, lvdesk/lvdesk.c, gl/glx and gl/tinygl s31_thr.c, and upstream SDL 1.2.15 and SDL 2.32.10 sources (fetched into build/cloud/probes/wide-syscall/).

QEMU probes, all in build/cloud/probes/wide-syscall/. clkcov + fakeclk.so (clkcov-strace.txt) shows which clock reads stay syscalls once every exported clock symbol is interposed. mchurn/mchurn2 (mchurn-result.txt) shows the mallocng mmap/munmap churn. ticks (ticks-result.txt) gives the instruction cost of SDL1 GetTicks' int64 division. Caveats: QEMU riscv32 has no __vdso_clock_gettime64, so s31clk falls back there. The sysroot is upstream musl 1.2.5, not the board's 352e9417 build. Board libc is confirmed mallocng by symbol names only.

Does the shipped fast clock cover SDL? Yes for the direct paths. SDL1 SDL_GetTicks uses gettimeofday (libSDL imports gettimeofday and not clock_gettime). SDL2 SDL_GetTicks64 uses clock_gettime(CLOCK_MONOTONIC_RAW), and RV32 musl does not redirect it to __clock_gettime64 (no _REDIR_TIME64). Both go through the PLT into s31clk. lvdesk and its children are preloaded via /etc/lvdesk.env, which sources s31fp.env, and login shells via /etc/profile.

It does not cover: musl-internal clock reads (timed waits, clock(), timespec_get, ftime); CPUTIME clocks (no vDSO possible); SDL_Delay/usleep (nanosleep, a real sleep); static binaries; daemons started without the env.

Closed or refuted leads, left out of the list on purpose. SYNC_PTR ioctls: C83 was rejected, snd_pcm_sync_ptr was 4 of 12,000 samples after the s31route avail_min fix, and the kernel refuses status mmap on 32-bit time64. Syscall entry itself: 1.5 us, and it is already in RAM. A vDSO for time as a CPU win: shipped; it was rejected before only on rates. HRTICK off: +1.3%, inside noise. NO_HZ_IDLE: hangs. Shared-futex GUP: an instrument artifact of pingpong only, since musl, SDL and TinyGL all use FUTEX_PRIVATE. The tiopex usleep(1) frame-cap loop and Sys_ConsoleInput select only run above the fps cap or when dedicated. SDL2 SDL_AtomicLock's SDL_Delay(0) is used only by the timer lists. getpid is uncached in musl but has no hot caller. The DRM DIRTYFB/cursor ioctl cost is work, not trap.

Measured kernel shares in GL profiles: syscall/fs/net 1.1-1.3%, irq/exception entry 1.1-1.3%, M-mode 1.1-1.6%, sched/tick/timer 8.6-9.9%, at 477 ctxt/s. So pure syscall elimination has a ceiling of a few percent. The larger levers are wakes, switches and timer ecalls.

Not reached: the board itself (no per-app syscall counts after XLITE-RING, no mmap/munmap census, no clock-call rates per game); the prboom, sdlquake and quakespasm binaries (absent from this checkout); the libSDL, libasound and vdso.so binaries (nm only); and whether SDL1's internal SDL_Delay call binds through the PLT, which needs the actual .so. The next step would be extending rootfs/syscount.c to cover mmap, munmap, select, nanosleep, futex and clock_gettime64, and running it once per app.

candidates.name: strtod / atof / strtof (and sscanf %f via vfscanf)
candidates.where: libc.so __floatscan (1166 insns long, toolchain libc 6041b2cd @0x... via strtod/strtof/atof/vfscanf); computes in binary128 long double: calls __addtf3 x6, __multf3 x7, __subtf3 x2, then __trunctfdf2/__trunctfsf2
candidates.apps: atof: quakespasm (pr_edict.c:813/828 ED_ParseEpair, gl_rmisc.c:359-368, gl_sky.c:341), tyr-glquake (ED_ParseEpair), tiopex-quake (ED_ParseEpair x2), SDL1, SDL2; strtod: SDL2, libasound (conf parse); strtof: libXt; sscanf %f: quakespasm gl_fog.c:232, common.c:1995
candidates.heat: MEASURED (my re-resolution of the board PC samples against artifacts/gl/glquake/nm/libc.so.nm, libcres.py): __trunctfdf2 0.30% of all samples in GLQuake prof8, 0.10% prof9 (+__addtf3 0.05%, __subtf3 0.04%), 0.11% tyr-glquake tgpfs2. Outside libm, __trunctfdf2's only libc callers are strtod/vfscanf/wcstod (objdump of the toolchain libc), so the caller is INFERRED to be strtod/atof/sscanf %f. Map-load share: unmeasured
candidates.pathology: musl long double on RV32 is IEEE quad, so each digit accumulates in soft-quad. That is 128-bit soft-float emulated in 32-bit integer ops on top of an ABI that is already soft-double. QEMU instruction counts (MEASURED, lc.c): strtod("3.14159") 13,235 insns, strtof("3.14159") 13,126, atof("0.5") 8,664, and even the integer strtod("640") takes 1,266
candidates.replacement: strtof: a Clinger fast path in hardware single precision. For up to 9 significant digits with mantissa <= 2^24 and a decimal exponent of -10..0, the result is (float)m / 10^k by fdiv.s, which is correctly rounded because both operands are exact. Fall back to libc for anything else (exponents, hex, inf/nan, long mantissas, a rounding mode other than RNE via fegetround). Prototype zb.c zstrtof: 126 insns vs 13,126 (104x), 0 bit/endptr mismatches over 2,000,000 random decimal strings (QEMU). strtod: an Eisel-Lemire 64-bit integer path (mulhu) with a Clinger path as backup and libc as fallback
candidates.est_gain: Per call 50-100x fewer instructions (MEASURED for strtof). Whole-process: up to the ~0.2-0.4% soft-quad share in GLQuake profiles, plus faster map-load entity parsing (unmeasured)
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical float/double: both sides are correctly rounded, so any correctly rounded path matches. endptr, errno (ERANGE on overflow/underflow falls back), sign of zero, and fenv rounding mode must match. Fall back unless FE_TONEAREST (one frrm CSR read, ~25-30 ns); inexact flag behaviour must match (fdiv.s raises NX exactly when the true result is inexact, as the quad path does)

candidates.name: printf %f/%g/%e (fmt_fp)
candidates.where: libc.so fmt_fp (1576 insns long; __addtf3 x4, __multf3 x4, __subtf3 x4, __eqtf2 x7, plus __udivdi3/__umoddi3), reached from printf_core
candidates.apps: quakespasm gl_screen.c:471 sprintf("%4.0f fps") every frame when scr_showfps is on; pr_cmds.c:1024/1040 PF_ftos/PF_vtos "%5.1f" (QuakeC); cvar.c:439/482 Cvar_SetValue "%f"; tyr-glquake PF_ftos/PF_vtos, SCR_UpdateScreen; host_cmd.c savegame fprintf %f
candidates.heat: MEASURED: printf_core is 0.15% (prof9), 0.16% (prof8), 0.19% (tgpfs2) and 0.29% (tgprof) of all samples. The fmt_fp share of that is unmeasured (fmt_fp does not appear as its own symbol in the samples)
candidates.pathology: musl formats every double as long double (binary128 soft-quad). QEMU (MEASURED): snprintf("%.2f") 7,047 insns, "%g" 7,027, "%.1f" of a small integer 2,947, against 833 for "%d"
candidates.replacement: For double args with explicit precision <= ~17 and no L modifier, use an exact integer %f/%e/%g digit generator (Ryu-printf style, 64/128-bit integer multiplies using mul/mulhu) and hand padding/flags back to the existing printf_core logic. Simplest shape: interpose snprintf/vsnprintf/sprintf/printf/fprintf, scan the format, and only take over when every conversion is in the fast set
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured for the replacement. The ceiling is the fmt_fp part of the 0.15-0.29% printf_core share, plus lower latency for QuakeC ftos and cvar sets
candidates.exactness: Output bytes identical, including rounding of the exact binary value (musl prints the exact decimal expansion rounded per current mode: check fegetround), %g trailing-zero stripping, -0.0, inf/nan spelling, and the return value. Validate against musl over random doubles x precisions on host

candidates.name: vfprintf two-pass format parse (integer/string formats)
candidates.where: libc.so vfprintf calls printf_core twice (0x5593c validation pass with f=0, then 0x55996). vsnprintf also memsets a ~150 B FILE each call (0x57a4e)
candidates.apps: snprintf/sprintf/vsnprintf importers: quakespasm/tyr-glquake/tiopex (Sbar "%3i" several per frame, sbar.c:644/776; va(); Con_Printf), SDL1, SDL2, libasound, libX11, libXt, libXpm, lvdesk (70+ call sites), s31-bt

candidates.replacement: An interposed snprintf/vsnprintf/sprintf fast path for formats with no '$', no floating conversions and no %n: a single pass with a small fmt_u (Zba sh2add *10 idiom, 32-bit only when the value fits) into the caller buffer, falling back to libc otherwise

candidates.exactness: Byte-identical output and return value, including truncation and NUL for size limits, errno (EOVERFLOW for >INT_MAX), and all flags and widths. Easy to fuzz against musl in QEMU

candidates.name: pthread_mutex_lock/unlock on recursive mutexes (SDL_mutex, xlite_out_lock)
candidates.where: libc.so pthread_mutex_lock -> pthread_mutex_timedlock -> pthread_mutex_trylock -> __pthread_mutex_trylock_owner, and pthread_mutex_unlock (the non-normal path does robust-list insert/remove plus LR/SC a_swap)
candidates.apps: SDL1 and SDL2 (SDL_CreateMutex is recursive), libasound, libX11 and xlite (recursive output lock, current-state.md:4373), tinygl threads
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 'libc pthread_mutex_unlock + __pthread_mutex_trylock_owner are 2.6% of CPU0 in play (recursive mutexes: SDL's and xlite's xlite_out_lock)' (docs/audio-48k-plan-2026-09-25.md:177,256-258). In my re-resolution: pthread_mutex_unlock 0.12% + trylock_owner 0.05% (prof8), 0.05% + 0.04% (prof9/tgpfs2)
candidates.pathology: musl sends every non-NORMAL type through the full timedlock/trylock_owner path and keeps every owned non-normal mutex on the thread's robust list. QEMU (MEASURED): a recursive lock+unlock pair is 122-123 insns against 43 for a normal mutex, and each pair runs 2+ LR/SC loops (no AMOs are used anywhere in this libc: 118 lr.w sites, 0 amo*)
candidates.replacement: Interpose pthread_mutex_lock/trylock/unlock. Nested re-lock (type&3==1, owner==self tid): _m_count++ with no atomics and no list change. Nested unlock (count>0): _m_count--. Everything else falls through to libc, so the robust-list state is untouched. Separately (fix at source, first-party): make xlite's lock a normal mutex with an owner/depth field
candidates.est_gain: Nested case about 122 -> ~20 insns (INFERRED from the disassembly). Share of nested versus outermost calls is unmeasured, so the bound is part of the MEASURED 2.6% CPU0
candidates.exactness: musl's mutex layout (_m_type, _m_lock owner tid, _m_count, robust list links) must be read exactly as musl does. The fast path only handles states in which musl itself makes no list or lock-word change. Return codes (EAGAIN on count overflow, EPERM on a non-owner unlock for errorcheck/recursive) must match; bail to libc for robust, PI or pshared types

candidates.name: Contended mutex path in Xorg (waiter a_inc/a_dec LR/SC loops + 100-iteration spin)
candidates.where: board libc __pthread_mutex_timedlock+0x1c2..0x1fa (the samples at libc +0x5cc22..5cc5a in cursor-latency.md:92, resolved by me against artifacts/gl/glquake/nm/libc.so.nm where __pthread_mutex_timedlock=0x5ca60). Toolchain equivalent 0x5d13c-0x5d18a: waiter increment CAS loop, contended-bit CAS, __timedwait, waiter decrement CAS loop; preceded by a 100-iteration fence rw,rw spin (li a5,101 at 0x5cfe6)
candidates.apps: Xorg (input thread vs main thread), SDL audio thread, libasound
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 8.7% of Xorg's CPU samples during continuous pointer motion sit in this lr.w/sc.w retry region (docs/cursor-latency.md:91-92, xprof CPU_CLOCK, 4117 samples). The symbol attribution is INFERRED: the nm is from a libc build whose strlen address matches bluetoothd's independently sampled strlen+16, but board-libc identity is not proven
candidates.pathology: musl builds a_inc/a_dec/a_swap/a_fetch_add from LR/SC CAS loops, and the toolchain libc contains zero AMO instructions. With two harts contending, LR/SC reservation loss causes retries. The fixed 100-spin before futex wait burns CPU whenever the owner is not running (for example the same CPU or a descheduled owner)
candidates.replacement: Interpose pthread_mutex_lock/timedlock for NORMAL/RECURSIVE private mutexes with the same state machine, using amoadd.w.aqrl for the waiter count and amoswap.w for unlock (amoadd indivisibility against cross-hart stores is proven in worklog-2026-09-19.md:1275). Skip the spin when rseq shows the owner is not running (owner tid lookup is impossible, so INFERRED option: skip the spin when single-CPU-affined). Fix at source where possible: Xorg input_lock is off-limits (do not patch Xorg), so the libc-side interposer is the only lever
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured. The upper bound is part of 8.7% of X CPU during pointer motion; the real part depends on whether the samples are retries or unavoidable futex round trips
candidates.exactness: Futex protocol and lock-word encodings identical to musl (0x40000000 owner-died bit, 0x80000000 waiters bit, _m_waiters) so mixed libc/interposed callers interoperate, which is essential because libc-internal pthread_cond paths still call the originals. The spin count is unobservable. Must preserve EOWNERDEAD/ENOTRECOVERABLE handling by falling back for robust types

candidates.name: memset (not interposed by s31str.c)
candidates.where: libc.so memset (musl generic C: sb head/tail, word stores, 8 sw per 10-insn loop), toolchain 0x595f6
candidates.apps: every app and library (memset imported by 42 of the repo binaries plus SDL1/SDL2/libasound/libGL/quakespasm/tyr-glquake); tinygl glClear/depth clears dominate
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 3.31% (tyr-glquake tgpfs2), 4.38% (tgprof), 0.68% (GLQuake prof9), 0.71% (prof8) of all samples; qsproxy QEMU 3.53% of instructions (artifacts/gl/phase5/qsproxy/prof-tf0.txt:12)

(b) Investigate whether PSRAM stores are write-allocate (not documented in docs/): if they are, a cache-line-zero/no-fill path would double effective fill bandwidth. candidates.name: strncmp (not interposed)
candidates.where: libc.so strncmp (musl byte loop, ~11 insns/byte), toolchain 0x59bfe. Also called internally by getenv
candidates.apps: libXt, SDL1, SDL2, libasound, quakespasm, tyr-glquake, tiopex (FindNextChunk, S_LoadSound, Hunk_Print), lvdesk (state_get/set, ctl_line), s31-bt; 9 repo importers

candidates.heat: unmeasured

candidates.where: libc.so strcasecmp (0x597b4) / strncasecmp (0x59b4c): a byte loop with out-of-line jal tolower calls on every non-identical byte

candidates.name: strtol / strtoul / strtoull / sscanf integer conversions
candidates.where: libc.so strtol/strtoul (build a 176-byte fake FILE, __shlim, then __intscan, which calls __shgetc per character with 64-bit position counters), vfscanf
candidates.apps: libX11 (strtol, strtoul), SDL1, SDL2, libasound (conf parse, strtol/strtoul), s31route ALSA module, lvdesk (ctl_line, notify_draw, memp_sample sscanf with 22 conversions every 250 ms while the popover is open), bluetoothd (UUID/address parsing), s31-coex
candidates.heat: MEASURED: __intscan 0.03% (prof8); bluetoothd's 18.7% in sscanf/strtol/strtoul/strlen (current-state.md:6313) was the corrupt-store pathology. Normally unmeasured
candidates.pathology: QEMU (MEASURED): strtol("12345678") 232 insns against atoi's 89. strtoul hex 243. sscanf("%d %d") 1,253. sscanf of a MAC address with %x x6 2,594
candidates.replacement: strtol/strtoul fast path for base 0/10/16 on plain ASCII with fewer than 10 digits (no overflow possible): parse directly and set endptr. Otherwise fall back. Prototype fstrtol10: 64 insns vs 232. For sscanf: an interposed fast path for formats made only of %d/%u/%x/%i/%*d plus literal separators
candidates.est_gain: Per call 3.6x (strtol). Process-level unmeasured, likely small outside startup/config parsing
candidates.exactness: Same value, endptr, errno (ERANGE only possible on the fallback path), leading whitespace per isspace, sign handling, base-0 prefix rules (0x/0) and the "0x" with no hex digits edge case (endptr after the '0')

candidates.name: malloc/free/calloc (mallocng) small-object churn
candidates.where: libc.so __libc_malloc_impl (287 insns), alloc_slot (577), get_meta, __libc_free, nontrivial_free, __malloc_allzerop, and __lock around them
candidates.apps: every app and library (malloc imported by libX11, libXt, libGL, SDL1, SDL2, libasound, quakespasm, tyr-glquake, lvdesk, s31-*)
candidates.heat: MEASURED (tgprof): __libc_malloc_impl 0.17%, get_meta 0.06%, __lock 0.06%, __malloc_allzerop 0.05%, alloc_slot 0.04% (about 0.4% in total); tgpfs2 __libc_malloc_impl 0.10%; prof8 nontrivial_free 0.04% + calloc 0.04%
candidates.pathology: QEMU (MEASURED): a steady-state malloc+free pair costs 210 insns (252 when threaded). The pattern of allocating and freeing a single object in an otherwise empty size class costs 1,602-1,674 insns per pair (malloc(16)/free), INFERRED to be group release and re-creation each time. calloc(16) 1,717; realloc 16->256 2,475
candidates.replacement: A tiny per-thread (rseq/TLS) cache of the last freed slot per small size class in front of mallocng, returning it on the next same-class malloc (bounded to a few KB total so RSS does not grow), or keeping one empty group alive per class (hysteresis). Must never hold memory mallocng would otherwise return, beyond a small fixed budget
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured. At most part of the ~0.4% tyr-glquake share; the churn case is up to 7x per pair
candidates.exactness: Not address-exact (allocation addresses may differ), which is semantically allowed. malloc_usable_size, realloc-in-place and calloc zeroing must be preserved; memory is the binding constraint (CLAUDE.md), so RSS must be measured on the board

candidates.name: Float libm computing in soft-double: sinf, cosf, sincosf, expf, logf, powf
candidates.where: libc.so sinf (4 __adddf3, 4 __subdf3, 3 __extendsfdf2), cosf, sincosf (__sindf/__cosdf in double), expf (6 __muldf3 ...), logf, powf (14 __muldf3, 10 __adddf3)
candidates.apps: sincosf: tyr-glquake/tiopex AngleVectors (3 per call), R_RotateBmodel, R_DrawSprite, R_EntityParticles; lvdesk (handle); sinf/cosf/powf/expf/logf/log10f/atan2f: SDL2; powf/cosf/atan2f/log10f: lvdesk (audio slider, arcs)
candidates.heat: unmeasured (no sincosf/sinf samples were resolved in the four Quake captures; tinygl's G01 non-exact float-trig swap measured -20% frame time in tinygl, a different code path: artifacts/gl/phase3a/LEVERS.md:127)
candidates.pathology: musl's float functions deliberately compute in double for accuracy, and double is soft here. QEMU (MEASURED): sinf 2,026, cosf 1,834, powf 3,899, expf 1,854, logf 1,816 insns, against log10f 74, atan2f 103, sqrtf 7 (pure float or fsqrt.s)
candidates.replacement: Reimplement each as float-only code using fmadd.s-based double-float arithmetic that reproduces musl's result bit for bit. Unlike the double functions, float->float is EXHAUSTIVELY checkable: all 2^32 inputs can be compared on the host against musl compiled natively (the host double is IEEE-exact), including fenv flags. Overlaps roadmap W7 (rebuild keeps double) and A5 (deferred float fast path); this is the exhaustive-verification route A5 lacked
candidates.est_gain: Per call INFERRED 5-20x, if a bit-exact float-float kernel exists; process-level unmeasured
candidates.exactness: Bit-exact result for every one of 2^32 inputs plus identical fflags (inexact/underflow/overflow/invalid) and errno. If any input disagrees, restrict the fast path to a verified interval and fall back

candidates.name: getenv
candidates.where: libc.so getenv: __strchrnul plus a byte-loop strncmp over every environ entry (internal calls, so s31str cannot reach them)
candidates.apps: all 21 repo importers plus libGL, SDL1, SDL2, libasound, quakespasm, tyr-glquake (SDL2 SDL_GetHint consults getenv on each call; tinygl knob() calls are at init)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: getenv 0.09% of all samples in GLQuake prof9 (7/8000), so something calls it per frame; the caller is unknown
candidates.pathology: QEMU (MEASURED): 557 insns per miss with a 20-variable environment, dominated by strncmp's byte loop
candidates.replacement: An interposed getenv: compute the name length once, then for each entry compare the first word (or 4 bytes via lw+orc.b) before a byte compare. No caching, because environ can be edited directly
candidates.est_gain: Per call INFERRED 2-3x; process-level under 0.1% (bounded by MEASURED 0.09%)
candidates.exactness: Returns the same pointer (first match in environ order); a name containing '=' behaves the same (musl: strchrnul(name,'=') length)

candidates.name: stdio per-character/small I/O locks (getc/fgetc/putc/fread/fwrite once threaded)
candidates.where: libc.so getc/fgetc -> locking_getc (__lockfile/__unlockfile LR/SC pairs), putc -> locking_putc, fread/fwrite -> __lockfile, __fwritex, __uflow
candidates.apps: tyr-glquake/tiopex (CL_GetMessage fread x3 per demo message, getc in CL_PlayDemo_f, fgetc in Host_Loadgame_f, putc in Sys_Printf), quakespasm, libX11, libXpm, SDL1, SDL2, libasound (getc/putc in conf parse), lvdesk (fgets/fscanf of /proc every tick)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: locking_getc 0.04%, __fwritex 0.03-0.04%, fread_unlocked 0.03%, __uflow 0.04% (tgprof/prof8)
candidates.pathology: Once any thread exists (SDL audio, xlite worker), every FILE carries a lock, and each getc/putc does 2 LR/SC loops. QEMU (MEASURED): getc 12 -> 40 insns when threaded, fread(4) 106 -> 136, fwrite(8) 81 -> 120
candidates.replacement: Interposed getc/fgetc/putc/fread/fwrite that skip the lock when the process has exactly one live thread (musl's own need_locks test is not reachable from outside, so use an equivalent counter maintained by s31str's existing pthread_create wrapper), and otherwise make the lock an amoswap-based owner store
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured; bounded by the ~0.1-0.15% measured stdio share
candidates.exactness: Identical data and errors; lock semantics must stay exact with flockfile users (FILE->lock owner-tid encoding). Risky: FILE internals are private musl ABI

candidates.name: LR/SC CAS loops everywhere in libc atomics (no AMOs)
candidates.where: libc.so: 118 lr.w sites, 0 amo* instructions (toolchain libc). Hot ones: __lock/__unlock (malloc, tz, stdio open list), __lockfile/__unlockfile, pthread_mutex_*, pthread_cond_timedwait (18 sites), sem_post, pthread_once
candidates.apps: every threaded process: SDL1/SDL2 games, Xorg, libasound, xlite clients, lvdesk
candidates.heat: MEASURED indirectly: Xorg 8.7% in an LR/SC retry region (cursor-latency.md:92); pthread mutex 2.6% CPU0 in Quake play (audio-48k-plan:177). The per-op LR/SC vs AMO cost on S31 is unmeasured
candidates.pathology: musl's RISC-V atomic_arch implements a_swap/a_fetch_add/a_inc/a_dec as lr.w/sc.w loops around a_cas. On a two-hart system with PSRAM-backed lines, lost reservations force retries; a single AMO would complete in one instruction (amoadd.w is proven indivisible cross-hart, worklog-2026-09-19.md:1275)
candidates.replacement: Signature-match the fixed musl a_swap/a_fetch_add idiom sequences inside libc functions (full-body matching as in v2) and patch each loop into amoswap.w.aqrl / amoadd.w.aqrl. Alternatively interpose the handful of exported entry points (pthread_mutex_*, sem_post, pthread_cond_signal)
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured. It first needs a board microbench of LR/SC-loop vs AMO latency on the same and the other hart
candidates.exactness: Same memory-ordering strength (aqrl on both) and the same returned old value; atomicity is equal or stronger. It writes libc text, which the roadmap marks killed for libc text swap (status-and-todo:172), so the interposition variant may be the only permitted one

candidates.name: localtime_r / strftime / __secs_to_tm
candidates.where: libc.so __secs_to_tm (2 __divdi3 + 2 __moddi3 64-bit divisions), __tz lock + do_tzset on every call, __strftime_fmt_1
candidates.apps: lvdesk (tray_clock_cb, clock_update, shot_take), quakespasm/tyr-glquake strftime (savegame and screenshot names)
candidates.heat: unmeasured (prof9 shows __divdi3 0.03% and __moddi3 0.03% with unknown caller)
candidates.pathology: QEMU (MEASURED): localtime_r 4,042 insns, localtime_r+strftime 9,076. 64-bit division is a libgcc loop on RV32, and TZ is re-parsed/locked per call
candidates.replacement: A 32-bit fast path for times within [1970, 2106): days = (uint32)(t/86400) via mulhu reciprocal, and civil-from-days with 32-bit ops (Hinnant's algorithm). Reuse musl's tz state via a single call when TZ is unchanged
candidates.est_gain: Per call INFERRED 3-5x; process-level negligible (a 1 Hz clock)
candidates.exactness: Identical struct tm including tm_gmtoff/tm_zone/tm_isdst and DST transitions; only safe when the TZ rules are fixed-offset or UTC, otherwise fall back

candidates.name: qsort (smoothsort with byte-cycle swaps)
candidates.where: libc.so qsort -> qsort_r (wrapper_cmp indirection) -> sift/trinkle -> cycle(), which moves elements with memcpy through a 256-byte stack buffer per rotation
candidates.apps: SDL1, SDL2 (mode lists, hint lists), libasound, tyr-glquake (VID_SortModeList), tiopex, ramhot
candidates.heat: unmeasured (no qsort samples in the four Quake captures)
candidates.pathology: QEMU (MEASURED): 7,374 / 46,030 / 246,302 insns for 16 / 64 / 256 ints (~960 insns per element at 256) with 2 memcpy calls per cycle
candidates.replacement: The same smoothsort algorithm (identical comparison sequence, so identical output order for unstable ties), specialised for width 4 and 8 with register swaps instead of memcpy cycles, and a direct comparator call instead of wrapper_cmp
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured heat; per call INFERRED 1.5-2x
candidates.exactness: Must perform the identical sequence of comparisons and moves as musl smoothsort, or equal elements could land differently (qsort is unstable). A different algorithm is NOT exact

candidates.name: dlsym called repeatedly at run time
candidates.where: libc.so do_dlsym / dlsym (and dlopen) appearing in steady-state frame profiles
candidates.apps: unknown caller in GLQuake and tyr-glquake (SDL1/SDL2 X11 dynamic loading, libGL glXGetProcAddress are INFERRED candidates)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: do_dlsym 0.04% (prof9), 0.04% (tgprof); dlopen 0.05% (tgprof)
candidates.pathology: Each dlsym is a hash walk over the DSO list with string compares (musl has no lazy binding; gnu_lookup_filtered was 73-78% of Qt's cold start, current-state.md:2418)
candidates.replacement: Interposed dlsym with a small cache of (handle, name-pointer or hash) -> result for explicit handles and non-NULL results only. musl never unloads (dlclose is a no-op), so explicit-handle results are immutable
candidates.est_gain: Bounded by the MEASURED 0.04-0.09%
candidates.exactness: Exact for explicit handles because musl dlclose never unmaps. RTLD_DEFAULT/RTLD_NEXT depend on caller and load order: do not cache. dlerror state must be cleared as libc does

candidates.name: sched_getcpu (syscall every call)
candidates.where: libc.so sched_getcpu: ecall 168 (getcpu); RV32 has no getcpu vDSO
candidates.apps: only test tools in the repo (smpstress, sdltone1/2, swapstamp.c); relevant to any future per-CPU routing code
candidates.heat: unmeasured
candidates.pathology: A full trap per query on a kernel that runs from XIP flash
candidates.replacement: Read the rseq cpu_id that s31str.c already registers per thread (use_libc() path); fall back to the syscall when unregistered
candidates.est_gain: Per call: trap to a few loads; process-level negligible today
candidates.exactness: The same value as getcpu at the instant of the read. Migration races are equally present in the syscall version

candidates.name: strspn / strcspn / strtok (bitset build per call)
candidates.where: libc.so strcspn/strspn build a 32-byte bitset each call; strtok = strspn+strcspn
candidates.apps: lvdesk (appmenu, xwin_on_window, ctl_line strtok), libasound (strcspn, strtok_r), SDL2 strtok_r, quakespasm/tyr-glquake strtok, s31-bt
candidates.heat: unmeasured
candidates.pathology: QEMU (MEASURED): strcspn(s, " \t\n") 250 insns at 16 B, 682 at 64, 2,410 at 256 B; strtok over 6 tokens 589
candidates.replacement: Special-case reject sets of 1-4 characters with an orc.b(v^k) word test per character (as in strchrnul), falling back to the bitset for larger sets
candidates.est_gain: Unmeasured heat; per call INFERRED 2-4x for short sets
candidates.exactness: Identical span length / token pointers and strtok's static state (interpose strtok as a whole)

result.coverage_notes:
What I searched. I pulled the full dynamic import lists (readelf --dyn-syms UND) of 87 dynamically linked RISC-V ELFs in the repo: the X11 libs in the overlay, lvdesk(.syms), the tiopex-quake(.dbg) binaries, the s31-* tools, rootfs test tools and the s31route ALSA module. Only 213 libc symbols are imported. I added the U-lists from the board nm dumps in artifacts/gl/{glquake,tyrquake}/nm for SDL-1.2, SDL2, libasound, libGL, quakespasm and tyr-glquake. Each imported function of interest was disassembled from the toolchain libc (6041b2cd), and I counted QEMU instructions per call with /plugins/libinsn.so. The probes are in build/cloud/probes/wide-libc/:
- lc.c: harness for about 60 libc ops, optionally threaded; results in counts.txt and countsT.txt.
- zb.c: Zbb strncmp/strchrnul and Clinger strtof prototypes, with 0 mismatches over 2M strtof strings and 300k string cases.
- libcres.py: re-resolves the board PC samples.

The key new heat source: I re-resolved the raw board PC samples (tyrquake/raw/tgpfs2 and tgprof, glquake/prof8 and prof9 .pcs with .qmaps) against artifacts/gl/glquake/nm/libc.so.nm, which includes static symbols. That gives full libc breakdowns: memset, printf_core, __trunctfdf2 (soft-quad), malloc internals, mutex, getenv, do_dlsym and the stdio locks. It also resolves cursor-latency.md's Xorg 'lr/sc retry loop' to __pthread_mutex_timedlock+0x1c2..0x1fa.

Interposition status. s31str.c interposes exactly: memcpy, memmove, memchr, memrchr, memcmp, bcmp, strcmp, strcoll, strnlen, strrchr, strstr, memmem. s31clk.c interposes clock_gettime, clock_getres, gettimeofday and time. pthread_create is wrapped for rseq. NOT interposed: memset, strlen, strchr/strchrnul, strncmp, strcpy/stpcpy, strncpy, strcasecmp/strncasecmp, strspn/strcspn, getenv, and every numeric/stdio/malloc/pthread function. Board libc XEspV covers only memcpy, memchr, memrchr, memcmp, strnlen and strcmp (xespv-libc.md). Interposition never reaches libc-internal calls (printf->strchrnul, getenv->strncmp, strcpy->stpcpy).

Checked and not worth pursuing:
- atoi (89 insns, fine)
- rand (21, unlocked)
- tolower/isalnum (9-11)
- log10f/atan2f/atanf (pure float, 74-103)
- sqrtf (fsqrt.s)
- small memset (44-130)

Could not reach:
- Xorg, SDL/SDL_mixer/libpng/zlib binaries (not in the repo; only nm U-lists for SDL1/SDL2/libasound).
- The overlay libfreetype.so.6.20.6 and libfontconfig.so.1.16.0 are 4.7-9.4 kB stubs with almost no imports.
- artifacts/s31fp-copy-fix/prboom.elf is absent.
- The quakespasm source was fetched from SourceForge (GitHub was blocked) to find callers.

Caveats:
- The toolchain libc is NOT the board libc 352e9417. Function bodies appear equivalent (same pthread_mutex_timedlock size 0x240), but all instruction counts are QEMU upstream-musl 1.2.5 counts with no timing.
- The nm used for re-resolution is inferred (not proven) to match the profiled libc; its memset/printf_core attributions agree with the recorded PROFILE.txt files.
- LR/SC vs AMO cost, PSRAM write-allocate behaviour and all per-call ns figures need board measurement.
- Excluded per instructions: libgcc soft-double helpers, double libm (sin/cos/pow/floor, W6/W7), OPL, fused chains and copy placement.

candidates.name: alsa-lib linear rate converter (linear_expand_s16 / linear_shrink_s16 + pcm_rate framework passes)
candidates.where: libasound.so.2 (alsa-lib 1.2.15.3), src/pcm/pcm_rate_linear.c:138-187 (static, selected through rate->func), driven by pcm_rate.c inside plug:'hw:0,0' below s31route
candidates.apps: Every app whose rate the codec lacks: prboom (22050), 22.05 kHz SDL apps, 32/36 kHz apps (sdltone arms), all mono/22.05 kHz SDL1.2/SDL2 clients
candidates.heat: MEASURED: alsa-lib's linear converter adds about 1.85 us (~590 cycles) per output frame, ~8% of a core at a 44.1 kHz output (artifacts/audio/first-principles-2026-09-27/REPORT.md §3). The 22.05 kHz mono path costs 5.1-5.3 us per app frame, 11.3-11.6% of a core. prboom: '~8-10% the 22050->44100 linear resampler and its copies' (docs/current-state.md:7936-7940). MEASURED in QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-libs/rl.c, the real source at -Os with the board -march): the linear_expand_s16 kernel alone is 41 insn per stereo output frame (20.6 per sample).
candidates.pathology: The kernel does a 32-bit udiv on every output sample, although the divisor (get_threshold>>pitch_shift) is constant for the whole call. It makes one strided pass per channel over interleaved data. The kernel is only ~41 of ~590 cycles per frame, so most of the cost is pcm_rate.c's intermediate buffers and extra area passes through PSRAM (INFERRED). The ~13.6 MB/s copy ceiling makes every extra pass expensive.
candidates.replacement: Match linear_expand_s16, linear_shrink_s16 and the pcm_rate commit/convert helpers by full-body signature. libasound is built once by Buildroot and there is exactly one copy on the board, so the reproducible staging build gives the reference bytes. Replace them with an interleaved-stereo S16 single pass that computes new_weight with an exact precomputed-reciprocal multiply-high (the divisor is fixed per call, so a Granlund-Montgomery magic is exact) and writes straight into the destination area. The first-party alternative is REPORT option 3: s31route resamples itself.
candidates.est_gain: Kernel 41 -> ~12 insn per frame. The framework passes are the larger prize. Realistic 2-5% of a core for 22.05 kHz apps (INFERRED; the measured ceiling is ~8-11%).
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical S16 output: the same integer formula (old*ow+new*nw)>>16, and the exact reciprocal must equal udiv for every pos < get_threshold. Also: the same old_sample carry-over per channel, and the same frame accounting returned to pcm_rate.

candidates.name: SDL2 ALSA hotplug enumeration (snd_device_name_hint every 5 s)
candidates.where: libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10 src/audio/alsa/SDL_alsa_audio.c:972-985 (ALSA_HotplugThread -> ALSA_HotplugIteration -> snd_device_name_hint at :848). libasound is reached through dlopen plus dlsym(handle) (SDL_sysloadso.c:57), so ordinary LD_PRELOAD interposition of snd_device_name_hint does NOT catch it.
candidates.apps: Every SDL2 app with audio: chocolate-doom, OpenTyrian (SDL2 build), TyrQuake SDL2, SDL2 test clients
candidates.heat: MEASURED: the hotplug thread was 42% of a core and is still 11% after the lean alsa.conf shipped. One enumeration takes 1.83 s, now 0.35 s (docs/perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:976-992).
candidates.pathology: Each iteration re-walks the ALSA config tree and opens ctl devices through the XIP overlay (path lookup plus the _snd_config_search/printf_core CPU path). Syscalls and file opens cost ms here, and the answer never changes on this board unless a card or the config changes.
candidates.replacement: Interpose dlsym in the preload, and hand SDL2 a wrapper when name == "snd_device_name_hint" (and the matching free_hint). The wrapper returns a deep copy of a cached hint list. The cache key is iface plus the mtime/size of /usr/share/alsa/alsa.conf, /etc/asound.conf and ~/.asoundrc, plus the contents of /proc/asound/cards, all read with one stat each. On any change it re-enumerates through the real function.
candidates.est_gain: ~7-11% of a core returned to every SDL2 audio app (enumeration 0.35 s per 5 s -> a few stats)
candidates.exactness: The same NAME/DESC/IOID strings in the same order, and a freshly malloc'd array so the caller's snd_device_name_free_hint still works. A change in cards or config must invalidate before the next call. errno and the return code must equal the real call's.

candidates.name: musl float libm that evaluates in double (sinf, cosf, sincosf, tanf, expf, exp2f, logf, log2f, powf, hypotf, asinf/acosf, cbrtf)
candidates.where: libc.so (musl 1.2.5; the board's is 352e9417, not byte-identical to the toolchain copy): __sindf/__cosdf/__tandf/__rem_pio2f and the double-based exp/log/pow kernels, exported as sinf etc.
candidates.apps: lvdesk/xshim (sinf/cosf/atan2f for X arcs, xshim.c:2215-2253; powf for gamma ramps, xshim.c:587,643; expf/cosf/sinf in the click synth, lvdesk.c:3150-3159), tiopex-quake (sincosf), SDL audio test clients (sdltone), GL demos, any app doing per-sample float trig
candidates.heat: MEASURED on the board: one sinf costs ~9 us (~3000 cycles). sdltone calling sinf once per sample spent 40-50% of a core at 48 kHz (REPORT.md §3). MEASURED instruction counts in QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-libs/tf.c, upstream musl 1.2.5): sinf 2005, cosf 2149, sincosf 4028, tanf 2932, expf 1823, logf 1847, powf 4082, hypotf 588. By contrast the float-only paths are atanf 74, atan2f 117 and sqrtf 16. The per-app call rate is unmeasured.
candidates.pathology: There is no D extension, so every double_t step in these float kernels is a soft-double helper call, while the hardware single-precision FPU (with fmadd.s) sits idle.
candidates.replacement: Float-float (double-single) evaluation with fmadd.s: Cody-Waite reduction plus a minimax polynomial, followed by a Ziv rounding test. When the result lies within the error bound of a float rounding boundary, call the original musl function (dlsym RTLD_NEXT). The result is therefore bit-exact by construction. The univariate functions can be verified exhaustively over all 2^32 inputs on the host against musl's source, since the double arithmetic is deterministic IEEE.
candidates.est_gain: ~2000-4000 -> ~60-150 insn per call (INFERRED; REPORT §7.5 estimates 50-100 cycles against 3000 measured)
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical float results for every input, including the NaN payload/sign, -0, and the inf/overflow/underflow edges. errno (ERANGE/EDOM) and fflags must match. Exhaustive 2^32 checks for the univariate functions. powf/hypotf need a proof plus a randomized oracle, because their domain is 2^64.

candidates.name: musl strtod / strtof / atof (decfloat/__floatscan in soft long double)
candidates.where: libc.so __floatscan/decfloat (the objdump shows 40 soft-TF helper call sites in decfloat and 26 in __floatscan). The toolchain libc's private __addtf3/__subtf3/__multf3 contain esp.lp.setup hardware loops (55 esp.lp.setup in libc.so).
candidates.apps: tiopex-quake (imports atof, sscanf, fscanf: entity/cvar parsing), fontconfig (FcStrtod), Xt/Xaw apps (xcalc), lvdesk sscanf/fscanf, any config parser
candidates.heat: MEASURED instruction counts in QEMU: strtod("1234.5678") 14,511 and atof("-0.25") 8,749 per call. The call rate is unmeasured: mostly load time.
candidates.pathology: long double is IEEE quad done in software on rv32, so every digit-accumulation step is a __multf3/__addtf3 call. In addition, the esp.lp hardware loops inside libc's TF helpers are a recorded userspace-corruption hazard under Linux (tinygl-hw-accel-assessment:122-123).
candidates.replacement: Interpose strtod/strtof/atof with an Eisel-Lemire fast path (64-bit mantissa, precomputed 128-bit powers of 5 using mul/mulhu) plus a Clinger fast path. Fall back to the original for hex floats, inf/nan, more than 19 significant digits, ambiguous halfway cases and locale oddities. The internal calls from sscanf/fscanf cannot be reached this way.
candidates.est_gain: 14.5k -> ~300-600 insn for typical decimals (INFERRED). A load-time win only.
candidates.exactness: musl's strtod is correctly rounded, so any correctly rounded algorithm returns identical bits. Must also match the endptr position, ERANGE/errno on over- and underflow, the sign of zero, and whitespace/prefix handling. Differential fuzzing against the original is required.

candidates.name: musl printf float conversions (fmt_fp in soft long double)
candidates.where: libc.so fmt_fp (23 soft-TF call sites), reached by printf/snprintf/fprintf %f/%g/%e

candidates.name: libgcc quad-precision helpers statically linked into apps (__multf3, __addtf3, __extendsftf2, __trunctfsf2)

candidates.name: libgcc 64-bit int <-> float helpers (__floatdisf, __floatundisf, __fixsfdi, __fixunssfdi)

candidates.replacement: Interpose sched_getcpu to read the rseq area that v3 already registers. CPUTIME clocks stay syscalls, because no vDSO data exists for them.
candidates.est_gain: ~5 us per call. Only material if a hot caller exists.
candidates.exactness: sched_getcpu is inherently racy; the rseq cpu_id is the kernel's own value at that instant. Fall back when rseq is unregistered.

result.coverage_notes:
What I searched: the heat sources in docs (current-state, perf-plan, perf-review and its JSON candidate/verdict files, gl-performance-campaign, the audio first-principles REPORT, and the s31fp roadmap for exclusions), the recorded profiles (artifacts/gl/glquake/prof9/PROFILE.txt, artifacts/gl/present-prof gp.pcs/lp.pcs, which I resolved myself against lvdesk.nm/libc.nm), the overlay binaries (libX*, libfreetype, libfontconfig, s31route, s31-bt, s31-a2dp, lvdesk), rootfs/tiopex-quake.dbg, and the toolchain libc.so.

Upstream sources fetched at the Buildroot-pinned versions (buildroot cb857ba4) into build/cloud/probes/wide-libs/src: SDL 1.2.15, SDL2 2.32.10, SDL2_mixer 2.6.3, zlib 1.3.2, mpg123 1.33.5, alsa-lib 1.2.15.3, sbc 2.2 (2.1 is installed). SDL_mixer 1.2's pinned GitHub commit was blocked, so the 1.2.12 release stood in.

QEMU instruction counts I took with the board -march and -Os (-mtune=esp-base where relevant): the libm/strtod/printf/TF/int64-float table (tf.c), zlib crc32/adler32/inflate (zt.c), alsa linear_expand_s16 on the real source (rl.c), the libsbc encode split with hotblocks (sb.c), SDL blit idioms (bl.c), malloc/qsort/str* (ml.c), and the -mtune=esp-base unaligned codegen demonstration (ua.c). All are instruction counts, not cycles; QEMU has no timing model.

Caveats:
- The toolchain libc is not the board's libc 352e9417, and the QEMU sysroot is upstream musl. The esp.lp finding inside libc's TF helpers comes from the toolchain libc.
- The SDL/SDL2/libpng/zlib/libsbc/libasound binaries themselves are not in the repo, so full-body signatures could not be cut. Copy-patch viability rests on each library being a single Buildroot-built copy with reproducible bytes.
- lp.pcs libc symbols are unreliable (the samples land on iconv/__fpclassifyl, which means misattribution).
- The kernel tree (linux-71-port) and OpenSBI are absent from this checkout, so the misaligned-trap path and PCM status-mmap gating are INFERRED from upstream and the docs.
- A crude static scan for misaligned-immediate loads was inconclusive and is not cited.

Not reached:
- No board, so nothing on hart timing, misaligned-trap cost, PIE throughput for the SBC/blit kernels, per-app call rates for sinf/strtod/malloc, or chocolate-doom/OpenTyrian SDL2 function-level splits beyond the recorded 30%.
- Not examined: fontconfig/expat/Xrm startup parsing, dbus marshalling, bluez, libGLU/freeglut, mpg123 (generic_fpu, float synth; no pathology found).
- libGL, xlite and lvdesk are first-party: they are listed only where the fix is at source (lv_memcpy config, xshim hash).
- Excluded per instructions: soft-double helpers, OPL, fused chains, floor/ceil/trunc, and copy placement. The double libm item overlaps W7 and is flagged as such.

candidates.name: strtof / strtod / atof / sscanf-%f (musl __floatscan/decfloat, soft-quad long double)
candidates.where: board libc.so (musl): decfloat makes 40 calls and __floatscan 27 calls to __multf3/__addtf3/__subtf3 etc. (static count, toolchain libc.so; board libc 352e9417 not in repo). Importers: tiopex-quake atof@plt (ED_ParseEpair x2, per entity field at map load), sscanf (CL_PlayDemo_f); libXt strtof; lvdesk fscanf/sscanf; libXpm sscanf
candidates.apps: Quake family at map/config load (tiopex ED_ParseEpair; quakespasm/tyrquake cvars and entities), Xt resource parsing, lvdesk config parsing
candidates.heat: unmeasured at runtime: no profile sample falls in __floatscan/decfloat. MEASURED icount (QEMU, board ISA): musl strtof takes 8,630 instr for "0.5", 13,202 for "3.14159", 11,354 for "-0.0078125", 15,468 for "0.001" and 1,164-1,189 for integer strings. strtod and atof average 9,387 over a 7-string mix; sscanf %f averages 10,061
candidates.pathology: On rv32, musl's long double is IEEE binary128, and decfloat does its scaling and rounding in long double. Every decimal conversion therefore runs a chain of soft-quad __multf3/__addtf3 calls, each hundreds of instructions. On the board those helpers also contain esp.lp loops. There is no hardware double, and the decimal conversion never needs quad at all.
candidates.replacement: Interpose strtof/strtod/atof (and the scanf %f path if vsscanf is taken over) with a Clinger fast path. Plain [+-]digits[.digits] with at most 7 significant digits (float) or 15 (double), a fraction of at most 10 (float) or 22 (double) digits, and frm==RNE is computed as (float)m / 10^k in one hardware fdiv.s. For double it is one correctly rounded division through the s31fp exact helpers, or Eisel-Lemire with 64-bit integer multiplies. Anything else (exponent, hex, inf/nan, more digits, a non-RNE mode, overflow or underflow) tail-calls libc. Prototype build/cloud/probes/wide-helpers/sf.c.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED, float fast path: 68-144 instr against 8,630-15,468 (60-110x) per call, and 78 against 1,189 for integer strings. The CPU-share gain is unmeasured: it is a load-time and parse-time gain, not a per-frame one
candidates.exactness: Result bits and endptr must equal musl's, and errno (ERANGE) must not change, so range cases go to libc. MEASURED: 0 mismatches in bits or endptr over 300,000 random decimals against musl strtof. The prototype only takes the fast path when frrm==0 (RNE), because strtof honours the current mode. The double path is not yet prototyped.

candidates.name: snprintf / printf / vfprintf with %f %e %g (musl fmt_fp, soft-quad long double)
candidates.where: board libc.so printf_core -> fmt_fp: 21 static soft-quad helper calls in fmt_fp, plus pop_arg. The importers are everywhere: tiopex-quake (sprintf/snprintf/vsnprintf, 60+ sites including Sbar_*, SCR_UpdateScreen, R_TimeGraph, PR_ValueString), lvdesk (printf/snprintf/vsnprintf), libX11, libXt, s31-* tools
candidates.apps: quakespasm, tyr-glquake, tiopex-quake (HUD/fps/console strings), lvdesk status text, any %f logger
candidates.heat: MEASURED printf_core+vfprintf share of CPU0 across my re-resolution of 14 committed PC-sample profiles: 0.05-0.22% for glquake (prof1 0.11%, prof8 0.20%, prof9 0.16%, p10a-c 0.09-0.12%) and 0.12-0.32% for tyrquake (tgp14 0.20%, tgpfs2 0.22%, tgprof 0.32%). The libc soft-quad helpers (__multf3 9, __addtf3 7, __subtf3 3, __divtf3 3 samples) show up in fp-g2/fp-g4 and quake profiles. The fraction of printf_core time spent in %f is unmeasured. MEASURED icount: snprintf("%.1f") 7,035, "%f" 6,937, "%g" 7,006, "%.2f" of a float 3,134, against "%d" 864
candidates.pathology: fmt_fp does frexpl and its scaling and rounding tests in binary128 long double, so every %f/%e/%g is a soft-quad chain (8x the instructions of %d). Its decimal algorithm is actually integer (base-1e9 limbs); only the long double glue is expensive.
candidates.replacement: Interpose the v*printf family with musl's own vfprintf.c compiled into libs31fp (the same approach as s31str's musl copy), with fmt_fp's long double glue replaced by exact integer extraction of the double (53-bit mantissa, exponent) feeding the unchanged base-1e9 limb algorithm. The rounding branch replicates musl's current-mode behaviour, or defers to libc when frm!=RNE. Output bytes are identical by construction.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: most of the ~6,000-instruction gap between %f and %d per conversion, bounded above by the 0.05-0.32% printf_core share measured in the Quake profiles
candidates.exactness: Byte-identical output, return value and errno for every format. FILE locking and stdio buffer semantics are unchanged (musl source). The rounding mode must be honoured exactly as musl does: its round-to-long-double-epsilon trick follows the current frm, so either model it or defer when frm!=0.

candidates.name: sin / cos / sincos / __rem_pio2 / __sin / __cos / __tan (double libm in libc)
