candidates.where: board libc.so: sincos, __rem_pio2, __sin, __cos, __tan. The callers are quakespasm (double sin/cos) and libc-internal code. libc's soft-double helpers are libc-private and cannot be copy-patched (libc text is off-limits per roadmap §5)
candidates.apps: quakespasm (AngleVectors-style trig), anything calling double sin/cos
candidates.heat: MEASURED share of CPU0 for sincos+__rem_pio2+__sin+__cos+__tan: prof8 0.26%, prof9 0.49%, p10a 0.45%, p10b 0.52%, p10c 0.46%, f12 0.28%, prof1 0.14%. These are the largest in-scope libc items outside memset/memcpy
candidates.pathology: Double trig runs entirely on libc-private libgcc soft-double helpers, which s31fp cannot patch because libc text is off-limits. __rem_pio2 runs whenever |x|>pi/4, which is the common case for angles in radians.
candidates.replacement: Interpose sin/cos/sincos/tan with musl's own sources compiled into libs31fp and linked against s31fp's exact fast double helpers. The results are bit-identical by construction: the algorithm is the same and every IEEE operation is the same. This overlaps roadmap W7 ("libm exports beyond floor/ceil/trunc"), so coordinate with it rather than duplicating it.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: the s31fp helper speed-up applied to 0.14-0.52% of CPU0
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical results and fflags (the musl source is unchanged, and the helpers are exact including fflags, as v2 verified). errno is untouched.

candidates.name: sinf / cosf / sincosf / tanf / expf / exp2f / logf / powf (float libm with double internals)
candidates.where: board libc.so float libm. Static soft-double helper calls per function in toolchain libc: powf 31, logf 15, expf 14, exp2f 13, sinf 11, sincosf 11, cosf 10, tanf 7. Importers: lvdesk (sincosf, cosf, powf, atan2f), tiopex-quake sincosf@plt (AngleVectors x3, R_RotateBmodel x3, R_EntityParticles x2, R_DrawSprite, RotatePointAroundVector, SV_SetIdealPitch)
candidates.apps: tiopex-quake (per entity/particle), lvdesk animations, quakespasm
candidates.heat: MEASURED share of CPU0 is small in the GL profiles: libc sincosf 5, sinf 2 and sincosl 3 samples in total. tiopex runtime share is unmeasured. MEASURED icount per call: sinf 2,053 (3,009 at x~100), sincosf 3,903, tanf 2,608, expf 1,816, exp2f 1,623, logf 1,703, powf 4,111, against atan2f 122 (float-only) and sqrtf 15 (hardware)
candidates.pathology: musl's float functions evaluate their polynomials in double (designed for hardware double), so each call on the S31 is 7-31 libc-private soft-double calls, even though the hart has a hardware single-precision FPU.
candidates.replacement: Same as the double-trig candidate: musl sources compiled into libs31fp against s31fp's fast exact double helpers (bit-identical). A float-only algorithm would need an exactness proof against musl's non-correctly-rounded outputs, and roadmap item A5 has deferred that.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: 2-4x fewer cycles per call (helper speed-up only). The absolute gain is unmeasured and likely small in the GL titles
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical to musl only if the same double-evaluated source is used. Do not substitute a float algorithm without a full 2^32-input comparison.

candidates.name: __udivdi3 / __umoddi3 / __divdi3 / __moddi3 (libgcc 64-bit division bodies)
candidates.where: Full-body signature matches of libgcc members (my scanner, masked GOT relocs): board /usr/bin/lvdesk __udivdi3 @0xa8cd8 (76 call sites), __divdi3 @0xa89be (15), __umoddi3 @0xa8fb4 (1). s31route ALSA plugin __udivdi3 (4 sites: sink_params x3, route_transfer x1). libXt and libXrender __divdi3 (1 each). s31-a2dp, s31-bt, s31-tone. nm-only: libSDL-1.2 __udivdi3 size 0x2dc (the same 732-byte body), __divdi3/__moddi3/__umoddi3; libasound the same set
candidates.apps: lvdesk (X server/desktop), SDL1 titles, ALSA route plugin
candidates.heat: MEASURED: lvdesk __udivdi3 0.11% of CPU0 (fp-g2 present probe) and 0.00-0.08% elsewhere. libSDL __divdi3 11 samples across 14 profiles (~0.01%). libc __moddi3 6 and __divdi3 2. MEASURED icount of the libgcc body plus call: 51 for 32-bit-range operands, 53 for ns/1e6, 76 for ns/1000, 156 for 64/64, and 55 for signed 32-bit/1000
candidates.pathology: libgcc's __udivmoddi4 has no n|d<2^32 shortcut: it always normalises through __clz_tab (a GOT-indirect PSRAM table load, although Zbb clz exists) and does udiv_qrnnd in C with 16-bit half-digits.
candidates.replacement: Copy-patch the matched bodies with a version that starts with `if(!((n|d)>>32)) return (u32)n/(u32)d;` (MEASURED 9 instr against 51), uses Zbb clz instead of __clz_tab, and otherwise tail-calls the original algorithm. The roadmap's kill (a replacement at 69 vs 51, and a fast path at 47 vs 51 above 2^32) was about the >2^32 path. This front-end costs +3 there and -42 on 32-bit operands.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED per call: 51->9 instr for 32-bit-range operands, +3 on the rest. As CPU share it is at most ~0.1% (lvdesk). The share of calls in 32-bit range is unmeasured: kms_flush_cb's ns/1e6 sites are above 2^32 and will not benefit
candidates.exactness: Quotient and remainder identical for all inputs, and division by zero keeps the same behaviour (libgcc does not trap: it computes 1/0 through the udiv path, so replicate by deferring d==0 to the original). MEASURED 0 mismatches over 2,000,000 mixed pairs (div.c).

candidates.name: 64-bit muldiv idiom `(int64)a*b/c` in lvdesk/LVGL
candidates.where: lvdesk: mulh+mul feeding __divdi3 in draw_indic (6 sites), lv_obj_get_scrollbar_area (4), render_request (2), update_knob_pos (2) and lv_cubic_bezier (1). The __udivdi3 versions are in xwin_on_draw (7) and xshim_window_pixels (2)
candidates.apps: lvdesk UI drawing, xshim window pixel paths
candidates.heat: unmeasured per site: no profile sample resolves inside these callers' division
candidates.pathology: The product of two 32-bit pixel or range values is widened to 64 bits by C semantics, then divided by a 32-bit c through the full 55-instruction libgcc body, although the product usually fits in 32 bits.
candidates.replacement: lvdesk is first-party, so fix at the source: use lv_map-style 32-bit arithmetic when the operands are bounded, or an inline `hi==sign(lo) ? (int32)p/c : __divdi3(p,c)`. The copy-patch front-end in the previous candidate also covers it without a rebuild.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: about 45 instr saved per call when the product fits in 32 bits
candidates.exactness: Identical quotient (C truncating division); the fast path is only taken when the 64-bit value equals its 32-bit sign extension.

candidates.name: lvdesk constant-divisor 64-bit division (ns -> us/ms)
candidates.where: lvdesk kms_flush_cb: 14 __udivdi3 calls, divisors 1,000,000 (lui 0xf4 + addi 576) and 1000, some chained (x/y then /1000). main has 31 sites, xsp_dump 13, con_slide_* 3
candidates.apps: lvdesk (every KMS flush)
candidates.heat: MEASURED lvdesk __udivdi3 total 0.11% of CPU0 (fp-g2); the per-site split is unmeasured
candidates.pathology: Dividing by a compile-time constant 1e6/1000 goes through a generic 53-76-instruction libgcc division with 1-2 hardware divu plus corrections, instead of a reciprocal multiply. rv32 GCC does not inline 64-bit constant division.
candidates.replacement: At the source (first-party): keep timestamps in 32-bit us or ms deltas, or use a mul-high reciprocal (Granlund-Montgomery, ~20-35 instr with mulhu). A 3-step divu chain prototype for /1e6 measured 53 against 65 instr including the loop, so the reciprocal is the better route; the roadmap's K=1000 thunk measured 35 against 81-83.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~30-50 instr per site per flush, a fraction of the 0.11% measured
candidates.exactness: Exact quotient for all 64-bit inputs (prototype div1e6: 0 mismatches over 2,000,000 after fixing an overflow bug found by the same test).

candidates.name: __floatdisf / __floatundisf (int64 -> float, libgcc soft-fp)
candidates.where: Static copies found by signature in tiopex-quake.dbg (called by Sys_DoubleTime x2) and rootfs/audiofp/rsbench. nm-only in tyr-glquake (__floatdisf @0x7ebcc). libgcc members are 332 and 268 bytes, with 2 CSR ops each (frrm, csrs fflags) and nested calls to __ashldi3/__lshrdi3
candidates.apps: tiopex-quake, tyr-glquake, rsbench; any (float)int64 conversion
candidates.heat: MEASURED ~0: no sample in __floatdisf across 32,000 tyrquake samples. My first resolution attributed 0.23-0.30% to tyr __ashldi3, but that was a resolver artefact: the PCs lie below `main` in the PLT (see the PLT candidate)
candidates.pathology: The soft-fp generic path saves 9 registers, reads frrm (a 25-30 ns CSR access), calls __ashldi3 and __lshrdi3 out of line, and sets fflags with csrs. The hardware fcvt.s.w/wu would round correctly in the current mode.
candidates.replacement: If hi==sign(lo), a single fcvt.s.w. Otherwise narrow to 31 or 32 significant bits with the dropped bits ORed into bit 0 (round-to-odd sticky), convert with fcvt.s.w or fcvt.s.wu (the hardware rounds in the current frm and raises NX), then multiply by an exact 2^k. Prototype: build/cloud/probes/wide-helpers/cvt.c.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED: 112->16 instr (int32-range input), 107->37 (large); __floatundisf 88->32. Both drop 2 CSR ops. The CPU-share gain is negligible on current evidence
candidates.exactness: MEASURED 0 mismatches in bits and fflags over 4,000,000 conversions (floatdisf, floatundisf, fixsfdi, fixunssfdi) under RNE/RTZ/RDN/RUP. Negative control (sticky OR removed): 1,080 mismatches in 800,000.

candidates.name: __fixsfdi / __fixunssfdi (float -> int64, libgcc soft-fp)
candidates.where: libgcc members fixsfdi.o (204 B, 3 CSR ops, calls __ashldi3) and fixunssfdi.o (138 B). Callers: toolchain libc llrintf/llroundf; tyr-glquake __fixunssfdi (nm @0x7eb48)
candidates.apps: tyr-glquake, libc llrintf/llroundf users
candidates.heat: unmeasured (0 samples in the committed profiles)
candidates.pathology: Soft-fp reads frrm, raises flags with csrs, and calls __ashldi3 out of line, although |x|<2^31 is a single fcvt.w.s rtz.
candidates.replacement: If the exponent is below 31 (32 for unsigned), fcvt.w.s or fcvt.wu.s with rtz. If 2^31<=|x|<2^63 the value is an integer: shift the mantissa exactly, with no flags. Overflow, NaN and negative-unsigned inputs go to the original body.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED: __fixsfdi 34->16 instr for small values and 41->22 for large; __fixunssfdi 38->20 (loop overhead subtracted)
candidates.exactness: Covered by the same 4,000,000-case bits+fflags run (0 mismatches). Overflow and NaN are deferred to libgcc for identical saturation values and NV.

candidates.name: PLT stubs in hot DSOs (call via auipc/lw GOT/jalr)
candidates.where: Pre-text PCs (below the first text symbol, 16-byte slots). libGL.so.1.2.0: all 30 samples of prof1 in the single slot at 0xc570 (first symbol 0xc810). quakespasm: slots 0xb680 (25 samples) and 0xb740 (9). tyr-glquake: 0xaeb8-0xba58 (first symbol main @0xbc70)
candidates.apps: quakespasm, tyr-glquake, libGL (every GL title), libasound, libX11
candidates.heat: MEASURED share of CPU0 in pre-text regions: quakespasm 0.72% (prof1), 0.55% (prof9), 0.41% (p10a); libGL 0.38% (prof1), 0.61% (tgpfs2), 0.31% (tgp16); tyr-glquake 0.30% (tgpfs2), 0.25% (tgp16); libX11 0.04-0.15%. That these PCs are PLT entries is INFERRED from address range and 16-byte stride; the target symbol behind libGL slot 0xc570 is unknown without the binary
candidates.pathology: Each cross-DSO call goes call->PLT: auipc, a GOT load (a PSRAM data access), then an indirect jalr, which is likely mispredicted, and the XIP text page adds an extra fetch line. One hot libGL slot takes 0.38% on its own, so the callee is called at per-pixel or per-span rate.
candidates.replacement: At load time (in the s31fp preload, like v2's patcher), rewrite hot `auipc+jalr` call sites that target .plt entries into direct `auipc+jalr` to the GOT value musl already resolved (musl binds everything at load and never re-binds). For first-party libGL and lvdesk, rebuilding with -fno-plt, or with visibility/aliases for intra-library calls, gets most of it without patching. First identify slot 0xc570 in libGL from a current build.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: up to the measured 0.3-0.7% per hot DSO, and ~1% of CPU0 combined for glquake/tyrquake if most stub time is the indirect jump plus GOT load
candidates.exactness: Same callee address as the GOT holds after relocation. It must skip symbols that can legitimately change (IFUNC does not exist in musl; watch dlopen'd interposers). The copy-on-write cost of patched XIP text pages must be budgeted against RAM (roadmap P7 found that entry-only redirects touch the same pages).

candidates.name: Kernel __div64_32 (lib/math/div64.c generic shift-subtract loop)
candidates.where: vmlinux weak __div64_32 @c015cb8a (0xb2 bytes, flash/XIP). Reached from the 20 outlined div_u64_rem copies, div_s64_rem, and do_div on non-constant divisors whenever the dividend is >=2^32 (ns_to_timespec64, ktime_divns and similar)
candidates.apps: all (timekeeping, scheduler statistics, clocksource conversions)
candidates.heat: MEASURED (prof10a-c, 24,000 samples, resolved with kfast/base-nm.txt, whose match to those kernels is INFERRED): __div64_32 0.013%, div_u64_rem 0.083%, div_s64_rem 0.071% of CPU0. MEASURED icount of the generic algorithm: 410 instr for ns/1e9, 1,026-1,050 for /1e6 or /1000
candidates.pathology: rv32 has no arch __div64_32, so the generic bit-by-bit long division runs (up to 64 iterations of 64-bit compare/subtract/shift, each several rv32 instructions) from 6x-slower flash, although the core has a hardware 32-bit divu.
candidates.replacement: A strong arch __div64_32: high word by one divu, then a clz-normalised two-digit 64/32 schoolbook step (Hacker's Delight divlu) using divu and Zbb clz. Prototype: build/cloud/probes/wide-helpers/kdiv.c. Place it in .text.fast.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED: 410->59 instr (ns/1e9) and 1,026-1,041->~61 (/1e3, /1e6), a 7-17x cut. The CPU gain is bounded by ~0.17% (div_*_rem plus __div64_32 shares)
candidates.exactness: Quotient and remainder identical. MEASURED 0 mismatches over 1,000,000 random (n, base) pairs including 1e9, 1000 and small bases.

candidates.name: Kernel generic_ffs / __ffs / fls (bitops without Zbb in an XIP kernel)
candidates.where: vmlinux: 7 outlined copies of generic_ffs (0x40 bytes each, e.g. c0114846, c018d78a, c0858844 in .text.fast)
candidates.apps: all (scheduler, IRQ, bitmap walks)
candidates.heat: MEASURED 0.062% of CPU0 in generic_ffs (prof10a-c)
candidates.pathology: RISCV_ISA_ZBB depends on RISCV_ALTERNATIVE, which depends on !XIP_KERNEL (INFERRED from upstream Kconfig; the kernel tree is not checked out here). The XIP kernel therefore falls back to the asm-generic bit cascade, and -Os outlines it, although KCFLAGS already pass -march=...zbb (Makefile:27/766).
candidates.replacement: In arch/riscv/include/asm/bitops.h, when `__riscv_zbb` is defined at compile time, use __builtin_ffs/__builtin_ctz/__builtin_clz directly (a compile-time selection with no alternative patching). This is a small local patch in the project's existing patches/ series.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: generic_ffs's ~15-20 instructions plus the call become 2-3 inline instructions; up to the 0.06% measured
candidates.exactness: Same results for all inputs (ffs(0)==0 preserved by the builtin).

candidates.name: Kernel __ashldi3 / __lshrdi3 / __ashrdi3 (out-of-line 64-bit shifts)
candidates.where: vmlinux __ashldi3 @c016c894 (flash), __lshrdi3 @c083a8f2 (.text.fast RAM), __ashrdi3 (flash); lib/*.c generic
candidates.apps: all (timekeeping mult/shift, clocksource cyc2ns)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: __lshrdi3 0.079% and __ashldi3 0.025% of CPU0 (prof10a-c)
candidates.pathology: The -Os kernel on rv32 emits libcalls for 64-bit variable shifts, and __ashldi3 still executes from XIP flash. Each call costs the jump, the stack and the branchy generic body.
candidates.replacement: Move __ashldi3 and __ashrdi3 into .text.fast (the FASTFN list), and/or build timekeeping.o and clocksource code at -O2 (the Makefile already has an S31_O2_OBJS hook), where GCC inlines the shifts.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: up to ~0.1% of CPU0
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical (the same C, or compiler-inlined shifts).

candidates.name: Kernel generic_atomic64_add (hashed spinlock + irqsave)
candidates.where: vmlinux generic_atomic64_add @c083a850 (.text.fast); the whole generic_atomic64_* family is present
candidates.apps: all
candidates.heat: MEASURED 0.171% of CPU0 (prof10a-c). The caller is unidentified (it is not in the 5 kernel symbols the resolved report shows); tgpfs2.prof.txt also lists it at 0.2%
candidates.pathology: rv32 has no 64-bit AMO, so every atomic64 op takes a hashed raw spinlock with irqsave/irqrestore: two sstatus CSR accesses at 25-30 ns each, plus lr/sc.
candidates.replacement: First identify the hot caller with a PROF=1 kernel. If it is per-task accounting on a path that is effectively single-writer on hart1, a 32-bit or per-cpu counter at the source is the fix. Otherwise nothing is exact and cheap.
candidates.est_gain: unmeasured; bounded by 0.17%
candidates.exactness: Must keep atomic64 semantics; only a caller-side change is safe.

candidates.name: Kernel crc32c / crc32_le table CRC (no Zbc clmul in an XIP kernel)
candidates.where: vmlinux crc32c, crc32_le and crc32_be wrappers (0x26 bytes) plus 1 KB tables crc32table_le, crc32ctable_le and crc32table_be: the slice-by-1 table path
candidates.apps: ext4/jbd2 metadata checksums (if metadata_csum is enabled on the card), Bluetooth/Wi-Fi stacks
candidates.heat: unmeasured (no sample in the committed profiles)
candidates.pathology: The upstream riscv clmul CRC needs RISCV_ISA_ZBC, which depends on RISCV_ALTERNATIVE and so is off in an XIP kernel (INFERRED from upstream Kconfig), leaving byte-at-a-time table lookups from PSRAM or flash rodata.
candidates.replacement: Compile-time selection of the riscv Zbc clmul CRC32/CRC32C (Barrett reduction) when `__riscv_zbc` is defined.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: several times faster per byte for large buffers; the absolute gain is unmeasured
candidates.exactness: The CRC value is identical (standard polynomial).

candidates.name: Kernel strlen / strcmp / strncmp / strnlen / memchr (byte loops, Zbb variants disabled)
candidates.where: vmlinux strlen 0x16 B, strcmp 0x20, strncmp 0x28, strnlen 0x1e, memchr 0x16, strchr/strrchr: all generic byte loops
candidates.apps: all (path lookup, sysfs, drivers)
candidates.heat: MEASURED ~0 in prof10a-c (sized_strscpy 0.050% is the only string function sampled)
candidates.pathology: The Zbb orc.b word-at-a-time strlen/strcmp/strncmp in arch/riscv/lib are alternative-patched, so the XIP kernel runs the byte versions.
candidates.replacement: Compile-time Zbb versions when `__riscv_zbb` is defined. Low priority, given the measured heat.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: negligible on current profiles
candidates.exactness: Identical results.

candidates.name: getenv (musl linear environ scan)
candidates.where: board libc.so getenv; the hot caller is unidentified (libGL's knob() results are cached per process in gl/tinygl/source/raster_sel.c and s31_mtex.c)
candidates.apps: quakespasm GL runs, tyrquake
candidates.heat: MEASURED share of CPU0: getenv 0.09% (prof9), 0.05% (p10c), 0.03% (p10b, prof1, tgp14, tgp16, tgprof, fp-g4)
candidates.pathology: Each call is a strncmp over every environ entry. Something is calling it at frame or audio-period rate.
candidates.replacement: First find the caller (SDL_getenv in SDL audio/X11 is the likely source) and fix it there. Failing that, interpose getenv with a cache keyed on the environ pointer and a setenv/putenv/unsetenv generation counter, also interposed.
candidates.est_gain: unmeasured; bounded by 0.03-0.09%
candidates.exactness: The same pointer must be returned; the cache has to be invalidated on any environ change.

candidates.name: memcpy / memset with small constant sizes routed through the interposed s31str
candidates.where: lvdesk 27 call sites at 64 bytes or less (send_event_d/send_error/send_reply memcpy 32 B, render_request memset 27 B, prop_set memset 20 B, and others); tiopex-quake memmove 3 B x4 (Mod_LoadAliasModel) and 16 B
candidates.apps: lvdesk X request and reply paths, tiopex model load
candidates.heat: unmeasured
candidates.pathology: Small fixed-size struct copies still pay PLT, the s31str dispatch (CPU0-PIE vs scalar via rseq) and the libc entry overhead for 20-32 bytes that 2-8 word moves would cover.
candidates.replacement: Give s31str's entry a leading `n<=64` path of unrolled word or byte moves before any routing decision. For first-party lvdesk, build with -fno-builtin removed or use __builtin_memcpy with constant sizes so GCC inlines them.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: tens of instructions per call; the CPU share is likely small
candidates.exactness: Byte-identical memory effects; memmove overlap semantics must be kept.

candidates.name: pthread_mutex_lock / unlock / trylock / timedlock (musl, uncontended)
candidates.where: board libc.so: pthread_mutex_unlock, __pthread_mutex_trylock_owner, pthread_mutex_timedlock, pthread_mutex_lock, pthread_mutex_trylock
candidates.apps: SDL audio thread vs main thread, libX11 (XLockDisplay), libGL threaded rasteriser
candidates.heat: MEASURED combined mutex share of CPU0: 0.04-0.20% (fp-g2 0.20%, tgprof 0.19%, fp-g4 0.17%, p10b 0.15%)
candidates.pathology: musl routes even a normal uncontended lock through several calls (lock -> timedlock -> trylock_owner) with a_cas lr/sc loops and fences.
candidates.replacement: No exact interposition is safe: the mutex layout is musl-internal. Report it as a source-level target instead: libX11 built without XTHREADS locking where single-threaded, or fewer SDL_LockAudio round trips.
candidates.est_gain: unmeasured; bounded by ~0.2%
candidates.exactness: Not applicable as an interposition; source changes must keep locking correctness.

result.coverage_notes:
Everything below is in build/cloud/probes/wide-helpers/. No tracked files were modified.

HELPER CENSUS
- census.sh / census.txt: nm symbol census over 96 riscv32 ELFs (the overlay's /usr/{lib,bin,sbin}, lvdesk/, rootfs/, artifacts/, the toolchain libc).
- sigscan.py / sigscan.txt: full-body signature scan of every libgcc.a member except the excluded soft-double, TF, HF and BF ones. It masks non-branch relocs and finds helpers in stripped binaries, then counts jal/call sites per match.

NEGATIVE RESULTS (measured, static)
- No binary references __muldi3, __mulsi3, __clzsi2, __ctzsi2, __popcountsi2, __bswapsi2, __bswapdi2, __extendhfsf2, __riscv_save/restore (no -msave-restore), __atomic_* or __sync_*, and nothing has libatomic as NEEDED. With Zbb and M in -march, GCC inlines all of the bit helpers.
- lvdesk has 0 lr/sc/amo. The only compiler helpers in shipped userspace are 64-bit div/mod and shift (__ashldi3/__lshrdi3 via soft-fp conversions), int64<->float conversions, and the excluded soft-double and TF helpers.
- The overlay's X client libs (libX11, Xext, Xt, Xft, fontconfig) contain no helper bodies except one __divdi3 each in libXt and libXrender. The overlay's libfreetype.so.6.20.6 is a 4.7 KB stub, so the real FreeType (FT_MulDiv/FT_DivFix -> __udivdi3, INFERRED) could not be inspected.

HEAT
- userprof.py re-resolves the 16 committed h1s PC-sample sets (glquake prof/prof8/prof9/kfast prof10a-c/present-probe, tyrquake tgp*) per DSO function using the committed nm and maps files.
- kprof-p10.txt resolves the kernel PCs of prof10a-c against kfast/base-nm.txt. That the nm matches those kernels is INFERRED.

CORRECTIONS
- My first pass attributed 0.23-0.30% to tyr-glquake __ashldi3. That was a resolver artefact: an absolute-address fallback lookup. The PCs are pre-`main` PLT slots, and the PLT candidate reports them as such.
- The m4 (tgl-gears) and present-prof (gp/lp) sets did not resolve, because their nm names do not match the maps.

QEMU MEASUREMENTS (board ISA, instruction counts only, no timing)
- fmt.c: printf/strtod icounts.
- sf.c: strtof fast path. 0/300,000 mismatches.
- cvt.c: int64<->float, all 4 rounding modes, bits and fflags, 0/4,000,000 mismatches. Negative control: 1,080 bad.
- div.c: libgcc 64-bit division classes, plus a 32-bit front-end and a /1e6 chain. 0/2,000,000 after a bug fix.
- kdiv.c: kernel generic __div64_32 against a divu-based version. 0/1,000,000.
- fm.c: float libm icounts.

CAVEATS
- The toolchain libc.so is not the board's libc 352e9417. Its helper bodies differ from libgcc's (for example __udivdi3 is 866 B against 732 B), and the board's TF helpers carry esp.lp loops, so absolute icounts differ on the board.

NOT REACHED
- No libSDL/SDL2/libasound/libGL/quakespasm/tyr-glquake/Xorg binaries are in the repo, only nm files. Their per-site call counts are unknown, including the SDL1 __divdi3 caller and the target behind libGL PLT slot 0xc570.
- The kernel tree (linux-71-port) is not checked out, so the Kconfig claims (XIP -> no RISCV_ALTERNATIVE -> no Zbb/Zbc bitops, CRC or strings) are INFERRED from upstream, supported by the generic symbols present in base-nm.txt.

OVERLAPS
- Roadmap §5 already kills a generic 64-bit division replacement (69 vs 51). My division candidate is only the 32-bit-range front-end: MEASURED 51->9 instr, +3 on the rest.
- The float and double libm items overlap roadmap W7/A5 and are included for their measured heat.

candidates.name: crc32c / crc32 (kernel lib/crc) via Zbc clmul
candidates.where: kernel XIP: lib/crc generic table code (crc32c_base/crc32_le_base), with the riscv clmul variant compiled out
candidates.apps: ext4 metadata_csum and jbd2 on every metadata write and verify on the SD root, so all file writes, mjpegrec/SD logging and swapfile metadata; also any other kernel crc32 user
candidates.heat: unmeasured. The kernel profiles have no crc32 symbol above the flat tail, and whether the card's ext4 has metadata_csum is not confirmed: BR2_TARGET_ROOTFS_EXT2_MKFS_OPTIONS="-b 4096" (esp32s31_rootfs_defconfig:109) leaves e2fsprogs' default feature set, which includes metadata_csum (INFERRED). Run dumpe2fs -h to settle it.
candidates.pathology: On this XIP kernel the Makefile's `--enable RISCV_ISA_ZBC` (Makefile:682) is a no-op. RISCV_ALTERNATIVE depends on !XIP_KERNEL (patches/0003 applied in reverse), and the ISA_Z* options depend on it. current-state.md:1158-1167 CONFIRMED this for ZBB, and ZBC is gated the same way (INFERRED from upstream Kconfig). So the kernel runs a byte-at-a-time 1 KB-table CRC whose table sits in flash rodata.
candidates.replacement: Kernel arch patch: build the riscv crc-clmul path unconditionally, since Zbc is always present on this SoC. No alternatives or static key are needed: one folding or Barrett loop per 32-bit word, no table.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED in QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-hwfit/ck.c, -Os, CRC over 4 KB): bytewise table 40,979 instructions against a per-word clmul Barrett loop at 9,240. That is 4.4x fewer instructions, with bit-identical results checked. It also removes flash-rodata table loads. Wall-clock is unmeasured.
candidates.exactness: The CRC value must be bit-identical. It is a pure function, verifiable exhaustively per word and with random buffers against the table version. Checked in the probe (mode 5 OK).

candidates.name: kernel bitops/strings/csum Zbb paths (__ffs, __fls, ffz, hweight, strlen, strcmp, strncmp, csum_partial)
candidates.where: kernel XIP: asm-generic/bitops/__ffs.h etc. generic C, lib/hweight.c __sw_hweight32, arch/riscv/lib/strlen.S etc. non-Zbb variants, and arch/riscv/lib/csum.c without its Zbb branch
candidates.apps: All workloads. Timer-wheel and cpumask find_next_bit scans, the scheduler, idr, the page allocator, path lookup, and the TCP/UDP checksum for Wi-Fi traffic.
candidates.heat: unmeasured per symbol. The only anchors are group totals: 'kernel: sched/tick/timer' 12.8% and 'kernel other' 4.9% of GLQuake hart-1 samples (artifacts/gl/glquake/prof9/PROFILE.txt), with no single symbol above 1% (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:925-935).
candidates.pathology: current-state.md:1158-1167 CONFIRMS it: CONFIG_RISCV_ISA_ZBB and RISCV_ALTERNATIVE are absent because of XIP, so 'the kernel's zbb ffs/fls/strlen/memchr paths are all off while -march advertises zbb'. KCFLAGS does pass zbb (Makefile:766), but the generic bitops are written as shift ladders, not builtins, so GCC cannot turn them into clz/ctz/cpop.
candidates.replacement: Small arch header patch. When __riscv_zbb is defined, use the asm-generic builtin-__ffs.h, builtin-__fls.h, builtin-ffs.h and builtin-fls.h, and __builtin_popcount for __arch_hweight*. That gives single ctz/clz/cpop instructions. Also select the Zbb strlen/strcmp/strncmp bodies and the csum Zbb branch unconditionally, because the SoC always has Zbb. No alternatives are needed.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED. A generic __ffs is about 10-15 instructions of shifts and branches against 1 for ctz, and __sw_hweight32 is about 12 against 1 cpop. The share of the flat kernel tail is unknown. Price it with a PROF=1 before/after or with the L1 counter instrument (C04).
candidates.exactness: Results are identical by definition, including the input 0 cases, which the kernel defines as undefined for __ffs and __fls.

candidates.name: hosted transport frame checksum (s31_frame_checksum)
candidates.where: kernel: esp32s31-hosted-sram.c:171-178 (patches/0048), called on TX at :501 and on RX at :876 for every Wi-Fi/BT frame
candidates.apps: Every Wi-Fi packet (wget 402 KB/s, s31-record serve 915 KB/s, streamed capture 25.8 Mbit/s) and every BT/A2DP ACL packet (47/s while streaming)
candidates.heat: unmeasured directly. INFERRED from rates: at 3.2 MB/s TX and ~6 instructions/byte that is about 19 M instructions/s, a few % of a core, plus the XIP instruction-fetch penalty if this is not in .text.fast. current-state.md:4810-4815 notes that the transport's hot path 'runs from XIP flash at ~6x'.
candidates.pathology: The checksum is `while (length--) checksum += *frame++;`, a byte-at-a-time u16 additive loop. -Os keeps it byte-serial, and it runs over the full frame on both TX and RX.
candidates.replacement: SWAR word loop: add (x & 0x00ff00ff) + ((x>>8) & 0x00ff00ff) per aligned 32-bit word into lane accumulators, flushed every 128 words, with a byte prologue and epilogue. The result is identical mod 2^16. Optionally fold it into the memcpy_toio / memcpy_fromio pass that already touches the bytes, and place both in .text.fast.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED in QEMU (ck.c, 1500-byte frame, -Os): 9,018 instructions against 4,198, which is 2.15x fewer with the checksum verified equal. A tighter unrolled loop should approach 1.5 instructions/byte (INFERRED). Board timing is unmeasured.
candidates.exactness: The 16-bit sum must equal the bytewise sum mod 2^16 for every length and alignment. This is easy to verify exhaustively for lengths 0-2048 across the four alignments. hart0 validates the same value (current-state.md:208-211).

candidates.name: __div64_32 / div_u64_rem / div_s64_rem (and mul_u64_u64_div_u64)
candidates.where: kernel: lib/math/div64.c generic __div64_32, a shift-subtract bit loop; div_u64_rem sits in flash and div_s64_rem in RAM text
candidates.apps: timekeeping (ns to timespec conversions), scheduler/PELT, cputime_adjust for /proc/<pid>/stat reads (s31-deskmon, top), jiffies conversions
candidates.heat: MEASURED small: 'flash div_u64_rem' 0.1% and 'RAM div_s64_rem' 0.1% of GLQuake hart-1 samples (prof9 PROFILE.txt, kernel other / sched groups). The bucket resolution is 64 B, so __div64_32 itself may sit in a neighbouring bucket.
candidates.pathology: RV32 has divu (32/32) but no 64/32 divide, and the kernel falls back to asm-generic's bit-at-a-time __div64_32: about 32 iterations of 64-bit compare, subtract and shift, roughly 300+ instructions. Compare libgcc's normalised __udivdi3, which the userspace roadmap measured at 51 instructions. The roadmap killed the userspace 64-bit division idea because libgcc is already good; the kernel does not use libgcc.
candidates.replacement: arch/riscv/include/asm/div64.h providing __div64_32 via the Hacker's Delight divlu: normalise with clz (Zbb) and do two 32/16 divu steps. That is about 30-40 instructions. mul_u64_u64_div_u64 gets the same treatment.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: about 5-8x per call on the divide itself, but only about 0.1-0.2% of CPU0 at the measured heat. Cheap and exact, low priority.
candidates.exactness: Quotient and remainder must be identical for all inputs, including divisor > 2^31 and dividend < divisor. Checkable against the generic routine with random plus edge vectors in QEMU.

candidates.name: copy_to_user / fallback_scalar_usercopy (uaccess.S)
candidates.where: kernel XIP flash: arch/riscv/lib/uaccess.S fallback_scalar_usercopy_sum_enabled
candidates.apps: Every buffered read(): app, pak and WAD loading, library reads, config reads, pipes and sockets (xshim control path)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: warm page-cache read() at 13.6 MB/s, against the SD's 32 MB/s. The copy costs 2.4x the SD read and is about 70% of a cold buffered read (current-state.md:2212-2231). The symbol is 0.2% of GLQuake samples (prof9 PROFILE.txt, paging/mm). Current-state records it as unmovable by FASTFN because it is assembly (current-state.md:96-100).
candidates.pathology: 13.6 MB/s is 3.8x below the CPU's own measured userspace memcpy of a 153,600-byte block at 51 MB/s payload (accel-plan.md:36-43: 2.99 ms). So it is not simply the PSRAM ceiling it has been attributed to (INFERRED). Candidates are the flash-resident loop, first-touch faults on the destination, and a misaligned shift path. The cause is undiagnosed.
candidates.replacement: First, attribute the gap: time copy_to_user into a pre-faulted, aligned buffer and compare it with memcpy of the same page-cache page in the kernel. Then either put an unrolled word-copy usercopy in RAM text (with the assembly moved into .text..fast by hand), or use a GDMA/PPA-assisted copy for page runs of 128 KB or more. That crossover is measured at about 128 KB in accel-plan.md:59, so only large read() calls would qualify.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: up to about 3x on warm read() throughput if the gap is code or alignment rather than bandwidth, which would make a cold read roughly 9.6 to about 20 MB/s. Unknown until the gap is attributed.
candidates.exactness: Byte-identical copies with identical fault/EFAULT semantics and partial-copy return counts.

candidates.name: clear_page / memset for anonymous faults (kernel flash memset)
candidates.where: kernel XIP: memset in arch/riscv/lib/memset.S (flash)
candidates.apps: Every anon/zero page fault (game heaps, swap-in of zero pages), GLQuake paging
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 'flash memset' 0.4% of GLQuake hart-1 samples under paging/mm (prof9 PROFILE.txt). The perf-plan kernel profile lists memset inside page faults (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:929).
candidates.pathology: It runs from flash (current-state.md:96-100 lists memcpy/memset as unmovable assembly). It is fill-bound: kernel fills reach 192 MB/s (accel-plan.md:43).
candidates.replacement: A RAM-resident unrolled clear_page (a 4 KB fixed size, so no tail logic) placed by hand into .text..fast. GDMA or PPA zero-fill is not worth it at 4 KB against a fixed cost of 13 us plus a wait of several hundred us (accel-plan.md:45-48).
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: under 0.4% of CPU0 at best. Only the instruction-fetch part is recoverable.
candidates.exactness: The page must be zero-filled. Trivially exact.

candidates.name: generic_atomic64_* (hashed-spinlock 64-bit atomics on RV32)
candidates.where: kernel: lib/atomic64.c generic_atomic64_add/read/set etc. (RAM)
candidates.apps: scheduler and timekeeping counters, any atomic64_t user
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 'RAM generic_atomic64_add' 0.1% of GLQuake samples, plus an unknown part of 'RAM do_raw_spin_lock' 0.6% (prof9 PROFILE.txt)
candidates.pathology: RV32A has no 64-bit LR/SC, so every atomic64 operation is irqsave plus a hashed raw spinlock plus irqrestore.
candidates.replacement: Audit the callers. Where atomic64 is only used as a statistics counter updated on one CPU, per-cpu u64 or u64_stats_sync avoids the lock. It is not a drop-in exact replacement for true RMW atomics.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: at most about 0.1-0.5% of CPU0
candidates.exactness: Semantics must be preserved across the lent CPU. Low priority and caller-specific.

candidates.name: printf-family %f/%e/%g (musl fmt_fp in long double)
candidates.where: libc.so (musl printf_core -> fmt_fp using long double = IEEE quad, soft-float via __addtf3/__multf3/__subtf3 linked into libc)
candidates.apps: Any app formatting floats: QuakeSpasm/TyrQuake (Cvar_SetValue, HUD fps, console), SDL hints, X clients (Xt/Xaw resource converters), s31 tools and deskmon printing percentages
candidates.heat: unmeasured per app. Per call MEASURED in QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-hwfit/fmt.c, upstream musl 1.2.5 sysroot): snprintf %d 864 instructions, "%.1f" 3,466, "%4.1f fps" 3,608, %f 6,937, %g 7,006.
candidates.pathology: There is no D extension, so musl's long-double (binary128) formatting is software quad arithmetic, and on the board's libgcc those tf3 helpers even contain esp.lp hardware loops (tools/cloud/README.md). %f costs about 8x %d.
candidates.replacement: Interpose snprintf/vsnprintf/printf/fprintf/sprintf with a wrapper that parses the format and handles plain %[flags][width][.prec]{f,e,g} of a double through an exact integer path: a Ryu-printf or Grisu-exact style formatter using 64x64 multiplies. Delegate every other conversion, and every locale or rounding-mode case other than RNE, to musl's vfprintf.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: roughly 5-10x per float conversion, about 3.5-7k down to about 0.5-1k instructions. The app-level effect is unknown until call rates are counted, for example with an LD_PRELOAD counter over a Quake timedemo.
candidates.exactness: Output strings must be byte-identical to musl, which is exact correctly-rounded decimal, for every double, precision and flag combination. Verify with a random plus edge-case differential against musl in QEMU. errno and return values must match.

candidates.name: strtod / strtof / atof / sscanf %f (musl __floatscan in long double)
candidates.where: libc.so: strtod/strtof/strtold -> __floatscan (long double decimal conversion); the scanf family goes through the same path
candidates.apps: Config and text parsing: QuakeSpasm/TyrQuake entity parsing (ED_ParseEpair ev_vector uses sscanf "%f %f %f" in id's code), cvars, X resource databases, fontconfig/xftlite config, ALSA config (alsa.conf numbers), SDL hints
candidates.heat: unmeasured per app. Per call MEASURED in QEMU (fmt.c): strtod("123.456") 14,070 instructions, strtof("0.75") 8,644, sscanf("3.5","%f") 9,733, atof("1") 1,145 (short fast path).
candidates.pathology: All of it is long-double software arithmetic on a machine without D.
candidates.replacement: Interpose strtod/strtof/atof with an Eisel-Lemire (fast_float) exact path: a 64-bit mantissa times a 128-bit power-of-five table, using mulhu. Fall back to musl for ambiguous halfway cases, more than 19 digits, hex floats, inf/nan, non-RNE rounding and non-C locales. sscanf cannot be reached cheaply, because musl calls __floatscan internally. That would need a separate vfscanf interposition, which is heavy, so leave it.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: about 10x per strtod call on the common path, 14k down to about 1-1.5k instructions. A map load that parses thousands of numbers could save tens of ms. Call counts are needed.
candidates.exactness: The result double or float must be bit-identical (correctly rounded). endptr, errno (ERANGE on overflow and underflow) and subnormal handling must match. Verify with a differential against musl over random decimal strings and the known hard cases.

candidates.name: float libm in double: sinf, cosf, sincosf, tanf, expf, exp2f, logf, powf, hypotf
candidates.where: libc.so (musl: __sindf/__cosdf/__tandf polynomials in double, and the ARM-optimized expf/logf/powf computing in double), so every double op is a soft-double call
candidates.apps: sdlquake imports sincosf (artifacts/s31fp-next/imports.txt); audio clients synthesising per sample; any SDL2 or app code using float trig. libGL already has its own float versions (G01), so it is excluded.
candidates.heat: MEASURED on the board for a synthetic client: sdltone calling sinf once per sample spent about 9 us per call, about 3000 cycles, which is 40-50% of a core at 48 kHz (artifacts/audio/first-principles-2026-09-27/REPORT.md:101-105). Real-app call rates are unmeasured. Per call MEASURED in QEMU (lib.c): sinf 2,036, cosf 1,873, tanf 2,599, expf 1,808, exp2f 1,620, logf 1,706, powf 4,085, hypotf 602 instructions. atan2f (117), log10f (90), acosf (49) and fmodf (78) are already pure float and cheap.
candidates.pathology: The results are float but musl evaluates them in double, and double is soft on this core. Note that the roadmap deferred a related 'float-float sinf/powf fast path (A5)' (s31fp-arithmetic-opl-roadmap:383) on exactness grounds.
candidates.replacement: This path is exact, not approximate. The unary functions (sinf/cosf/tanf/expf/exp2f/logf) have only 2^32 inputs, so a replacement can be verified exhaustively against the board's musl. Implement each as musl's own algorithm, with its double steps done in a fused, specialised integer or double-float form whose bounded exponents are known, or as a float-only kernel. Accept a function only if it matches all 2^32 inputs bit-for-bit, including fflags. powf is binary (2^64 inputs) and stays deferred.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: 2k down to a few hundred instructions per call (5-10x). That matters only where apps call these per sample or per vertex.
candidates.exactness: Results, fflags and errno must be bit-identical to the board's libc across all inputs. Exhaustive 2^32 host verification against a bit-exact model of musl, then a board spot check.

candidates.name: strncmp / strcasecmp / strncasecmp / strchr / strchrnul (byte-serial musl)
candidates.where: libc.so (musl generic C; not interposed by s31str, whose RES list is memmove memchr memrchr memcmp bcmp strcmp strcoll strnlen strrchr strstr memmem plus mem* at s31str.c:539-540)
candidates.apps: ALSA config search (_snd_config_search/snd_config_walk were hot during SDL2 hotplug enumeration, perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:976-980), Xrm/Xt resource lookup, SDL hint and env lookups, getenv, fontconfig/xftlite, BlueZ/D-Bus string handling
candidates.heat: unmeasured per function. Per call MEASURED in QEMU (lib.c): strncmp over 200 equal bytes 2,217 instructions (about 11/byte), strcasecmp over 200 bytes 2,077, strchr over 255 bytes 691 (already word-at-a-time).
candidates.pathology: musl strncmp and strcasecmp are byte loops. musl's word-at-a-time routines use the HASZERO bit trick plus a byte rescan and never orc.b or ctz, even though Zbb is present (0 orc.b in the toolchain libc disassembly).
candidates.replacement: Add them to s31str's scalar set. For strncmp, use aligned word compare with orc.b-based NUL detection and ctz/rev8 to locate the first differing byte. For strcasecmp, use a SWAR ASCII fold ((x | 0x20202020) masked to letters) with a byte fallback for non-ASCII or locale cases. Also use orc.b+ctz to locate the terminator in sc_strlen and sc_memchr (s31str.c:104-133) instead of the byte rescan.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: 3-5x on long equal prefixes; little on short strings. App-level heat is unknown and probably small.
candidates.exactness: Return sign and value semantics must match musl (musl returns the byte difference), with the same page-safety rules s31str already enforces (aligned words only). strcasecmp must match musl's C-locale tolower exactly.

candidates.name: SBC analysis filterbank (libsbc sbc_analyze_* / sbc_calc_scalefactors)
candidates.where: libsbc.so (s31-bt / s31-a2dp; the primitives are selected through function pointers in sbc_init_primitives)
candidates.apps: A2DP streaming to headphones (s31-a2dp / s31-bt)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: codec alone 9.1% of a core, 453 ms CPU per 5 s of 48 kHz audio on a quiet system, and 1.8 ms per 8-frame packet (current-state.md:4790-4800; rootfs/sbcbench.c). The larger measured A2DP cost is the hosted-transport interrupt load (about 4 ms per IRQ), not the codec.
candidates.pathology: The generic C 'simd' filterbank does 16x16 to 32-bit MACs one at a time. The S31's PIE has 16-bit multiply-accumulate into wide accumulators, but it is reachable only on CPU0.
candidates.replacement: Override the analysis function pointers after sbc_init: interpose sbc_init/sbc_reinit, or copy-patch sbc_init_primitives' tail. The override points at a PIE esp.vmulas.s16 filterbank on CPU0, routed by the rseq check s31str already uses, and a scalar fallback elsewhere. Pinning s31-a2dp's encoder thread to CPU0 would make routing trivial.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: the filterbank might get 2-4x cheaper, which is at most about 5-7% of a core while streaming. It is secondary to the transport's IRQ cost.
candidates.exactness: The int32 subband samples must be bit-identical to libsbc's generic path. This is integer arithmetic, so it is exactly verifiable with the libsbc test vectors and sbcbench output hashes.

candidates.name: SDL2 software-renderer converters: Blit_RGB888_RGB565, Blit1to4, SDL_ConvertPixels, SDL_FillRect (SDL_memset4)
candidates.where: libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10 (static functions in SDL_blit_N.c / SDL_blit_1.c / SDL_fillrect.c; body-signature identifiable)
candidates.apps: SDL2 clients: tyr-quake / tyr-glquake (SDL2), chocolate-doom if re-enabled, any SDL2 app with an indexed or ARGB texture presented to the 16-bit window
candidates.heat: MEASURED: chocolate-doom main thread spent about 30% in SDL2's own converters and copies (Blit1to4, Blit_RGB888_RGB565, SDL_FillRect, memcpy) (current-state.md:8650-8660). The sdlbench SDL2 indexed texture frame costs 10.6 ms for conversion plus upload and 16.7 ms for clear, copy and flush of a 44.4 ms frame (sdlbench-results-2026-09-13.md:165-167, single run). For stock TyrQuake on SDL2, 'libs 14% (memcpy 4)' (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:985-989).
candidates.pathology: Per-pixel shift/mask packing in -Os C (BR2_TARGET_OPTIMIZATION -Os, esp32s31_rootfs_defconfig:24). The 8888-to-565 packing is compute over PSRAM-streamed data.
candidates.replacement: Copy-patch the identified bodies. RGB888 to RGB565 becomes a PIE 128-bit load/shift/and/or pack on CPU0 via rseq, with a scalar 2-pixel-per-word SWAR fallback. Blit1to4 becomes an unrolled word-store LUT loop with sh2add. SDL_FillRect becomes a word-fill. The PIE memset measured 1.00x, so fills gain only if the per-pixel loop is the cost, not bandwidth.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: RGB888 to RGB565 perhaps 1.5-3x on its share (compute-heavy). LUT and fill kernels are bandwidth-bound, so 0-20%. Price it with W0a heat on a live SDL2 app first.
candidates.exactness: The output pixels must be bit-identical, including SDL's rounding (truncation) and alpha handling, verified by hashing converted buffers across random inputs and all widths and alignments.

candidates.name: SDL_mixer mix_channels -> SDL_MixAudio (S16) and SDL 1.2 SDL_ConvertAudio filters
candidates.where: libSDL-1.2.so.0.11.4 SDL_MixAudio / SDL_Convert* / SDL_RateMUL2; libSDL_mixer-1.2 mix_channels
candidates.apps: prboom (NEEDED libSDL_mixer, artifacts/s31fp-next/imports.txt), other SDL_mixer 1.2 users; SDL_ConvertAudio for apps whose format differs from the device
candidates.heat: unmeasured. The roadmap killed HW3 for OpenTyrian and tiopex, which do not use it (s31fp-arithmetic-opl-roadmap:374), and did not price prboom. It is INFERRED small: 8 channels x 22,050 x 2 samples x about 17-19 instructions is about 1% of a core.
candidates.pathology: Per sample it does multiply, shift, add and clamp in scalar code. GCC already emits Zbb min/max (roadmap:374), so a scalar twin buys nothing.
candidates.replacement: Only a PIE saturating 16-bit vector mix on CPU0 (8 lanes per op) could win. Otherwise leave it.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: at most about 1% of a core for prboom sound. Low priority. It is listed so the prboom case is not re-derived.
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical samples, including SDL's ADJUST_VOLUME truncation and clamp order.

candidates.name: __floatdisf / __floatundisf / __fixsfdi (int64 <-> float)
candidates.where: libgcc, statically linked into apps (for example tiopex-quake.dbg contains __floatdisf); libc.so exports __fixsfdi
candidates.apps: tiopex-quake and any app converting 64-bit integers (timers, Uint64 ticks, file offsets) to or from float
candidates.heat: unmeasured. No profile shows them. Per-call cost is roughly 50-100 soft-float instructions (INFERRED; not counted here).
candidates.pathology: RV32F has no 64-bit integer conversions, so libgcc's generic soft-fp handles them even though an F unit exists.
candidates.replacement: Exact short sequences: if the high word is a sign-extension, one fcvt.s.w (or .wu); otherwise normalise with clz, round to 24 bits in integer with RNE plus sticky bits, and assemble the float. __fixsfdi splits into exponent cases. These are exact and short, and fit the v2 body-matched copy-patch framework.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: about 3-5x per call. The app-level gain is unknown and likely tiny.
candidates.exactness: Results and fflags must be bit-identical to libgcc in every rounding mode (the v2 harness already checks fflags and frm).

candidates.name: lrintf / lrint path (rintf + fcvt)
candidates.where: libc.so lrintf at 0x3870e (toolchain libc): calls rintf and then fcvt.w.s rtz
candidates.apps: Audio and graphics code rounding floats to int (SDL2 audio, resamplers, games)
candidates.heat: unmeasured. MEASURED 36 instructions per call in QEMU (lib.c mode 15).
candidates.pathology: It makes two calls and a round-trip where a single fcvt.w.s with dynamic rounding does the job.
candidates.replacement: lrintf is fcvt.w.s a0, fa0, dyn after fmv.w.x. Take care with out-of-range inputs, where musl returns the converted rintf and the C standard leaves the result unspecified, and with FE_INVALID.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: about 36 down to 3 instructions per call. Only matters at per-sample call rates.
candidates.exactness: Values and fflags must match musl for in-range inputs. Out-of-range and NaN cases must also be checked for identical result and flags, or delegated to musl.

candidates.name: xshim row hash + copy (FNV-1a row scan then separate copy)
candidates.where: lvdesk: xshim.c row_hash :329-345 and scan loop :7801-7815; lvdesk.c fsrh_hash :6455
candidates.apps: Every MIT-SHM client presented windowed (glxgears, sdlquake windowed, TyrQuake X11, prboom windowed)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: xshm_request (copy plus hash) 12.7% of CPU0 in windowed glxgears (gl-plan-2026-09-25.md:784) and 2.8% of samples in GLQuake prof9 (PROFILE.txt).
candidates.pathology: It makes two full read passes over the client buffer, one to hash and one to copy changed rows, through PSRAM, which is the scarcest resource (13.6 MB/s class). FNV-1a is a serial xor-multiply chain.
candidates.replacement: Fuse hash and copy into one pass per row: hash while copying into the destination, then undo or skip the copy only when unchanged. Or compare against the destination directly with a memcmp-style word or PIE compare on CPU0, which needs no hash state at all. This is first-party code, so change the source.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: up to about half of the read traffic of xshm_request for changed rows, a few % of CPU0 in windowed present-bound cases.
candidates.exactness: Damage results must be identical (the same rows are detected as changed). The hash is private state, so its value need not be preserved.

candidates.name: musl qsort (smoothsort)
candidates.where: libc.so qsort
candidates.apps: Anything sorting: QuakeSpasm/TyrQuake (sorting surfaces, file lists), fontconfig, xfiles directory listings, ALSA hint lists
candidates.heat: unmeasured. MEASURED in QEMU: 64 ints in 44,853 instructions, about 700 per element (lib.c mode 12), including the comparator calls.
candidates.pathology: Smoothsort's constant factor is high for the small arrays typical here. It has no small-n insertion-sort cutoff.
candidates.replacement: This is only exact if the output order is identical, and qsort is not stable. Only a replacement that reproduces smoothsort's final permutation, including the order of equal elements, is safe, and that is hard. It is realistic only for callers known to have unique keys, which makes it app-specific.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: 2-3x for n < 100, but it is exact only when the comparator never returns 0 for distinct elements.
candidates.exactness: The final array must be byte-identical, including the order of equal elements. That is the blocking constraint, so this is low priority.

candidates.name: malloc/free (musl mallocng)
candidates.where: libc.so malloc/free/realloc/calloc
candidates.apps: All clients, with allocation-heavy X/SDL/ALSA paths
candidates.heat: unmeasured (rootfs/mallocprof.c measures bytes, not time). MEASURED in QEMU: malloc(32)+free about 1,166 instructions per pair and malloc(4096)+free 539 (lib.c).
candidates.pathology: mallocng trades speed for low fragmentation and hardening. A faster allocator is not an exact replacement and risks RAM, which is the binding constraint (CLAUDE.md).
candidates.replacement: Probably none. At most a thread-local small-size free-list cache in front of mallocng. It would have to be measured for RSS before it is considered.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: small, and possibly a RAM regression. Listed for completeness.
candidates.exactness: The semantics (alignment, errno, realloc behaviour) are exact but addresses change. RAM is the constraint.

candidates.name: SHA-1/SHA-256/AES in userspace (wpa_supplicant internal crypto, busybox sha*/md5sum) -> S31 SHA/AES engines
candidates.where: wpa_supplicant (internal crypto: PBKDF2-SHA1 when a passphrase is configured, EAPOL HMAC/AES key wrap); busybox sha1sum/sha256sum; kernel driver drivers/crypto/esp32s31-crypto.c
candidates.apps: Wi-Fi association, deploy and verification tooling
candidates.heat: unmeasured and low (one-off per association or per file). The kernel AES/SHA offload is not even registered: its self-test fails with -EIO (current-state.md:5162-5165). 'Nothing in userspace uses kernel crypto offload (wpa_supplicant carries its own; BlueZ uses software AES)' (current-state.md:5017-5019).
candidates.pathology: Software SHA1 runs at -Os in XIP. PBKDF2 is 16,384 SHA1 compressions per passphrase association (INFERRED).
candidates.replacement: Fix the driver self-test, then either interpose wpa_supplicant's sha1_vector/pbkdf2_sha1 exports (internal symbols, so copy-patch) with AF_ALG calls, or store psk= hex in the config so PBKDF2 never runs. AF_ALG round trips cost syscalls, so this only helps bulk hashing.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: association latency perhaps 50-100 ms lower. Not a steady-state CPU lever.
candidates.exactness: Digests are identical by definition.

candidates.name: zlib crc32/adler32 (libpng inside prboom)
candidates.where: libz.so / libpng16.so (prboom NEEDED libpng16, artifacts/s31fp-next/imports.txt)
candidates.apps: prboom (PNG screenshots, and PNG lumps if present)
candidates.heat: unmeasured, INFERRED near zero during play. No profile shows zlib.
candidates.pathology: Table-driven, byte-oriented crc32 (braided) and adler32 in -Os C. Zbc is unused.
candidates.replacement: Interpose the exported crc32/crc32_z/adler32 with clmul-folding CRC (the same kernel as the kernel crc candidate) and a Zbb or unrolled adler32. These are exported symbols, so this is plain interposition.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: about 4x per byte on CRC (the QEMU kernel above measured 4.4x fewer instructions). App-level effect is about 0.
candidates.exactness: The checksums must be bit-identical, which is easy to verify exhaustively for short inputs and randomly for long ones.

candidates.name: sched_getcpu / getcpu via rseq cpu_id
candidates.where: libc.so sched_getcpu (syscall; no riscv32 vDSO getcpu)
candidates.apps: Callers that use it (thread pools, s31 tools); s31str already registers rseq per thread
candidates.heat: unmeasured, likely near zero for current apps. A trivial syscall costs about 1.6-5 us (current-state.md:1190-1200).
candidates.pathology: It traps even though the answer already sits in the rseq area s31str registers.
candidates.replacement: Interpose sched_getcpu to return rseq->cpu_id when the thread is registered, otherwise fall back to the syscall.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: 1.6 us down to about 5 ns per call. There is no known hot caller.
candidates.exactness: This is the same value the kernel reports at the time of the call. It is inherently racy in both implementations.

result.coverage_notes:
What I searched: the docs listed in the task (perf-review, perf-plan, gl-plan, gl-performance-campaign, current-state, accel-plan, xespv-libc, sdlbench-results, status-and-todo, the s31fp roadmap for exclusions), artifacts/gl/glquake/prof9/PROFILE.txt (8,000-sample GLQuake hart-1 profile), artifacts/gl/phase5 instruction profiles, artifacts/audio/first-principles-2026-09-27/{REPORT,IMPLEMENT}.md, artifacts/s31fp-next imports and inventory, rootfs/s31fp/v3 (s31str/s31clk coverage), lvdesk/xshim sources, patches/0048 (hosted transport), patches/0003 plus Makefile:660-770 (kernel ISA gating), and the Buildroot defconfig (-Os globally, -march including zbb/zbc).

Scans of the overlay and board binaries show Zbb/Zba already emitted by GCC across userspace: libc has clz 66, rev8 66, min/max, but orc.b 0 and clmul 0. The generic 'use Zbb for bit tricks' lever is therefore already harvested in compiled code. What remains is idioms GCC will not form: orc.b string scans, clmul CRC, and the XIP kernel, where Zbb/Zbc paths are compiled out.

New QEMU instruction counts, all under build/cloud/probes/wide-hwfit/ (fmt.c, lib.c, ck.c; upstream musl 1.2.5 QEMU sysroot, not byte-identical to the board's libc 352e9417; counts are instructions, not time):
- printf and strtod family: 864 to 14,070 instructions per call.
- float libm: 1.6 to 4.1k instructions per call.
- strncmp and strcasecmp: about 11 instructions per byte.
- qsort, malloc, lrintf: counted (see those candidates).
- Checksum SWAR against bytewise: 4,198 against 9,018 instructions per 1500 B, verified equal.
- CRC clmul Barrett against table: 9,240 against 40,979 instructions per 4 KB, verified equal.

Deliberately not re-proposed, because they are already closed or deferred with numbers:
- The excluded soft-double, OPL, fused-chain, floor/ceil/trunc and placement work.
- 64-bit userspace division helpers (killed, roadmap:373).
- SDL_MixAudio for OpenTyrian and tiopex (killed, :374).
- DMA engines behind interception (closed, :377).
- Quake span loops (deferred, :375).
- zram and lzo compression (rejected, current-state.md:2259-2279).
- PPA/GDMA for glyphs and small blits (accel-plan crossover of about 128 KB for copies, about 2 KB for blends).
- The alsa-lib linear resampler and route: already replaced by s31route's own converter (IMPLEMENT.md:96-176), so not listed.
- XEspV memset (1.00x) and memcpy (1.10x) already in libc.
- The vDSO clock (shipped).

Hardware loops (xesploop) are unusable in userspace: silent corruption, and the CSRs are M-mode only (Makefile:31-38, accel-plan.md). PIE is CPU0-only, so any PIE candidate needs s31str-style rseq routing. The single-precision FPU is already used for int/float conversion and sqrtf by GCC and musl (sqrtf is one fsqrt.s).

Could not reach:
- No board (no timing, no new heat).
- No System.map or vmlinux, and the kernel tree is not checked out. Kernel claims rest on current-state.md:1158-1167 (ZBB confirmed off), the reversed patches/0003 Kconfig, and upstream structure; ZBC being off is INFERRED from the same gating.
- No SDL, SDL2, SDL_mixer, libpng, zlib, libsbc, libasound or wpa_supplicant binaries in the repo (only nm dumps for SDL-1.2, libasound and libc under artifacts/gl/*/nm). Body signatures for the copy-patch candidates are not yet generated.
- The per-app call rates for printf/strtod/float-libm/strncmp are the key unknowns. A W0a-style LD_PRELOAD call counter over a Quake timedemo, a prboom timedemo and an idle desktop would rank all the libc candidates in one pass.
- ext4 metadata_csum on the card is unconfirmed; dumpe2fs -h is needed.
- The copy_to_user gap (13.6 against about 51 MB/s) is undiagnosed and could be the largest item here if it is not purely bandwidth.

candidates.name: busybox (static) XEspV memcpy/memchr/memrchr/memcmp/strcmp/strnlen
candidates.where: /bin/busybox (CONFIG_STATIC=y, buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/busybox.fragment); musl's XEspV bodies linked statically. current-state.md:6224 says only musl and static busybox carry vendor insns
candidates.apps: every init script, every shell helper lvdesk spawns (sh -l -c), s31-deskmon, runsh harnesses, s31-play/s31-open/xfilesctl
candidates.heat: MEASURED: gl-plan-2026-09-25.md:994-997: busybox sh was 259 of one window's 368 PIE bounces (each = illegal-insn trap on the lent CPU + migration to CPU0, ping-ponging the foreground client 0.5-3 s). Boot forks 301 times (current-state.md:4531)
candidates.pathology: PIE only exists on CPU0. musl's routines enter esp.vld.128 at >=64 B; a shell on CPU1 traps and is migrated onto the game/desktop core. LD_PRELOAD (s31str rseq dispatch) cannot reach a static binary, so busybox is the one big PIE user nothing routes
candidates.replacement: Body-match the six XEspV routines inside busybox (same full-body signature scheme as mksig3/preload3) and redirect them to s31str's rseq-dispatched versions (PIE on CPU0, scalar elsewhere). Delivery options, since no preload runs: rebuild busybox against a libc whose XEspV entry points check rseq cpu_id first, or do the patch at exec from a kernel/binfmt hook, or the kernel sepc redirect below
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: removes ~70% of the measured desktop PIE-bounce count (259/368) and the 0.5-3 s ping-pong episodes they trigger; per-call cost unchanged
candidates.exactness: identical return values and memory effects (same results for memcmp sign, memchr pointer); no errno; must preserve alignment/page-boundary safety of the originals

candidates.name: PIE illegal-instruction trap on CPU1 -> in-kernel redirect to scalar clone instead of migrating
candidates.where: kernel PIE trap handler (the 'existing PIE trap handler' in rootfs/s31fp/v3/README.md) + libc.so XEspV routines (memcpy >=64 B, memchr, memrchr, memcmp, strcmp, strnlen: docs/xespv-libc.md, gl-plan-2026-09-25.md:982-986)
candidates.apps: all processes: libc-INTERNAL callers that s31str cannot interpose (fgets/getline->memchr, fread/fwrite/stdio->memcpy, ld.so strcmp/memcpy, qsort, libsbc's 13 memcpy calls), every daemon started from rcS without LD_PRELOAD (bluetoothd, s31-bt, s31-a2dp, wpa_supplicant, dbus-daemon, crond, ntpd)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: desktop PIE bounces 6-22 per window before lvdesk's lentcpu.c fix, 1-8 after (gl-plan:989-993); long frames showed 0.86-1.18 bounces each vs 0.000-0.005 normally, with 8-12 involuntary switches
candidates.pathology: A bounce = trap + migration + displacement of whatever owns CPU0; the remaining bounces come from paths no userspace interposition reaches (libc-internal hidden calls, static binaries, daemons)
candidates.replacement: Register the address ranges of each PIE routine (libc.so text is XIP and fixed per image; busybox likewise). On the trap from CPU1 with sepc inside a registered routine, rewrite sepc to a per-routine scalar continuation that resumes from that trap point with the same register allocation (the routines are hand-written asm, so live registers at each esp.* site are known), and do not set PIE-affinity/migrate
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: turns each residual bounce (trap+migrate+later return) into one trap (~1.7 us ecall-class round trip measured for SBI, hot-text-plan) and removes CPU0 displacement entirely
candidates.exactness: results identical to the PIE path; must be restart-safe at each trap site (all six are pure or idempotent until their first store; memcpy continuation must resume, not restart, after partial stores)

candidates.name: export LD_PRELOAD=libs31fp to init-launched daemons
candidates.where: /etc/init.d/rcS and S46bluetoothd/S47s31-bt/S40network (overlay etc/init.d); musl has no /etc/ld.so.preload, only /etc/profile sets it (overlay etc/profile) and lvdesk.c:15604-15613 for its children
candidates.apps: bluetoothd (glib/dbus), dbus-daemon, s31-bt, s31-a2dp (libsbc memcpy), wpa_supplicant, crond, ntpd, udevd
candidates.heat: unmeasured for daemons (no per-daemon bounce count recorded); s31-a2dp is 20.4% of a core during playback (current-state.md:4893) and floats across CPUs
candidates.pathology: Daemons never get s31str/s31clk: their memcpy>=64/memchr/strcmp/memcmp calls PIE-trap on CPU1, and their clock_gettime/gettimeofday/time are real syscalls (riscv32 musl has no internal vDSO use)
candidates.replacement: Set LD_PRELOAD in rcS (or per init script) once the v3 library is validated for those programs; exported mem*/str*/clock calls route through rseq dispatch and the vDSO
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: removes daemon-originated PIE bounces and syscall clocks; small absolute CPU, but removes cross-core disturbance of the foreground app
candidates.exactness: same as shipped v3 (bit-exact results, same errno, S31STR/S31CLK kill switches)

candidates.name: musl float libm computed in double: sinf/cosf/sincosf/tanf/powf/expf/exp2f/logf/log2f/hypotf/asinf
candidates.where: libc.so (toolchain copy): sinf@0x3cd00 (474 B, calls __sindf/__cosdf + __adddf3/__subdf3/__extendsfdf2), cosf@0x2c348, sincosf@0x3c7a2, powf@0x39eca (14 __muldf3, 10 __adddf3), expf@0x2ede6, logf@0x384ce, exp2f, log2f, tanf, hypotf, asinf. Contrast: atan2f/atanf/log10f/acosf/sqrtf are pure single-precision (sqrtf = fsqrt.s)
candidates.apps: lvdesk (imports sincosf, cosf, powf, log10f, atan2f: bong synthesis cosf per attack sample lvdesk.c:3150-3159, volume powf lvdesk.c:3033), xshim draw_arc cosf+sinf per arc point (xshim.c:2252-2253, oclock/xeyes-class clients), gamma ramp powf (xshim.c:587,643); sdlquake imports sincosf (s31fp-next/imports.txt)
candidates.heat: MEASURED instruction counts (QEMU, QEMU-sysroot musl 1.2.5, build/cloud/probes/wide-desktop/lcbench-icount.txt): sinf 2,036, cosf 1,873, sincosf 3,889, powf 4,111, expf 1,808, logf 1,697 insns/call vs atan2f 117, log10f 90. Call-rate heat on the desktop unmeasured (bong: ~192 cosf per click at 48 kHz, INFERRED from atk_n=rate*4/1000)
candidates.pathology: double is soft on S31, so each float function pays ~10-20 soft-double helper calls although the FPU could do the whole thing in single precision
candidates.replacement: Interpose with single-precision kernels (FPU, FMA-free) evaluated with a proven error bound, plus a Ziv-style rounding test: if the float result is farther than the combined error of (fast kernel + musl's own double kernel error) from a float rounding boundary, return it; otherwise fall back to musl's routine. Also handle specials/large-argument reduction by falling back
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~10-30x per call on the fast path (100-200 hardware-float insns vs 1.7-4.1k measured)
candidates.exactness: bit-identical to musl's output (fallback on every ambiguous case), including -0, NaN payload/quiet, inf, and fflags only if raised identically (fallback when inexact/underflow flags could differ, or restore fcsr); errno unchanged (musl sets none for these except via __math_oflowf etc. which the fallback covers). Note: fallback path overlaps the excluded fused-soft-double work

candidates.name: musl strtod/strtof/atof/scanf %f via __floatscan/decfloat in binary128 soft-float
candidates.where: libc.so: strtof@0x5873c, strtod@0x5879e -> __floatscan -> decfloat (27 soft-quad call sites) with __multf3/__addtf3/__trunctfsf2; libc has 261 __multf3 and 215 __addtf3 call sites overall (objdump of toolchain libc)
candidates.apps: libXt (imports strtof: resource converters), X clients using atof (xcalc), libasound config reals, busybox awk (static - needs the static-binary route), any sscanf("%f")
candidates.heat: MEASURED instruction counts (QEMU): strtod("3.14159265") 13,315, strtof("0.75") 8,644, atof 9,555, sscanf %f 9,411 vs strtol 211 insns/call. Desktop call rate unmeasured
candidates.pathology: long double is IEEE quad on rv32, fully software; every decimal->binary conversion runs a quad multiply/add chain
candidates.replacement: strtof: Clinger fast path in hardware float (<=7 significant digits, |pow10|<=10 -> one correctly rounded fmul/fdiv of exact operands); strtod: Eisel-Lemire (64x64->128 via mul/mulhu ladder) with fallback to musl for the ambiguous ~1e-3 cases, hex floats, long inputs, inf/nan; wrap sscanf only via strto* interposition where musl's vfscanf calls the exported name (it does not - internal __floatscan), so scanf needs the copy-patch of __floatscan/decfloat
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~50x on common short inputs (≈100-250 insns vs 8.6-13.3k)
candidates.exactness: correctly rounded like musl in round-to-nearest; fall back when frm != RNE; identical endptr, errno=ERANGE behaviour and hex/inf/nan parsing by fallback

candidates.name: musl printf fmt_fp (%f/%g/%e) in binary128 soft-float
candidates.where: libc.so fmt_fp (static, 19 soft-quad call sites) reached from vfprintf/snprintf/printf/fprintf
candidates.apps: xcalc display (sprintf %g per keypress), busybox awk number output (%.6g; static), s31-deskmon (awk printf %.0f each sample), any X client printing floats; lvdesk deliberately avoids %f (lvdesk.c:13238)
candidates.heat: MEASURED instruction counts (QEMU): snprintf("%.2f") 7,102 and ("%g") 7,113 vs snprintf("%d %s %u") 1,743 insns/call. Call rates unmeasured (low on the desktop)
candidates.pathology: musl formats every double by first widening to long double (quad, soft) and doing its big-decimal loop with quad ops
candidates.replacement: Body-match fmt_fp inside libc.so (and busybox) and replace with an exact integer digit generator for doubles (Ryu-printf / exact bignum on 32-bit limbs with Zbb clz), falling back to the original for long double arguments
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~5x per float conversion (removing ~5.4k of 7.1k insns)
candidates.exactness: byte-identical output strings (musl prints exact decimal expansion, correctly rounded in the current rounding mode); fall back if frm != RNE; same return count

candidates.name: libgcc soft-quad helpers __multf3/__addtf3/__subtf3/__divtf3/__trunctfdf2/__extenddftf2/__floatsitf
candidates.where: local copies inside libc.so (and in any static binary: busybox). README (tools/cloud) notes the board libgcc's __addtf3/__subtf3/__multf3 use esp.lp.setup hardware loops
candidates.apps: everything reaching strtod/printf %f/long-double libm (see the two entries above), busybox awk
candidates.heat: unmeasured directly; bounded by the strtod/fmt_fp counts above (MEASURED 7-13k insns per conversion, dominated by these helpers)
candidates.pathology: Generic soft-fp for 113-bit mantissas on a 32-bit core: 4-limb multiplies without Zbb clz normalisation and generic unpack/special paths
candidates.replacement: Same scheme as the shipped soft-double copy-patch: full-body signature match in libc/busybox and replace with Zbb-normalised, mulhu-ladder exact versions (fast path for normal finite operands, jump back to the original for specials)
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: 2-3x per helper; only matters if the fmt_fp/decfloat replacements are not done
candidates.exactness: bit-exact results and identical fflags under all rounding modes (same harness as v2's 50k-operand check)

candidates.name: __udivdi3/__umoddi3/__divdi3 using __clz_tab byte table instead of Zbb clz
candidates.where: libc.so __udivdi3@0x6733c (lbu from __clz_tab, no clz insn), called from __secs_to_tm (4), select, sysconf, fmt_fp, decfloat, lldiv; lvdesk (/usr/bin/lvdesk, lvdesk.syms @0xa65e2) with 31 call sites in main, 14 in kms_flush_cb, 7 xwin_on_draw, 6 draw_indic; also s31-bt, s31-a2dp, s31-tone
candidates.apps: lvdesk frame/profiling paths, localtime_r/strftime (tray clock), select() timeouts, SDL/X clients doing 64-bit time math
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 61 insns for a uint64/1e6 under QEMU; call rates unmeasured (lvdesk's are mostly LVPROF/report paths every 5 s)
candidates.pathology: libgcc built without assuming Zbb: count_leading_zeros is a table load chain; generic path even when the dividend high word is 0
candidates.replacement: Body-match and replace with: if (hi==0 && d<2^32) one divu/remu; else Zbb clz-normalised 2-by-1 division; divisor-constant cases unchanged semantics
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~1.5-3x per call; low absolute heat on the desktop
candidates.exactness: bit-exact quotient/remainder, same division-by-zero behaviour as libgcc (no trap on RISC-V: all-ones/ dividend)

candidates.name: musl localtime_r/__secs_to_tm/strftime
candidates.where: libc.so localtime_r@0x6000e (weak), __secs_to_tm (4 __udivdi3 calls), __secs_to_zone, strftime@0x60c6c
candidates.apps: lvdesk tray_clock_cb (localtime_r + strftime every 5 s tick), xclock/oclock per minute, busybox date, syslogd timestamps
candidates.heat: MEASURED: localtime_r 4,059 insns/call, strftime("%H:%M") 2,434 (QEMU). Rate is low (per 5 s)
candidates.pathology: 64-bit soft divisions by 86400/400-year cycles and a TZ re-check (getenv + compare, lock) on every call
candidates.replacement: Interpose localtime_r with a per-thread cache: if TZ string and zone file generation unchanged and the new time is within the cached day, derive h/m/s by 32-bit arithmetic from the cached midnight; else call musl
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~20x for same-day calls; negligible system-level gain
candidates.exactness: identical struct tm including tm_gmtoff/tm_zone/tm_isdst (cache must be invalidated at DST transitions: only reuse when no transition lies within the cached span)

candidates.name: snd_device_name_hint (SDL2 ALSA hotplug thread every 5 s)
candidates.where: libasound.so.2 (alsa-lib 1.2.15.3) snd_device_name_hint, called by SDL2 2.32.10 SDL_alsa_audio.c:972-985
candidates.apps: every SDL2 app (TyrQuake SDL2, OpenTyrian, Chocolate Doom); also any app listing ALSA devices
candidates.heat: MEASURED: one enumeration 1.83 s with stock alsa.conf, 0.35 s with the shipped lean alsa.conf; hotplug thread 42% of a core before, 11% after (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:976-992)
candidates.pathology: Each call re-walks the whole ALSA config tree and opens control devices through the XIP overlay (path_openat/link_path_walk/ovl_getattr in the kernel profile, _snd_config_search/snd_config_walk/printf_core in libasound)
candidates.replacement: Preload wrapper: cache the returned hint array keyed on /dev/snd directory mtime+inode set, /proc/asound/cards content, and alsa config file mtimes; return a deep copy (freed by the wrapped snd_device_name_free_hint); call through on any change
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED ceiling: ~11% of a core per SDL2 app -> ~0 (one stat set per 5 s)
candidates.exactness: identical hint strings/order while the device and config set is unchanged; invalidates on any card add/remove or config edit

candidates.name: dynamic exec: +38 ms per dynamically linked program
candidates.where: kernel exec path (load_elf_binary mapping PT_INTERP /lib/ld-musl-riscv32*.so.1 = libc.so through the overlayfs-over-cramfs stack) + page faults of the program's GOT/data; NOT ld.so's symbol work
candidates.apps: every X client launch (xcalc, xclock, xfiles, st), aplay/amixer, bluetoothctl, SDL games, s31-* dynamic tools
candidates.heat: MEASURED: spawnbench exec static 14 ms vs dynamic busybox 52 ms (current-state.md:4518-4531). MEASURED here: ld.so resolving a libc-only program is ~43k insns (QEMU hello-dyn 44,981 vs static 1,804), i.e. <0.3 ms, so the 38 ms is kernel-side. hot-text-plan.md:162-164: a spawn loop profiled link_path_walk, path_openat, dup_mmap, do_exit near the top
candidates.pathology: Kernel code for path walk, overlay lookups, mmap and faults runs XIP from 80 MHz flash (~6x slower than RAM) and is cold at each exec; the overlay stacks two cramfs + ext4 so each open walks three layers
candidates.replacement: Move the exec/path-walk/fault hot set (link_path_walk, path_openat, ovl_lookup/ovl_getattr, load_elf_binary, dup_mmap/exit_mmap, handle_mm_fault) into .text.fast; and/or point PT_INTERP (and the libc NEEDED path) at a non-overlay mount of the XIP cramfs so the interpreter open skips overlay walking
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: a large fraction of the 38 ms per dynamic exec; each extra DSO also pays it (s31fp 'loaded, off' +0-12.8 ms per launch, V2-REPORT.txt:318-326)
candidates.exactness: no semantic change (same files, same mappings); RAM cost of .text.fast must be weighed

candidates.name: s31fp constructor syscalls and scan at every launch
candidates.where: libs31fp.so constructor (rootfs/s31fp/v2/preload3.c; v3 s31str_init/s31clk init)
candidates.apps: every dynamically linked program started from a login shell or by lvdesk (LD_PRELOAD set in /etc/profile and lvdesk.c:15612)
candidates.heat: MEASURED (V2-REPORT.txt:318-326, board-b4, 20 launches each): library loaded but off +0 to +12.8 ms; scan +3.8 to +28 ms; cache hit +6 to +28 ms per launch. ~10 syscalls in the constructor
candidates.pathology: On this board the syscalls (auxv open/read/close, statx, cache open/read/close, 2 mprotect, fence.i) and the extra DSO mapping, not the scan, dominate
candidates.replacement: Use getauxval/dl_iterate_phdr instead of /proc/self/auxv (-3 syscalls), key the cache on an in-memory fingerprint verified by the body check instead of statx (-1), skip the cache file entirely for binaries whose first-halfword filter finds nothing in the first pages, and merge v2+v3 constructors into one
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED (V2-REPORT.txt:453-456): 'a further few ms off every launch'
candidates.exactness: no behavioural change; patch decisions identical

candidates.name: lvdesk app launch: fork of the desktop + 253 close() calls + sh -l -c
candidates.where: lvdesk.c:9880-9910 (fork, cg_join, close loop fd 3..255, execl("/bin/sh","-sh","-l","-c",cmd))
candidates.apps: every menu/app launch from the desktop
candidates.heat: MEASURED components: trivial syscall ~5 us (current-state.md:4357-4358) -> ~1.3 ms for 253 closes INFERRED; fork+exit 13 ms and static exec 14 ms (spawnbench) for a small process; lvdesk's own fork cost (large VMA set, SHM) unmeasured
candidates.pathology: One syscall per possible fd; a full fork of the biggest process on the board; an extra busybox exec plus /etc/profile sourcing before the real exec
candidates.replacement: close_range(3, ~0U, 0) via syscall(SYS_close_range) (kernel 7.1 has it); posix_spawn (musl uses CLONE_VM|CLONE_VFORK, no page-table copy) with file actions for the dup2/setsid; exec the target directly when cmd has no shell syntax, exporting what /etc/profile would
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~1 ms (close_range) + ~14 ms (skipped busybox exec) per launch; fork share unmeasured
candidates.exactness: same fds closed, same environment and session; behaviour identical for simple commands

candidates.name: busybox ash applet spawning (SH_STANDALONE/SH_NOFORK/PREFER_APPLETS off)
