candidates.where: busybox 1.38.0 config: buildroot cb857ba package/busybox/busybox.config has '# CONFIG_FEATURE_SH_STANDALONE is not set', '# CONFIG_FEATURE_SH_NOFORK is not set', '# CONFIG_FEATURE_PREFER_APPLETS is not set'; the project fragment (buildroot-external/board/esp32-s31/busybox.fragment) does not change them
candidates.apps: init scripts (cat/grep/cut/tr/wc/head/tail/date/awk/free/top in etc/init.d), s31-deskmon's $(awk ...) per sample, s31-play, s31-open, xfilesctl
candidates.heat: MEASURED: fork+exit 13 ms, static exec 14 ms, spawn 27-29 ms (current-state.md:4524-4533, 6136); boot forks 301 times
candidates.pathology: Every external applet in a script is fork+exec of the 1 MB static busybox even though the shell already contains the applet
candidates.replacement: Enable FEATURE_SH_STANDALONE + FEATURE_SH_NOFORK (+PREFER_APPLETS): NOFORK applets run in-process, NOEXEC applets fork without exec
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~14 ms per NOEXEC applet and ~27 ms per NOFORK applet invocation; boot-time savings proportional to the 301 forks
candidates.exactness: same applet code; differences only where scripts depend on /proc/self/exe or on a PATH override of an applet (must be audited)

candidates.name: musl dynamic linker symbol lookup (gnu_lookup_filtered/find_sym) for large DSO sets
candidates.where: libc.so (ld.so) find_sym -> gnu_lookup_filtered + strcmp, executed from XIP flash
candidates.apps: Qt apps from /opt/qt5 (dlopen of xcb plugin stack), any late dlopen (SDL2 dlopens libXrandr/libasound plugins)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 73-78% of Qt's ~20 s QApplication cold start sampled in gnu_lookup_filtered (current-state.md:2410-2420); dlopen of the xcb stack 4.79 s; desktop client chain dlopens in 10-20 ms (current-state.md:2355-2358)
candidates.pathology: Eager binding, one lookup per symbol per DSO, loop and hash tables fetched cold from 80 MHz flash
candidates.replacement: For dlopen phases (after the preload constructor runs), copy gnu_lookup_filtered/find_sym into RAM (body match in libc.so, same as v2 copies) or interpose dlopen with a per-process (name,hash)->(dso,sym) memo consulted before the chain walk
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: meaningful only for Qt-class apps (tens of thousands of relocations); ~0 for the stock desktop
candidates.exactness: identical symbol resolution order and results (memo keyed by the full lookup context incl. DSO scope)

candidates.name: libsbc 2.1 SBC analysis filter (Generic C primitives)
candidates.where: libsbc.so.1 (Buildroot SBC_VERSION 2.1) sbc_primitives.c: sbc_analyze_4b_8s_simd / sbc_analyze_eight_simd (int16xint16->int32 MAC), selected by function pointer in sbc_init_primitives (sbc_primitives.c:598-640; no RISC-V backend)
candidates.apps: s31-a2dp (Bluetooth A2DP source)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: A2DP playback ~30% of a core, s31-a2dp 20.4% of which the codec ~6-9% (current-state.md:4882-4897); sbcbench 0.23 ms/frame codec alone (current-state.md:4746-4750)
candidates.pathology: Scalar 16-bit MACs on a core with an 8-lane PIE MAC unit that libsbc cannot use
candidates.replacement: Replace the analyze primitive with a PIE esp.vmulas.s16.qacc version (CPU0 only, rseq-dispatched to the scalar C elsewhere), installed by body-matching the static function in libsbc or by overwriting the encoder-state function pointer after sbc_init_a2dp (s31-a2dp is ours)
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: analysis filter several x faster; up to the 6-9% codec share of a core during playback
candidates.exactness: integer bit-exact (same products and int32 sums, same shifts/rounding constant)

candidates.name: LVGL builtin lv_memcpy (misaligned path is byte-by-byte)
candidates.where: /usr/bin/lvdesk: lv_memcpy@0x9e548 -> lv_memcpy.part.0@0x9e338 (32x unrolled lbu/sb when src/dst alignment differ); 105 call sites; lv_conf.h:46 LV_USE_STDLIB_STRING = LV_STDLIB_BUILTIN
candidates.apps: lvdesk (LVGL draw buffers, label/text, image copies)
candidates.heat: MEASURED ambiguous: perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:922 'lvdesk's own code at 6% (2.9% lvdesk + 3.3% its memcpy)' of hart-1 samples during a game; the split between lv_memcpy and libc memcpy is not recorded
candidates.pathology: Mis-co-aligned copies move one byte per load/store pair; LVGL's copy bypasses both the XEspV libc path and lvdesk's own lentcpu.c dispatch
candidates.replacement: Build lvdesk with LV_STDLIB_CLIB for string ops so lv_memcpy goes to lentcpu.c's rseq-dispatched memcpy, or give lv_memcpy a word-load + shift/merge misaligned loop
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: up to ~4x on misaligned copies; bounded by the ~3.3% share
candidates.exactness: identical bytes copied

candidates.name: LVGL 1bpp glyph draw path (terminal/unscii_8)
candidates.where: lvdesk: lv_font_get_glyph_dsc_fmt_txt@0x4d448, lv_font_get_bitmap_fmt_txt@0x4d104, lv_draw_sw_blend@0x91c74 -> lv_draw_sw_blend_color_to_rgb565@0x87ea6 with an A8 mask per glyph
candidates.apps: lvdesk terminal and every LVGL label
candidates.heat: MEASURED: terminal redraw LVGL rasteriser 47.3 ms/frame = 68% (accel-plan.md:181); per-glyph attribution explicitly NOT established (accel-plan.md:285-296)
candidates.pathology: Each 8x8 1bpp glyph is unpacked to an A8 mask and blended per pixel through the generic masked blend, instead of a 1-bit expand-and-store
candidates.replacement: A dedicated 1bpp->RGB565 glyph blitter hooked as a draw-unit/letter callback (Zbb-assisted bit expand via a 16-entry nibble->2-pixel table), falling back to LVGL for AA fonts
candidates.est_gain: unmeasured until per-render vs per-line terms are separated (accel-plan's own prerequisite)
candidates.exactness: pixel-identical output for 1bpp fonts (opa 0/255 only)

candidates.name: lvdesk palette expansion (8->16 bpp LUT)
candidates.where: lvdesk.c ~4256 (perf-ideas-sweep.md:26); xshim ShmPutImage depth-8 path
candidates.apps: 8-bit clients through lvdesk (prboom-class, XShm 8bpp)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 3.75 ms/frame at 320x200, 13.9 ms at 640x480, ~51 MB/s vs 160 MB/s for the copy+hash loop in the same frame (perf-ideas-sweep.md:20-30, big-ideas.md:14-19)
candidates.pathology: Serial lbu->sh1add->lhu->sh dependent chain, not bandwidth-bound
candidates.replacement: Word-source loads (one lw -> four independent LUT lookups), unroll, two pre-shifted 32-bit palettes to pack pixel pairs; Zba sh1add already used
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED (sweep doc): up to ~3x on the expansion if it is latency-bound as argued; unverified
candidates.exactness: pixel-identical

candidates.name: musl strlen/strchr/strchrnul/strcpy/stpcpy/strncmp without Zbb orc.b
candidates.where: libc.so strlen (26-line word-at-a-time C, no orc.b/ctz), strchr, strchrnul, strcpy, stpcpy, strncmp, strcasecmp - none in the XEspV set and none exported by s31str (it covers strnlen/strrchr/strstr/strcmp/mem*)
candidates.apps: bluetoothd/glib (UUID/address parsing), dbus, X clients, xshim, libasound config walk
candidates.heat: MEASURED instruction counts (QEMU, build/cloud/probes/wide-desktop/slen.c): strlen 12 B 47 vs 37, 40 B 89 vs 65, 200 B 329 vs 225 insns (musl vs orc.b+ctz). System share unmeasured except the pathological bluetoothd case (79% in strlen, current-state.md:6313)
candidates.pathology: Carry-chain word test (sub/andn/and per word) where Zbb gives orc.b + ctz
candidates.replacement: Add Zbb orc.b/ctz versions of strlen, strchr, strchrnul, stpcpy/strcpy, strncmp to s31str's exported set (scalar, CPU-agnostic, no PIE needed)
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED ratio 1.27-1.46x fewer instructions per call
candidates.exactness: identical return values; aligned word reads never cross a page

candidates.name: kernel string/hash helpers built without Zbb under XIP_KERNEL
candidates.where: kernel lib string routines (strlen/strcmp/strncmp) and path hashing used by link_path_walk; big-ideas.md: 'Kernel Zbb is compiled out by XIP_KERNEL'
candidates.apps: every open/exec/stat (path walk), ALSA enumeration, udev
candidates.heat: MEASURED qualitatively: link_path_walk/path_openat/ovl_getattr prominent in the ALSA-enumeration kernel profile (perf-plan:978-981) and the spawn-loop profile (hot-text-plan.md:162-164); no percentage recorded
candidates.pathology: RISC-V Zbb string variants are chosen by ALTERNATIVE patching, which an XIP kernel cannot do, so the generic byte/word C versions run - from flash
candidates.replacement: Compile the Zbb variants unconditionally (the S31 always has Zbb) and place them in .text.fast
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~1.3-1.5x on those routines (same ratio as the userspace strlen count); small overall
candidates.exactness: identical results

candidates.name: esp32s31-crypto driver self-test polling at boot
candidates.where: drivers/crypto/esp32s31-crypto.c polls RSA_QUERY_IDLE and ECC_INT_RAW for 2,000,000 us each (current-state.md:5015-5020)
candidates.apps: boot (everything behind it)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: ~6.2 s of a 26 s boot; nothing in userspace uses kernel crypto offload (wpa_supplicant has its own, BlueZ uses software AES). Current status not re-verified here
candidates.pathology: The blocks never answer (clock/power gate), so the probe waits out two 2 s timeouts
candidates.replacement: Disable CONFIG_CRYPTO_DEV_ESP32S31 or fix the gate; if kept, probe asynchronously
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED: ~6.2 s of boot
candidates.exactness: no userspace-visible change (no consumer)

candidates.name: wpa_supplicant PBKDF2-SHA1 / internal crypto
candidates.where: /usr/sbin/wpa_supplicant 2.11 (BR2_PACKAGE_WPA_SUPPLICANT_PASSPHRASE=y; no OpenSSL in the defconfig, so INFERRED internal crypto: sha1_vector/hmac_sha1/pbkdf2_sha1)
candidates.apps: Wi-Fi bring-up (S40network), reconnects
candidates.heat: MEASURED end-to-end only: wpa_supplicant start 2.1-2.4 s, association 5.6 s (current-state.md:3630-3645); crypto share unmeasured; whether the card config uses a passphrase (PBKDF2 each start) or hex psk is unknown
candidates.pathology: A passphrase costs 2x4096 HMAC-SHA1 iterations of generic C at every start
candidates.replacement: Copy-patch the SHA-1 compression function to a Zbb-rotate/unrolled version or the SoC SHA accelerator (if present and reachable from Linux); or precompute the PSK in the card config
candidates.est_gain: unmeasured (INFERRED tens to hundreds of ms per start at most)
candidates.exactness: bit-identical digests

candidates.name: musl mallocng for X-client start-up
candidates.where: libc.so malloc/free/realloc/calloc (musl 1.2 mallocng)
candidates.apps: Xt/Xaw clients (xfiles, xcalc), SDL init, glib in bluetoothd, xshim
candidates.heat: MEASURED indirectly: xfiles launch 5.0 s of which 2.1 s is the client's own CPU (current-state.md:4577); allocator share unmeasured (rootfs/mallocprof.c exists to measure it)
candidates.pathology: mallocng trades speed for compactness (out-of-band metadata, group allocation, eager madvise/munmap syscalls on free)
candidates.replacement: Measure with mallocprof first; if hot, interpose a size-class allocator with in-band headers for small sizes while keeping musl for large blocks
candidates.est_gain: unmeasured
candidates.exactness: API-exact only (addresses differ); RAM footprint must not grow on a 15.4 MB board

result.coverage_notes:
What I searched: docs/current-state.md (spawn cost, launch timings, Qt loader, bluetoothd spin, A2DP, boot breakdown, PIE hook), perf-plan-2026-09-23.md (lvdesk/SDL2/ALSA hotplug profiles), perf-review-2026-09-23.md, perf-ideas-sweep.md, big-ideas.md, accel-plan.md (LVGL rasteriser and poll-loop costs), hot-text-plan.md, gl-plan-2026-09-25.md (PIE-bounce root cause), xespv-libc.md, x11-review.md, xftlite/xlite docs, status-and-todo-2026-09-27.md, rootfs/s31fp/v2/V2-REPORT.txt (constructor launch cost), rootfs/s31fp/v3 (what s31str/s31clk export already).

Binaries disassembled: the toolchain libc.so (soft-quad call sites, float-libm callee lists, __udivdi3 with __clz_tab, str* without orc.b; NOT byte-identical to the board's libc 352e9417, so every libc address and body above is a caveat until checked against the board copy); overlay /usr/bin/lvdesk plus lvdesk/lvdesk.syms (imports, __udivdi3 call sites, lv_memcpy/lv_memset bodies); overlay /usr/lib X libraries (all are slim stubs: libfreetype 4.7 KB, libfontconfig 9.4 KB, so freetype glyph loading and fontconfig cache parsing are NOT desktop costs here, only for Qt in /opt/qt5); s31-bt, s31-a2dp, s31-tone (local libgcc helpers).

Measured here under QEMU, instruction counts only, no timing, with the QEMU-sysroot upstream musl 1.2.5 (build/cloud/probes/wide-desktop/lcbench.c, lcbench-icount.txt, slen.c, hello-dyn/hello-st, calls.sh). Fetched: buildroot cb857ba busybox.config (SH_STANDALONE/NOFORK off) and package versions, and sbc-2.1 source; its primitives compile with no soft-double calls (fabs folded).

Not reached: the board's libc and busybox binaries (the busybox under build/cloud/probes/ram-userspace is another agent's QEMU build); the real xfiles, xcalc, st, Xt and Xaw binaries; bluetoothd, dbus-daemon, wpa_supplicant, libasound, libsbc, SDL2 and mpg123 binaries (not in the repo); the kernel tree (linux-71-port is not checked out here), so the kernel items rest on the docs; and the wpa_supplicant.conf on the card. mpg123's decoder choice depends on how BR2_SOFT_FLOAT resolves for rv32 ilp32 with F, so I did not list it.

Considered and left out as too small: xshim atom lookup (linear strcmp over 256 atoms, only at connect time); FNV row_hash (the copy it runs inside is memory-bound at 160 MB/s); lvdesk sscanf/fscanf/snprintf of /proc every 5 s; qsort (44.8k insns for 64 ints under QEMU, but no hot desktop caller found).

Some items are already measured or proposed elsewhere and are listed for completeness: palette expansion (perf-ideas-sweep), the crypto self-test (current-state.md:5015-5020, may already be fixed), and the SDL2 hotplug relief, where the lean alsa.conf already shipped and the interposition would go beyond it.

Mechanism caveats:
- musl has no /etc/ld.so.preload, so daemons get s31fp only through the environment.
- Static busybox cannot be reached by any preload.
- ld.so's own lookups run before any preload constructor, so a copy-patch of the loader only helps dlopen phases.

Excluded per instructions: soft-double helpers, OPL, fused soft-double chains, floor/ceil/trunc, and s31fp copy placement. The float-libm entry's fallback path touches the fused-chain exclusion, and that entry says so.

candidates.name: alsa-lib linear rate converter (linear_expand_s16 / generic linear_expand)
candidates.where: libasound.so.2 built-in pcm_rate_linear.c, chosen by overlay/etc/asound.conf `defaults.pcm.rate_converter "linear"`; the rate plugin sits inside s31route's `plug:'hw:0,0'` sink (rootfs/audiofp/s31route-proto.c:160)
candidates.apps: prboom (22050 -> 44100, current-state.md:7902-7912), sdlquake/tiopex at 11025/22050, any SDL1/SDL2 app not at 44.1/48 kHz (36 kHz, 32 kHz). Called once per audio period on the audio thread, 2 channels per call.
candidates.heat: MEASURED: about 1.85 us, or about 590 cycles, per output frame, about 8% of a core at 44.1 kHz (artifacts/audio/first-principles-2026-09-27/REPORT.md:85-86). Doom: '~8-10% the 22050->44100 linear resampler and its copies', worth ~1.5-2 fps (current-state.md:7937-7940). The ptrace PC sample had ~10% of the audio thread in 'linear resampler + copies' (current-state.md:7900-7902). MEASURED in QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-framepath/lin/): the inner loop alone is 17-18 instructions per sample, so most of the 590 cycles is divide latency, strided PSRAM access and plug copies (INFERRED).
candidates.pathology: Each output sample on each channel does an integer divu: `new_weight = (pos<<(16-shift))/(get_threshold>>shift)`. The divide latency on the S31 is unmeasured. The loop makes one strided pass per channel over interleaved PSRAM data, so it touches each cache line twice. If plug negotiates any format other than S16 on both sides, it falls to the generic `linear_expand`, which does two computed-goto conversions per sample. It is also chained behind plug's intermediate buffers.
candidates.replacement: Our own ALSA rate module (libasound_module_rate_s31lin.so), selected with `defaults.pcm.rate_converter "s31lin"` in our own asound.conf. It does not patch alsa-lib. It is an exact twin of linear, with `input_frames`/`output_frames`/`muldiv_near`/`adjust_pitch` copied verbatim. Hot loop: (a) when d = G>>shift is a power of two, a shift, since d = 32768 for 22050->44100 and 11025->44100; (b) otherwise q = mulhu(n, 0xFFFFFFFF/d), then `while (n-q*d >= d) q++`. Both channels are processed in one interleaved pass. There is a CPU0 PIE variant for the weighting MACs.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: removing the per-sample divu and the second strided pass is likely 1/4-1/2 of the ~8% of a core, i.e. +2-4% of CPU0 during sounded Doom/Quake at 22.05/11.025 kHz. That is roughly +0.5-1 fps of 23. It needs a board A/B.
candidates.exactness: Output PCM must be bit-identical to built-in linear, including old_sample carry across periods, pitch adjustment and frame accounting. QEMU probe: the pow2 path and the reciprocal-plus-correction path gave 0 mismatches against the original loop for 22050/11025/32000/8000->44100 and 22050/36000/44100->48000, over 20 periods of random stereo data (lin3.c). The reciprocal path is exact by construction: q_est <= floor(n/d), then it is corrected upward.

candidates.name: alsa-lib route plugin mono->stereo (snd_pcm_route_convert1_one) plus the plug/ioplug area copies
candidates.where: libasound.so.2 pcm_route.c / pcm_plugin areas copy (snd_pcm_areas_copy, snd_pcm_area_copy per-sample loops) inserted by plug below s31route; ioplug transfer in s31route
candidates.apps: OpenTyrian (asks for 44100 mono S16, 2048-frame periods: REPORT.md:111-117), any mono SDL app. The copies apply to every sounded app, once per period.
candidates.heat: MEASURED: routing mono to stereo adds ~0.34 us, or ~110 cycles, per output frame (REPORT.md:84). The 44100-mono route-only arm cost 4.8% of a core, against 3.2-3.6% for stereo direct (REPORT.md:76-77). The copies are part of the '~10% linear resampler + copies' (current-state.md:7902).
candidates.pathology: Generic per-sample route conversion through a ttable with computed-goto get/put, one channel at a time. Then plug and ioplug stage the data through intermediate buffers, adding extra PSRAM passes at the ~13.6 MB/s copy ceiling.
candidates.replacement: First-party s31route: open the sink as stereo and duplicate L=R itself in the pass that already moves the samples. Better, write straight into the sink with snd_pcm_mmap_begin/commit, so neither the route plugin nor ioplug's staging copy is instantiated. Combine this with the s31lin rate module above.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~1.2-1.5% of a core for Tyrian (110 cycles x 44100/s = 4.9 Mcycles/s at 320 MHz). The copy removal is unmeasured, a share of the Doom 8-10%.
candidates.exactness: Identical samples: duplicated channels and byte-identical copies. The same period/avail/xrun semantics as today's plug chain (the rounding-bug fix still applies).

candidates.name: musl float libm evaluated in soft double: sinf / cosf / sincosf / tanf / expf / exp2f / logf / log2f (and powf)
candidates.where: libc.so (musl 1.2.5 libm). Disassembly of the toolchain libc: sinf, cosf and sincosf call __sindf/__cosdf/__rem_pio2f/__adddf3/__subdf3/__extendsfdf2; expf, logf and powf call __muldf3 x6-14 (build/cloud/probes/wide-framepath/libc.dis). These are libc's OWN internal soft-double copies, which s31fp's main-executable copy-patch never reaches.
candidates.apps: tiopex/sdlquake sincosf: 11 static sites. AngleVectors does 3 sincosf per call, from R_SetupFrame, V_CalcRefdef, V_CalcRoll, R_AliasSetUpTransform (x2 per alias entity), R_DrawSprite (per sprite), CL_RelinkEntities, and R_RotateBmodel (3 per rotating bmodel). INFERRED ~15-25 AngleVectors, i.e. ~45-75 sincosf, per frame. Also OpenTyrian (imports sincosf), lvdesk/xshim (sinf/cosf/expf in click-sound generation lvdesk.c:3150-3159, cosf+sinf per point in draw_arc xshim.c:2252-2253), SDL2, and any audio app calling sinf per sample.
candidates.heat: MEASURED on the board: one sinf ~9 us, ~3000 cycles; sinf once per sample cost 40-50% of a core at 48 kHz (REPORT.md:100-104). MEASURED in the X11 TyrQuake profile: 'libc 5% (memcpy 0.9, the rest in the float-math region)' (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:897). MEASURED in QEMU (instructions per call, net of loop, build/cloud/probes/wide-framepath/lm/icount.txt, upstream musl 1.2.5): sinf ~2046, cosf ~2055, sincosf ~4000, tanf ~2800, expf ~1830, logf ~1820, powf ~4120. log10f (~89) and atan2f (~111) are already float-only.
candidates.pathology: The float API computes its polynomials in double on a core with no D. Every multiply and add is a ~100-instruction soft-double call into libc-internal helpers, and the S31's real single-precision FPU (fmadd.s) goes unused.
candidates.replacement: Interposed float-native versions in s31fp. Evaluate musl's own sindf/cosdf/exp2f/log2f polynomials in double-float (float pairs with fmadd.s error-free products), with Cody-Waite pi/2 reduction in float-float, and delegate large |x| (the __rem_pio2_large path), specials and subnormals to libc via RTLD_NEXT. Detect results that land within the float-float error bound of a float rounding boundary and delegate those to libc too. Fast path only when frm == RNE.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~2000 -> ~60-150 instructions per call (15-30x). For tiopex, ~0.8-1% of CPU0 per frame from sincosf. The measured 'float-math region' of ~4% in TyrQuake X11 is the ceiling there. Large for any per-sample synth using sinf. lvdesk arcs and click generation become cheap.
candidates.exactness: Result bits must equal musl for every input. For single-argument float functions this is EXHAUSTIVELY checkable: all 2^32 inputs, host-side, against the board libc image. fflags must match too: the inexact behaviour of the delegated cases is preserved because libc computes them. Every other case must raise NX exactly when musl does, and musl raises it for all non-exact results. powf (2^64 domain) cannot be exhaustively verified: keep it out, or delegate unless both args are in verified sub-domains. Overlaps roadmap A5 (deferred) and W7; this census adds the per-frame callers.

candidates.name: musl double libm sin / cos / sincos / tan / atan2 / pow / atan (libc-internal soft double)
candidates.where: libc.so (musl), called via PLT from app executables
candidates.apps: tiopex per frame (static sites in tiopex.dis): sin x3 in V_AddIdle, x3 in CalcGunAngle, x1 in V_CalcBob; tan in SCR_UpdateScreen/R_ViewChanged; atanf in SCR_UpdateScreen; atan2 per beam in CL_UpdateTEnts; sqrt in V_CalcBob/R_ViewChanged. prboom-plus: 2 sin + 2 cos in R_BuildModelViewMatrix (r_main.c:702-705), INFERRED once per frame from R_SetupFrame. QuakeSpasm and SDL2 import sincos/sqrt/atan2.

INFERRED per frame: tiopex ~7 sin + 2 tan + 2 sqrt, about 38k instructions per frame, ~0.1-0.2% of CPU0 at 12-15 fps. prboom ~15k instructions per frame, ~0.2% at 47 fps.

candidates.replacement: Roadmap W7: rebuild musl __sin/__cos/__rem_pio2/sin/cos/sincos bound to s31fp's fast exact helpers, and delegate non-RNE and large |x| to libc. candidates.est_gain: INFERRED, small: <=0.2% CPU0 per app per frame. It is listed so the census is complete, not as a lead.
candidates.exactness: Result bits and fflags under all 5 rounding modes, the same as W7's 0/500k oracle. It must be re-run against board libc 352e9417.

candidates.name: OpenTyrian 8->16 palette-expansion scaler (nn_16) every frame
candidates.where: opentyrian executable, video_scale.c scaler16, reached because video.c:74-80 walks bpp from 32 down and SDL_VideoModeOK(32) returns 16 on the default visual. It therefore never asks for the depth-8 PseudoColor visual that xshim already serves.
candidates.apps: OpenTyrian: one full 320x200 LUT pass per presented frame, then SDL_Flip. The same idiom exists in stock TyrQuake-X11 VID_ResolveFramebuffer.
candidates.heat: MEASURED for the analogous loop: TyrQuake-X11's 8->16 LUT pass was 3.6% of the game's samples (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:894-895). Tyrian's own loop is unmeasured. INFERRED ~64,000 pixels x 5-6 instructions per frame, ~3-4% of a core at Tyrian's frame rate.
candidates.pathology: A scalar byte-load, LUT-load, halfword-store loop over PSRAM. Separately, xshim/lvdesk then copies and row-hashes the 128 KB result, where an 8-bit client would be zero-copy with the expand done once by lvdesk's direct-expand path (frame-path-plan.md:98-110).
candidates.replacement: (a) Copy-patch an app-body signature for nn_16: index-quad loads, Zba sh1add LUT addressing, 2-pixel packed stores, on CPU0 a PIE store path. This needs an owner ruling, because it is app-specific. (b) Better, but steering: interpose SDL_VideoModeOK so a SWSURFACE|HWPALETTE request is answered with 8, so Tyrian selects scaler8 and the client goes zero-copy. That is a behaviour change and is subject to the no-steering rule.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED +2-4% CPU0 for (a). (b) removes the pass and one 128 KB copy entirely.
candidates.exactness: (a) identical RGB565 output bytes. (b) the displayed pixels must be identical after lvdesk's expand, and the palette update ordering must be preserved.

candidates.name: xshim/lvdesk row_hash (32-bit FNV-1a) in the MIT-SHM copy-and-hash loop
candidates.where: lvdesk/xshim.c:329-345 (row_hash) and the fused copy+hash loop in mitshm_request (xshim.c:6408 ff.)
candidates.apps: Every SHM client present: prboom (5,032 ShmPutImage in one timedemo, xshim.c:6126), Tyrian, tiopex windowed, SDL2 clients. One call per client frame, 200-240 rows.
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 11.7% of lvdesk's on-CPU samples fell on the page holding this loop during a prboom timedemo (xshim.c:6122-6126). lvdesk takes ~25-37% of a core during games (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:1000-1003; current-state.md:8462).
candidates.pathology: `h = (h ^ w) * p` is a serial multiply dependency chain, one mul latency per word. Whether PSRAM load latency hides it is unmeasured; the code comment assumes the ALU is free.
candidates.replacement: Keep the fused copy but break the chain: 4 independent FNV lanes combined at row end, or a Zbc clmul-folded CRC-32 (Zbc is present), or on CPU0 a PIE path (vector load/store plus lane XOR/multiply). The hash is private to xshim, so any collision-equivalent function is fine.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED 0-2% of a core, depending on whether mul latency is exposed. It needs an A/B with XSHIM_NOROWDMG as the reference arm (current-state/perf-plan: 10.9 vs 12.4 fps shows the hash itself is a win).
candidates.exactness: Internal only: every row changed by a writer must still be detected (wrgen/hole logic unchanged). The collision rate must stay <= 2^-32 per row.

candidates.where: lvdesk, built with LV_USE_STDLIB_STRING = LV_STDLIB_BUILTIN (lvdesk/lv_conf.h:46). nm: lv_memcpy.part.0 0x210 B, lv_memset 0x76 B (artifacts/gl/glquake/nm/lvdesk.nm)

Kernel profile of windowed Doom: snd_pcm_stream_lock_irq 3.6%, ioctl entry 2.5% and snd_pcm_sync_ptr 1.7% of kernel ticks, with kernel mode ~10% of wall (frame-path-plan.md:128-135). candidates.name: Mix_DoEffects + _Eff_position_s16lsb (SDL2_mixer 2.6.3 per-channel panning effect)
candidates.where: libSDL2_mixer-2.0.so: src/mixer.c:296 Mix_DoEffects (static, called from mix_channels at mixer.c:384/411) and src/effect_position.c:766 _Eff_position_s16lsb (static; installed by the exported Mix_SetPanning)
candidates.apps: chocolate-doom 3.1.1 (the only SDL2_mixer client; i_sdlsound.c:897 calls Mix_SetPanning for every sound it starts and updates), any other SDL2_mixer app that pans or positions channels
candidates.heat: unmeasured on the board. Chocolate-doom audio has never been profiled by function, and its sound path was not verified in-game (current-state.md:390-438). QEMU MEASURED on the effect body rebuilt standalone at -Os with s31-cc: 20 instructions per stereo frame per channel (2,062,740 instructions for 100 calls of 1,024 frames, minus a 12,575-instruction baseline). Its inner loop is 2x fcvt.s.w, 4x fmul.s, 2x fcvt.w.s rtz and 2x lh/sh. INFERRED: slice = 1,024 frames at snd_samplerate 48000 (chocolate-fullscreen.cfg), about 47 callbacks/s, so about 1 M instructions/s per active channel for the effect alone, before malloc, memcpy and free. With NUM_CHANNELS=8 at full load, about 8 M instructions/s.
candidates.pathology: Every panned channel, on every audio callback, pays SDL_malloc(len) + SDL_memcpy(len) of the chunk slice (4 KB in PSRAM, at the ~13.6 MB/s copy ceiling class) + a separate float pass writing it back + SDL_free, and only then SDL_MixAudioFormat reads it again. Three passes over PSRAM plus mallocng churn happen on the audio thread per channel. Chocolate-doom never has left=right=255, so the effect is always installed while a sound plays. The float math is hardware (F), so the cost is the extra passes and the allocator, not soft float.
candidates.replacement: Copy-patch the static Mix_DoEffects/mix_channels pair, found by full-body signature in libSDL2_mixer. Use a fused per-channel path: when the channel's only registered effect is _Eff_position_s16lsb and the mixer format is S16 stereo, compute swapl/swapr with the same float ops (same (float)x*left_f then *dist_f order, then fcvt rtz) and feed each Sint16 straight into the S16 mix formula SDL_MixAudioFormat uses (same volume scaling and clamp) into stream. That removes the malloc, the memcpy, the intermediate store and the free. Fall back to the stock path for any other effect chain.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: removes about 3 of 4 PSRAM passes per panned channel plus a malloc/free pair per channel per callback. The float work (about 20 instructions/frame) stays. Likely 30-50% of per-channel mixer cost on the SDL2_mixer audio thread. Not measured on the board, and chocolate-doom's audio share of CPU is unknown.
candidates.exactness: Bit-exact if the fused path keeps the effect's float op order and rounding mode (fmul.s x2 then fcvt.w.s rtz to Sint16 with the same (Sint16) wrap) and the identical SDL_MixAudioFormat S16 arithmetic and clamp. The opp (room_angle==180) swap must be honoured. Output must equal the stock stream byte for byte; verify with QEMU against the stock pair over random chunks, pan values and volumes.

candidates.name: timidity update_signal/update_tremolo and recompute_amp in soft binary128 + SDL_sin (SDL2_mixer built-in timidity)
candidates.where: libSDL2_mixer-2.0.so: src/codecs/timidity/mix.c:148 update_tremolo (inlined into update_signal) and playmidi.c:178-213 recompute_amp. TIM_FSCALENEG at options.h:91 is (1.0L / (double)(1<<b)): long double = binary128 on RV32. Measured on an s31-cc -Os rebuild: update_signal calls SDL_sin, __adddf3, 2x __muldf3, __extenddftf2 and __multf3. recompute_amp calls 2x __extenddftf2/__multf3 plus __extendsfdf2/__muldf3. update_vibrato makes 8 __muldf3 + 2 __divdf3 + SDL_sin calls on a cache miss.
candidates.apps: any SDL2_mixer client that plays MIDI through Mix_LoadMUS (timidity is enabled by SDL2_mixer's default configure and not disabled by Buildroot's sdl2_mixer.mk)
candidates.heat: 0 as currently configured, MEASURED from config. Chocolate-doom has snd_musicdevice 0 (overlay/etc/lvdesk/chocolate-fullscreen.cfg). No timidity.cfg or GUS patch package (freepats) is in esp32s31_rootfs_defconfig, so timidity cannot initialise. The per-voice rate would be CONTROLS_PER_SECOND=1000 x active tremolo voices, each doing SDL_sin in soft double plus a soft-quad multiply.
candidates.pathology: The tremolo is recomputed per voice every control tick (1 ms) through a double sin() and a binary128 multiply, which is the soft-quad path the S31 has no hardware for. Note-on and expression changes also go through binary128 in recompute_amp.
candidates.replacement: Copy-patch update_signal and recompute_amp with versions that compute TIM_FSCALENEG(x,b) as the exact double product x * 0x1p-b (a power-of-two scale is exact in any binary format, so the long-double detour is value-identical). Use one __muldf3/ldexp instead of __extenddftf2+__multf3+__trunctfdf2.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: per call removes the binary128 conversion and multiply (hundreds of instructions of soft quad). Zero system-level gain until someone ships MIDI patches or enables music.
candidates.exactness: The power-of-two scale is exact in binary128 and in double unless it overflows or underflows, which the magnitudes here (|x| < 2^31, b <= 17) cannot. The sin() argument and the double chain must stay unchanged, so results are bit-identical.

result.coverage_notes:
MPG123 (the main target), all under QEMU, instruction counts only. Scratch: /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-audiodec/ (allbb.so is a per-TB exec-count plugin written for this; attr.py maps counts to symbols).

(1) Which decoder the board uses. Buildroot cb857ba4 package/mpg123/mpg123.mk:23 sets MPG123_CPU = $(if $(BR2_SOFT_FLOAT),generic_nofpu,generic_fpu). On riscv nothing selects BR2_SOFT_FLOAT: arch/Config.in.riscv never references it, and only the ARM, MIPS and m68k-cf options select it. So the board gets --with-cpu=generic_fpu, which configure.ac:1663 turns into -DOPT_GENERIC -DREAL_IS_FLOAT. The decoder is float; nothing in the synth or DCT is fixed point or double. The defaults also give ACCURATE_ROUNDING and IEEE_FLOAT, so REAL_TO_SHORT is ftoi16(), a float magic-number add (sample.h:40-50). The double-literal compare in WRITE_SHORT_SAMPLE compiles to fle.s, so no soft double.

(2) Which encoding it writes. mpg123 picks S16 first (format.c:40, enc_16bit_range), so synth_1to1 runs, not the synth_s32 that does contain soft double. s31route passes 44.1 kHz through natively (s31route.c:380), so there is no alsa-lib rate converter behind mpg123.

(3) Soft double and __divdi3 exposure, MEASURED. The test vector is a synthetic 10 s, 44.1 kHz stereo 128 kbps MP3 made with lameenc; the output is 884,736 s16 samples. The -O2 build decodes it in 107.7 M instructions:
- synth_1to1 50.7%
- III_dequantize_sample 14.7%
- dct64 14.7%
- dct36 11.7%
- do_layer3 4.6%

All soft-double helpers together are about 0.6% of instructions and nearly all of it is one-time table init (gainpow2 exp2, make_decode_tables). A 1 s file already carries 0.73 M of the 0.92 M. The steady-state per-frame residue is __divdf3 and __floatdidf from the position and time bookkeeping, about 0.1%. __divdi3, __udivdi3 and __moddi3 execute 0 times. dct64 and synth_1to1 contain 0 soft-double calls (nm -u per object). So mpg123 has no double or int64-division target.

(4) A candidate refuted before submission. With my configure, Buildroot-style -Os after mpg123's own "-O2 -funroll-all-loops -ffast-math" wins. That leaves dct64 as loops: 41.2 M vs 16.3 M instructions per 10 s. An exact replacement compiled -O2 -ffp-contract=off was bit-identical on two vectors, and together with layer3.o at -O2 it gave -23.5% (141.7 M -> 108.4 M). Plain -O2 -ffast-math dct64 is NOT exact: 101 of 884,736 samples differ by 1 LSB. However, the board's libmpg123 function sizes (rootfs/s31fp/mpg.nm) match my -O2 build, not -Os:
- dct64 1830 vs 1790 (-Os 1128)
- III_dequantize_sample 5654 vs 5534 (-Os 2926)
- do_layer3 14696 vs 14136 (-Os 5250)
So the board already runs the unrolled -O2 code and this is not a board opportunity. The board's function sizes are the evidence.

(5) What is left in mpg123 is FPU-throughput bound. synth_1to1 at -O2 runs about 62 instructions per output sample: 32 flw for 16 fmadd in two chains that fast-math already split. There is no float SIMD in PIE, and any reassociation breaks exactness. Consistent with the board's record: docs/worklog-2026-09-19.md:532-535 has s31fp giving NO CHANGE on mpg123 -t, with synth_1to1 38% and dct36 12% of the board profile.

SDL2_MIXER 2.6.3 as Buildroot builds it (sdl2_mixer.mk):
- MP3 is off (--disable-music-mp3, so no dr_mp3/minimp3).
- FLAC is off (no BR2_PACKAGE_FLAC, so no dr_flac).
- fluidsynth, modplug, opus and tremor are off. xmp is off by its own default.
- Left on: WAV, stb_vorbis (float) and built-in timidity, which carries the soft-quad finding above with zero heat.
- Native MIDI does not apply on Linux.

CHOCOLATE-DOOM 3.1.1, source fetched via raw.githubusercontent:
- As configured it plays no music (snd_musicdevice 0), so no OPL and no music decoder.
- SFX go through SDL2_mixer at 48 kHz S16 stereo (use_libsamplerate 0).
- ExpandSoundData_SDL (i_sdlsound.c:604-714) does its 11025->48000 conversion and low-pass filter in float with f-suffixed constants, so it runs in hardware. It runs once per cached sound, with one uint64 __udivdi3 per sound. Not hot.
- PitchShift uses float division per sample, but only when pitch shifting is on.
- The runtime cost lives in SDL2_mixer's per-channel effect path, the first candidate; SDL_MixAudioFormat itself was already on the found list.

APLAY and alsa-lib: aplay does no per-sample work unless -V (vumeter) is given. Format conversion is in alsa-lib plug. pcm_lfloat's FLOAT_LE path is float, with power-of-two scaling. The FLOAT64 path (plugin_ops.h:698-712) is soft double per sample, but only for float64 streams, and no shipped client emits them. s31route's own resampler (rootfs/s31resample.h) is already single-precision by design.

NOT REACHED:
- No board and no timing. QEMU gives instruction counts only.
- The board's libmpg123.so and libSDL2_mixer binaries are not in the repo; only nm output exists for libmpg123. Signature-level matching for the copy-patches was not done.
- Chocolate-doom's audio-thread share on the board is unmeasured, so the first candidate's heat is inferred.
- alsa-utils source was not fetched: aplay behaviour is from knowledge of aplay.c, not re-read here.

candidates.name: gluCylinder / gluDisk / gluPartialDisk / gluSphere (sin/cos tables rebuilt on every call)
candidates.where: libGLU.so.1 (Mesa GLU 9.0.3). src/libutil/quad.c:207-229 and 742-776: angle = 2*PI*i/slices is worked out in double, then SIN/COS = sin/cos (gluint.h:43-44; _EXTENSIONS_ is not defined), which GCC fuses into an imported sincos. quad.c:180 also calls double sqrt once per gluCylinder. In a rebuild with the shipping toolchain at the board's -Os and hidden visibility, the only libm imports are sincos, sqrt and sqrtf. All three go through the PLT.
candidates.apps: mesa3d-demos 'engine' (immediate mode is the default, engine.c:204: 25 gluCylinder, 18 gluDisk and 18 gluPartialDisk per frame). Any GLU app that draws quadrics per frame instead of from display lists. ipers, spectex, teapot, texcyl and reflect build quadrics into display lists once, so they pay this only at start-up.
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU with the real engine.c and GLU 9.0.3 against a no-op libGL (build/cloud/probes/wide-glu/h/demo_engine, pcprof.so): 13,220,588 instructions per frame on the app and GLU side. That is 1,688 sincos calls per frame, about 11.5 M instructions inside libm sincos (43.4 k __muldf3 per frame, of which only 3,377 come from GLU or app code), plus about 1.5 M of GLU's own soft double. Single calls, also QEMU: gluSphere 24x24 402 k, 18x9 212 k, gluCylinder 32x8 275 k, a 12-slice cylinder plus disk 195 k. Not measured on the board.
candidates.pathology: There is no D extension, so each sincos is a chain of about 26 __muldf3 plus about 22 add/sub helper calls: about 6.8 k instructions, roughly 27 us from the MEASURED 705 ns __muldf3 and 420 ns __adddf3. The same angles are recomputed on every call and every frame, because the quadric object keeps no cache.
candidates.replacement: Two exact options. (a) Preferred: in the preload, interpose sincos, sin and cos with an exact memo in front of the real musl function. Key on the 64-bit argument bits and store the result bits plus the fflags the miss raised; on a hit, OR those fflags back into fcsr. 256 entries, 4-way, about 6 KB per process. Hit rate MEASURED in QEMU on engine: 99.2% over 11 frames (136 distinct arguments, 18,568 calls). Direct-mapped tables of 256/512/1024 entries hit only 80/90/95%. (b) Interpose gluCylinder/gluPartialDisk/gluSphere with copies of the GLU code that cache the float sin/cos tables per (slices or stacks, orientation, normals, radius), so the GL call stream stays identical. Separately, the remaining ~1.5 M/frame of libGLU-private libgcc df helpers is reachable only by copy-patch once W4 covers DSOs: preload3 scans the main executable only (preload3.c:18).
candidates.est_gain: engine immediate mode: about 11.3 M of 13.2 M instructions per frame removed (about 50-73 ms per frame at the docs' 4.5-6.5 ns per instruction; INFERRED). A quadric call drops from 200-400 k instructions to its vertex-emission loop, about 10-37 k.
candidates.exactness: Bit-identical sin/cos results, because the memo only returns what musl computed for the same argument bits. fflags must be replayed on a hit, since soft-fp raises inexact. musl math sets no errno, so there is none to preserve. NaN and inf arguments must not hit or must replay their flags too. Option (b) must emit the same GL calls in the same order with identical float arguments. gl/tests/glu_check.c page 1 (quadrics, all styles and orientations) is the ready oracle.

candidates.name: glutSolidSphere / glutSolidCone / glutSolidCylinder / glutSolidTorus (and Wire*): geometry rebuilt on every call
candidates.where: libglut.so.3 (freeglut 3.8.0) src/fg_geometry.c:1256-1300. fghCircleTable does malloc x2, then (GLfloat)sin(angle*i) and (GLfloat)cos(angle*i) in double for each slice and stack. It is called from fghGenerateSphere, Cone, Cylinder and Torus (:1302-1640) on every glutSolid*/glutWire* call. Only the teapot/teacup/teaspoon geometry is cached (fg_teapot.c:62-73). Vertex, normal and index arrays are malloc'd and freed per call too.
candidates.apps: GLUT programs that draw GLUT primitives in their display callback. Installed demos: fplight, arbfplight, renormal (per-frame glutSolidSphere/Torus in display), cuberender, cubemap, dinoshade, shadowtex. redbook/samples/tests are built but not installed, because their meson.build has no install:true.
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU on the extracted freeglut generator code (h/fgprobe): fghGenerateSphere(1, 20, 16) costs 250,253 instructions per call (61% __muldf3, 18% __subdf3, 10% __adddf3, almost all inside libm sin/cos). fghGenerateTorus(0.275, 0.85, 15, 30) costs 321,774 per call. Board frequency is unmeasured: which of these demos run on the board is unknown.
candidates.pathology: Double sin/cos from libc through the PLT: about 6.8 k instructions each with no D extension. Also __extendsfdf2/__truncdfsf2 around every value, and 4-6 mallocng calls per primitive per frame.
candidates.replacement: The same exact sincos memo as the GLU quadric item. With the angles fixed, every call after the first hits. Alternatively, interpose glutSolidSphere/Cone/Cylinder/Torus and cache the generated vertex/normal/index arrays keyed on (radius, slices, stacks), as freeglut already does for the teapot. That removes both the trig and the malloc churn. The draw must still go through freeglut's own fghDrawGeometrySolid path (1.1 vs 2.0), which is internal to libglut, so the memo is the lower-risk option.
candidates.est_gain: About 240 k instructions (about 1.1-1.6 ms) per glutSolidSphere(1, 20, 16) call, and about 310 k (1.4-2 ms) per torus, each frame (INFERRED from the QEMU counts and 4.5-6.5 ns per instruction).
candidates.exactness: Memo: bit-identical results, with fflags replayed. Array cache: the arrays must be byte-identical to a fresh generation, keyed on the exact float radius bits and on slices/stacks.

candidates.name: gluScaleImage (scale_internal) and the packed-pixel gluBuild2DMipmaps paths (halveImagePackedPixel, extract565/shove565 and friends)
candidates.where: libGLU.so.1 src/libutil/mipmap.c:1289-1390 scale_internal. Per output pixel it computes y = convy*(i+0.5) and x = convx*(j+0.5) in double. Per component it computes dataout = (totals[k]+0.5)/area: a double add, __divdf3, then __fixunsdfsi. halveImageSlice/halveImagePackedPixel carry every component through the GLdouble extract/shove routines (mipmap.c:157-178, 884-982). The public gluScaleImage always takes this path (via fill_image and empty_image). The GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE path of gluBuild2DMipmaps uses the float scale_internal_ubyte instead.
candidates.apps: Apps that call gluScaleImage for NPOT textures (installed demos projtex and lodbias; samples/stretch is not installed). Any app that uploads GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5, 4_4_4_4 or 5_5_5_1 mipmaps through GLU. 565 is our libGL's native format (plan G13).
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU (h/gluprobe): gluScaleImage RGBA 100x60 to 128x64 costs 18,112,348 instructions per call. __divdf3 is 31%, __adddf3 16%, __extendsfdf2 9%, __muldf3 8%, __fixunsdfsi 5%: about 72% in libGLU-private libgcc helpers. gluBuild2DMipmaps 128x128 GL_UNSIGNED_SHORT_5_6_5 costs 3,250,471 (__adddf3 36%, __fixunsdfsi 14%). For contrast, the ubyte path over the same NPOT 100x60 input costs 1.88 M. Board usage is unmeasured and likely load-time only.
candidates.pathology: Up to 8,192 output pixels x 4 components x (double add + double divide + double-to-uint), plus per-pixel double geometry. On the S31 every one is a libgcc call (__divdf3 about 173 instructions). The x geometry does not depend on the row yet is recomputed on every row.
candidates.replacement: Interpose gluScaleImage (an exported GLAPI symbol reached through the app's PLT) with an exact reimplementation. (1) Work out the per-column lowx/highx/xint/xpercent once, with the same double expressions, then reuse them for every row. (2) Evaluate (GLushort)((double)(t+0.5f64)/(double)area) exactly in integer arithmetic. t and area are floats, so take 24-bit mantissas and a 64/32 Zbb-normalised division for floor(num/area). Then fix up the one case where RN-to-double would round a quotient just below an integer up to it. (3) Unpack 565 with Zbb/shift instead of the double extract/shove. The static scale_internal and halveImagePackedPixel bodies could instead be copy-patched, but only once W4 covers DSOs.
candidates.est_gain: About 5-10x on gluScaleImage: 18.1 M to about 2-3 M instructions, or about 70-100 ms saved per 128x64 RGBA scale (INFERRED). Packed-pixel mipmaps 3.25 M to about 0.5 M.
candidates.exactness: Output bytes must be identical, including the double rounding of totals+0.5 and truncation toward zero. The fallback can call the original for NaN or zero area. gl/tests/glu_check.c page 2 already checksums gluScaleImage and the gluBuild*Mipmaps output. Compare it and random sizes/images against the stock libGLU under QEMU.

candidates.name: GLU tessellator (gluTessVertex/gluTessEndPolygon: __gl_edgeSign, __gl_edgeEval, __gl_vertLeq, __gl_edgeIntersect, sweep.c)
candidates.where: libGLU.so.1 src/libtess/geom.c and sweep.c. All vertex coordinates are GLdouble (tess.h:55-79), so every predicate is __subdf3/__muldf3 plus __ltdf2/__gtdf2 compare calls into libGLU's private libgcc copies. meson builds GLU with gnu_symbol_visibility 'hidden' (src/meson.build:106), so the __gl_* internals are NOT interposable. Only the glu* API and the imports (malloc, setjmp, sqrt) cross the PLT.
candidates.apps: tessdemo, dinoshade (builds the extruded dinosaur with gluTess at init), redbook tess/tesswind (not installed). Any GL app that triangulates polygons at load time. prboom-plus GL does this per sector, but it is built GL-off (defconfig:448).
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU (h/gluprobe): a 40-vertex star polygon costs 150,658 instructions per tessellation; a 400-vertex star costs 13,625,949. Of that, __muldf3 29%, __subdf3 24%, __adddf3 11%, __ltdf2 8%, __gtdf2 3%: about 75% in soft-double helpers. Board usage is load-time only and unmeasured.
candidates.pathology: The sweep does O(n log n) predicate evaluations, each several soft-double multiplies and compares at 100-450 instructions per helper. Double compares alone are more than 10%.
candidates.replacement: Copy-patch libGLU's private df helper bodies with the existing faster exact v2 helpers, which needs W4 DSO coverage because preload3 scans the main executable only (preload3.c:18). Better, copy-patch whole predicates by full-body signature: __gl_vertLeq and the VertLeq/EdgeGoesLeft compares as integer compares on the IEEE bit patterns (exact for non-NaN), and __gl_edgeSign/__gl_edgeEval as fused exact soft-double kernels that unpack each operand once.
candidates.est_gain: About 2-3x on tessellation (INFERRED from the helper share). A 400-vertex polygon goes from about 60-90 ms to about 25-40 ms. Load-time only.
candidates.exactness: The same triangles, in the same order, with identical GLdouble combine coordinates. Double compare semantics must hold for -0.0 and +0.0 (equal), and NaN must be unordered (it cannot occur from finite input). glu_check page 1 covers concave polygons, holes, winding rules, boundary-only and combine.

candidates.name: gluUnProject / gluUnProject4 / gluProject / gluPickMatrix
candidates.where: libGLU.so.1 src/libutil/project.c:149-330: __gluMultMatricesd (64 double multiply-adds), __gluInvertMatrixd (a cofactor 4x4 inverse, about 200 double operations plus a __divdf3) and __gluMultMatrixVecd. All are static and hidden. The exported gluUnProject/gluProject are reached through the app's PLT.
candidates.apps: GL apps that pick with the mouse (gluUnProject per motion event), and gluPickMatrix with GL_SELECT. Among the installed mesa demos this is rare.
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU: gluUnProject 34,825 instructions per call (__muldf3 65%, __adddf3 16%, __subdf3 7%); gluProject 7,404. Board frequency is unmeasured and probably per input event, not per frame.
candidates.pathology: The matrix product and inverse are pure soft double: about 150 __muldf3 at 705 ns MEASURED each, so about 110-160 us per gluUnProject.
candidates.replacement: Interpose gluUnProject/gluProject with an exact reimplementation that keeps the same double operation order but uses a fused soft-double 4x4 kernel. Operands are unpacked once per matrix element instead of per operation, and the mantissa products use Zbb/mulhu. Alternatively, copy-patch the static __gluInvertMatrixd/__gluMultMatricesd bodies under W4.
candidates.est_gain: About 2-3x per call (about 35 k to about 12-15 k instructions). Only noticeable in picking-heavy apps (INFERRED).
candidates.exactness: Every double result bit-identical to the stock sequence, including the order of the cofactor accumulation and the det==0 early return. Replay fflags as soft-fp would set them.

candidates.name: halveImage_ubyte (gluBuild2DMipmaps GL_UNSIGNED_BYTE box filter)
candidates.where: libGLU.so.1 src/libutil/mipmap.c halveImage_ubyte. For each output byte it computes (a+b+c+d+2)/4 from four unsigned bytes, one byte at a time. This is the path taken by every power-of-two ubyte gluBuild2DMipmaps, including util/readtex.c LoadRGBMipmaps, which the demos use.
candidates.apps: Texture load in the GLUT demos: fire 128x128 RGBA, terrain 256x256 LUMINANCE, and ipers, tunnel, reflect, engine and teapot through LoadRGBMipmaps. Also any SDL/GLX app that builds mipmaps with GLU.
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU: gluBuild2DMipmaps 256x256 GL_RGB ubyte 1,221,021 instructions (98.6% halveImage_ubyte); 128x128 RGBA 404,870; 256x256 LUMINANCE 522,627. Load-time only; board unmeasured.
candidates.pathology: About 4 instructions per source byte in scalar byte loads, with no use of 32-bit SWAR or the PIE 128-bit vectors, on a CPU where byte loads from PSRAM are the bottleneck.
candidates.replacement: A SWAR version: load 4 bytes per word from each of the two rows, split into 0x00FF00FF lanes, add the four neighbours per lane, add 0x00020002, shift right by 2 and repack. That is about 4x fewer instructions and exact for any byte values. On CPU0 a PIE esp.vld.128 variant is possible, subject to the CPU1 PIE-trap caveat. It is reached by interposing gluBuild2DMipmaps, which means reproducing the stock glTexImage2D/pixel-store call sequence, or by copy-patching the static body under W4.
candidates.est_gain: About 1.2 M to about 0.3 M instructions per 256x256 RGB mipmap chain, about 4-6 ms per texture at load (INFERRED). Small; only worth doing alongside the other GLU work.
candidates.exactness: Output bytes identical: an integer average with +2 rounding. Width-1 and height-1 edge cases, and row padding by GL_UNPACK_ALIGNMENT, must match. glu_check page 2 checksums the result.

result.coverage_notes:
None of these candidates has been measured on the board. Every instruction count is from QEMU (MEASURED, instruction counts only). Every time is INFERRED from the docs' 4.5-6.5 ns per instruction (docs/tinygl-hw-accel-assessment-2026-09-25.md:218) and the MEASURED __muldf3 705 ns / __adddf3 420 ns (same doc :70).

Scratch work is all under /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-glu/:
- The Buildroot-pinned upstream sources: glu-9.0.3, freeglut-3.8.0, mesa-demos-9.0.0 (per docs/gl-packaging.md).
- h/pcprof.so, a per-TB QEMU plugin I wrote for per-symbol instruction attribution; /plugins/libhotblocks prints only its top 20.
- h/gluprobe: GLU 9.0.3 C sources against a no-op libGL.
- h/demo_engine, h/demo_morph3d, h/demo_gears: the real demo sources with GLUT and GL stubbed.
- h/fgprobe: freeglut's generator code, extracted.
- libGLUh.so: a hidden-visibility rebuild with the shipping toolchain at the board's -Os/-march, used to read the import list and the local libgcc copies.

Neither libGLU.so.1, libglut.so.3 nor the demo binaries is in the repo, so imports and helper copies are INFERRED from that same-flags rebuild. What it shows:
- libGLU imports only sincos, sqrt, sqrtf and strtod from libm/libc (plus malloc, setjmp and string functions).
- It carries private local copies of __adddf3, __subdf3, __muldf3, __divdf3, the compares, __extendsfdf2, __truncdfsf2, __fixdfsi, __fixunsdfsi, __floatsidf and __floatunsidf.
- GLU's meson build uses gnu_symbol_visibility hidden (src/meson.build:106), so the __gl_* tessellator internals cannot be interposed.
- s31fp preload3 scans the main executable only (rootfs/s31fp/v2/preload3.c:18). libGLU's and libglut's own helper copies are therefore reachable only through the roadmap's W4 DSO coverage. Its SDL-only heat basis (0.2-1.4%) did not consider GL/GLU; the engine and tessellator numbers above are the first GLU heat.

The census G01 item does NOT shadow any of this:
- libGL drops TinyGL's glu.c (gl/api/build-lib.sh:46), and artifacts/gl/present-prof/libGL.nm has no glu* symbols.
- libGL imports sincos and cos itself for glRotate. G01's float sin/cos lives inside libGL and never serves GLU or freeglut callers.

Checked and rejected, with numbers:
- gluPerspective is 8,158 instructions per call and runs on reshape only. gluLookAt is 857 per call and works mostly in float (project.c:108-147); it is per-frame in fire, terrain, tunnel, teapot and ipers but negligible.
- glxgears app code: MEASURED 0 of 4,000 board PC samples in the glxgears binary (artifacts/gl/present-prof/gp.pcs against gp-gears.maps). GLUT gears.c per frame is 1,580 instructions in QEMU.
- freeglut timing is fgPlatformSystemTime: CLOCK_MONOTONIC, uint64 ms, no division by a variable. Its select timeout does do 64-bit division (the listed __udivdi3), and its XPending per loop iteration is the listed xlite/clock_gettime items.
- NURBS (libnurbs, C++) computes in float (REAL = float, types.h:41) and renders through GL evaluators, which our libGL does not implement (plan F8, glu_check.c page 3). Dead on the board.
- gluBuild2DMipmaps calls strtod(glGetString(GL_VERSION)) on every call (mipmap.c:3415), about 10 k instructions of soft-quad. That is the listed strtod item.
- The ubyte NPOT path (scale_internal_ubyte) is float, 1.88 M instructions for 100x60 RGBA, and is acceptable.
- morph3d rebuilds a display list every frame: 240,422 instructions per frame (QEMU, tetra), 83% soft double. It comes from float + double-literal chains such as Xa = Xf + 0.001 (morph3d.c:230-330) in the main executable. The existing main-exe copy-patch already reaches it, and it is an instance of the excluded fused-chain work.
- The most useful item for engine and the freeglut primitives is really a call-pattern fix, an exact sin/cos memo. Most of their cost is libc's soft-double sincos, the listed double-libm item.

Not reached:
- Board frequencies for any GLUT demo.
- Whether engine, fplight or renormal actually run correctly on our libGL; the ARB/NV fragment-program demos probably exit.
- Real libGLU/libglut bytes from the Buildroot build.
- Timing, since QEMU has no timing model.

gl/tests/glu_check.c, pages 1-2, is the ready exactness oracle for every GLU replacement proposed here.

candidates.name: Hosted-transport frame build: kmalloc(GFP_ATOMIC) + memset + memcpy into a bounce frame, then memcpy_toio into the ring slot (s31_send_payload_meta -> s31_send_frame); RX memcpy_fromio into rx_frame then skb_put_data copy
candidates.where: patches/0048-esp32s31-hosted-hid/esp32s31-hosted-sram.c:542-570 (bounce kmalloc+memcpy), :483-533 (memcpy_toio into slot + 4 writel/wmb + doorbell), :1872-1925 and :357-380/:889-893 (RX: memcpy_fromio, then bt_skb_alloc/napi_alloc_skb + skb_put_data)
candidates.apps: All Wi-Fi TX/RX (wget, s31-record serve, udpblast), and Bluetooth A2DP (every ACL packet goes through s31_hci_send -> s31_send_payload)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: under Wi-Fi TX hart1 is saturated and s31_send_payload_meta alone is 7.2% of the profile (docs/current-state.md:4869-4871). The additive checksum is inlined in there, and it is already on the found list. The bounce allocation and the double copy are not. A2DP adds 43-47 frames/s (current-state.md:4800-4802), and a Wi-Fi upload runs at 459-958 KB/s, i.e. ~330-680 frames/s of 1400 B (current-state.md:4906-4908).
candidates.pathology: Every outbound frame pays a GFP_ATOMIC slab allocation and free (kmalloc-2k for Wi-Fi) and a header memset, then touches the payload three times: memcpy into the bounce buffer, the byte-serial checksum, and memcpy_toio into shared SRAM. RX also touches it three times: memcpy_fromio into rx_frame, the checksum, and the skb_put_data copy. The PSRAM copy ceiling is ~13.6 MB/s (docs/current-state.md), so each redundant pass over a 1.4 kB frame costs on the order of 100 us (INFERRED from that ceiling), and all of it runs from XIP flash.
candidates.replacement: Write the 12-byte header and the payload straight into the ring slot under tx_lock, accumulating the 16-bit additive sum in the same word loop (an exact fused copy+sum; sum-of-bytes is order-independent, so a word-wise SWAR accumulate gives the same u16). Then patch the header's checksum field in the slot before publishing sequence/producer. This drops the kmalloc/kfree, the memset and one full copy. On RX, checksum the slot in place and copy once directly into the skb (napi_alloc_skb / bt_skb_alloc sized from the slot length), dropping the rx_frame bounce.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: one of three payload passes and one slab alloc/free per frame. For Wi-Fi TX that is roughly a third of s31_send_payload_meta's non-checksum cost, a few percent of hart1 under upload. Small for A2DP (~45 frames/s). Not measured.
candidates.exactness: Byte-exact on the wire. The checksum must still be computed over the frame with the checksum field zeroed, the seq_num assignment must stay under tx_lock, and the wmb ordering (data, then sequence, then producer, then doorbell) must be preserved.

candidates.name: s31-bt per-packet and idle-loop syscalls: dbus_connection_read_write(conn,0) poll(0) every iteration, 2x clock_gettime(CLOCK_THREAD_CPUTIME_ID) per packet, fixed 200 ms poll timeout under SCHED_FIFO, procfs open/read/close every 500 ms in route mode

candidates.heat: MEASURED: s31-bt 20.4% of the core while routing a tone (docs/current-state.md:5609). The split given there is SBC ~8% and L2CAP write ~2%, with 'the rest is the ALSA read path' (:5611-5613). An earlier cut from 645 to 43 reads/s took it from 50.1% to 20.4% (:5623), i.e. ~0.49 ms per removed syscall INFERRED. The CPU-time clocks are not in the vDSO, so each is a trap into XIP kernel text. That is ~130 syscalls/s at 43 pkt/s. When idle, a SCHED_FIFO task with zero slack wakes exactly every 200 ms and on each pass also runs the libdbus poll(0) and dispatch. In route mode with a sink active, route_watch adds open+read+close of a procfs seq_file every 500 ms.

Keep cpu_us() behind a debug flag, or sample it once per 5 s report instead of per packet. Use timeout=-1 when !st.active && !st.route && no pending deadlines (scan_stop_at, confirm, want): every deadline is already known, so compute the poll timeout from the nearest one. Keep the status fd open and pread(fd,buf,63,0) it rather than reopening it.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: ~86-130 fewer syscalls/s while streaming. At the 0.1-0.5 ms per trivial syscall implied by the 50.1 -> 20.4% result, that is ~1-4% of the core during Bluetooth playback, plus ~5 fewer timer interrupts and context switches per second at idle. Needs an A/B with 5+ fresh-boot runs per arm.
