candidates.heat: MEASURED-by-subtraction: s31-bt 20.4%, less SBC ~8% and L2CAP write ~2%, leaves ~10% attributed to 'the ALSA read path' (docs/current-state.md:5609-5613). The player side's write into the loopback, and aloop's timer copy (charged to whoever is interrupted), are extra and unmeasured.
candidates.pathology: A 176 KB/s stream is 43 reads/s plus aloop timer copies, and every ALSA core and aloop function runs from XIP flash. The byte copy itself is cheap (~1.3% at 13.6 MB/s, INFERRED), so most of the ~10% is per-call kernel path overhead in flash-resident code. alsa-lib's SYNC_PTR is already on the found list; the kernel-side placement is not.
candidates.replacement: Add the aloop timer/copy functions and the pcm_native/pcm_lib read path (snd_pcm_common_ioctl, snd_pcm_lib_read/__snd_pcm_lib_xfer, interleaved_copy, snd_pcm_update_hw_ptr, loopback_jiffies_timer_*, copy_play_buf, loopback_pointer) to a FASTFN list built from a profile captured during routing.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: a share of the ~10% ALSA path, perhaps 2-4% of the core while desktop audio is routed to Bluetooth. Unmeasured.
candidates.exactness: Bit-exact (relocation only).

candidates.name: libdbus message validation: _dbus_string_validate_utf8 ASCII byte loop and validate_body_helper, run on every message at every hop
candidates.where: dbus-1.14.10 dbus/dbus-string.c:2641-2710 (per-byte NUL and <128 test), dbus/dbus-marshal-validate.c:334-700 (validate_body_helper, called from dbus-message.c:4484-4531 with DBUS_VALIDATION_MODE_DATA_IS_UNTRUSTED for every loaded message). The code is statically linked into dbus-daemon (libdbus-internal) and exported/hidden inside libdbus-1.so for bluetoothd and s31-bt. Neither binary is in the repo, so no offsets.
candidates.apps: dbus-daemon, bluetoothd, s31-bt
candidates.heat: MEASURED low: dbus-daemon and bluetoothd do not appear in the switches/s census (>=0.5/s) of a 34.5 s busy window (artifacts/gl/glquake/tick/attribution.txt:17-36), and 'bluetoothd measured 0% CPU' (docs/current-state.md:4603). The bursts are GetManagedObjects replies, which carry every BlueZ object: s31-bt made 7,800 of them in 6.5 h before a 3->60 s backoff (s31-bt.c comment above route_find_transport). Each reply is validated by dbus-daemon and again by libdbus in s31-bt.
candidates.pathology: An ASCII string is validated one byte at a time with two compares per byte. The validation is not interposable (internal symbol, and the daemons are not preloaded) and runs twice per hop.
candidates.replacement: A word-at-a-time exact validator: load 4 bytes, and if (w & 0x80808080)==0 and orc.b(w)==0xFFFFFFFF (Zbb: no NUL byte), skip 4 bytes; otherwise fall back to the byte path at that word. Apply it to dbus-daemon's static copy via a signature-matched copy-patch, or rebuild dbus with the patch applied to the ASCII fast path.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED negligible in steady state (the daemons are idle). It only shortens the GetManagedObjects burst and connect/discovery signal storms. Recorded so it is not re-derived, not recommended ahead of the kernel items.
candidates.exactness: The validity result must be identical: stop at the first NUL (invalid), and the exact same acceptance of overlong/surrogate/range cases, handled by the unchanged byte path.

candidates.name: BlueZ storage hex decoders: record_from_string (strtol per byte), str2buf / main.c key parsing (sscanf "%02hhX" per byte), load_gatt_db UUID128 (strtol per byte)
candidates.where: bluez-5.79 src/storage.c:128-147, src/adapter.c:3950-3965, src/main.c:232, src/device.c:4011-4017, statically inside bluetoothd (/usr/libexec/bluetooth/bluetoothd, XIP)
candidates.apps: bluetoothd
candidates.heat: MEASURED only in the failure mode: with a corrupt 3 MB store, 18.7% of samples were in bluetoothd's sscanf/strtol/strtoul loops and 79% in musl strlen (docs/current-state.md:6309-6315). A healthy store is parsed only at boot and connect, where heat is unmeasured and presumably ms-scale.
candidates.pathology: Each byte of an SDP record or key costs a strtol, or a full vsscanf with a fake-FILE setup (musl vsscanf's string_read memchr-scans up to len+256 bytes per refill; INFERRED from musl source, not checked against the board's libc 352e9417). The per-byte cost is large even though the total per boot is small. Bluetoothd is not preloaded, so s31fp interposition cannot reach its strtol/sscanf.
candidates.replacement: A table- or arithmetic-based hex pair decoder (nibble = (c & 0xF) + 9*(c >> 6), with validity checks), patched in via a full-body signature match of record_from_string/str2buf, or upstreamed as a BlueZ source patch.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: sub-millisecond per boot and connect on a healthy store. Only material as damage limitation if a store grows again, and the 64 kB quarantine guard already bounds that. Low priority.
candidates.exactness: The same bytes for valid hex. For malformed input it must match strtol's behaviour (stop at a non-hex character, giving a partial value) and sscanf's return count in main.c:232.

result.coverage_notes:
What I searched:
- Measured daemon heat: docs/current-state.md (the bluetoothd corrupt-store spin at 6290-6360, the bluealsa glib pool-spawner at 4486-4510, the A2DP cost tables at 4882-4908 and 5595-5625, the hosted-IRQ section at 4780-4815) and docs/perf-review-2026-09-23.md:440-452. Row 52 retracts the "~4 ms per hosted IRQ" figure, and the disable_irq pair it blamed has already been removed from s31_hosted_poll.
- Per-process switches and timer slack: artifacts/gl/glquake/tick/attribution.txt. Process lists: artifacts/gl/dips/swn-*.txt.
- Kernel RAM-text coverage: the three FASTFN lists (patches/0062, 0069, 0073).
- Code: the hosted driver (patches/0048-esp32s31-hosted-hid/esp32s31-hosted-sram.c) and rootfs/s31-bt.c.
- Pinned versions, fetched from Buildroot cb857ba4: dbus 1.14.10, glib 2.86.5, expat 2.8.2, BlueZ 5.79, wpa_supplicant 2.11, eudev 3.2.14. dbus, BlueZ and the glib thread/main/utf8 sources are unpacked under build/cloud/probes/wide-btdbus/.

Main finding: the daemons themselves are cold in steady state.
- bluetoothd, dbus-daemon, udevd, crond and ntpd are all below 0.5 switches/s in a busy 34.5 s window. wpa_supplicant is 1.6/s and bluetoothd was measured at 0%.
- So D-Bus marshalling, g_str_hash, GSList walks, the glib main loop and expat introspection parsing have no measured heat. Expat only runs on Introspect calls, and nothing in steady state issues them.
- The real Bluetooth heat is the A2DP data path: s31-bt at 20.4% and the hci0 kworker at 8-9.2%. The new candidates are therefore mostly kernel placement and copy elimination on that path, plus redundant per-packet syscalls in s31-bt.

Glib futex check: I looked at glib 2.86.5's futex wrappers because of the old bluealsa pool-spawner spin. On riscv32 musl, `__NR_futex` is aliased to `futex_time64` (sysroot bits/syscall.h:297), and glib's g_futex_simple and g_cond_wait_until paths look correct. That spin is not explained by a futex ENOSYS fallback, and bluetoothd does not use GThreadPool, so I report no candidate there.

What I could not reach:
- The board binaries for bluetoothd, dbus-daemon, libdbus-1, libglib-2.0, libexpat, wpa_supplicant and udevd are not in the repo. There are no offsets and no signature feasibility check for the two copy-patch items. The musl vsscanf behaviour I cite is from upstream source, not the board's libc.
- The kernel source for net/bluetooth and aloop is not checked out, so the function names come from upstream knowledge (INFERRED).
- There is no BT-streaming /proc/profile capture, so the kernel split between hci TX, hci RX and L2CAP is unmeasured.
- There is no board, so nothing was run.

candidates.name: memcmp (n = 1 or 2, one call per colour tried per pixel)
candidates.where: libc memcmp, reached through the s31str interposer (rootfs/s31fp/v3/s31str.c:384-392 forwards any n<64 to l_memcmp, so it costs PLT + preload + indirect call + musl scalar memcmp). Call site: xstubs/xstubs.c:517-521, the XLITE-SHM fast path of xpm_build() (XpmCreatePixmapFromData), which does a linear memcmp search over the colour table for every pixel. The batched fallback at xstubs.c:566-587 is worse: colours x pixels.
candidates.apps: xfiles (loads all 32 compiled-in 64x64 icons at startup: xfsrc/icons.c; docs/x11-shim.md:606 records 32 pixmaps handed over); any client that uses XPM through our libXpm stub
candidates.heat: MEASURED (QEMU instruction counts, replica of the xstubs.c:500-529 loop over xfiles c47a0d9 icons, upstream musl memcmp and strlen, scratch build/cloud/probes/wide-litelibs/xpmh_all.c): 658,898 memcmp calls and 131,072 strlen calls for one xfiles startup, 32.3 M instructions in total. The worst icons are file-image.xpm and folder-image.xpm, at 388 and 390 colours with cpp=2: 86,516 memcmp and 2.85 M instructions for file-image alone, against 0.96 M for the 7-colour file-archive.xpm. A per-icon key hash (xpmf_all.c) does the same 32 icons in 3.6 M instructions, 9x fewer. There is no board timing.
candidates.pathology: Each 1-2 byte compare pays the full call chain: PLT, the preload's eligibility test, an indirect call into libc, and musl's alignment prologue. The work is 1-2 byte loads. On the board the interposer adds a second call level that the QEMU count leaves out.
candidates.replacement: Fix at source, because xstubs is first-party. Build the key-to-index table once per icon: a 256-entry LUT for cpp=1, and a 1024-slot open-addressed hash for cpp<=4 on the packed key. Then pack the key per pixel with integer shifts, with no libc call. In the stock-routine direction, the s31str memcmp could inline n<=8 before it forwards to l_memcmp. That removes the indirect call for every tiny compare in every app, and it is exact because it returns the same first-differing-byte difference.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED about 28.7 M of 32.3 M instructions removed from xfiles startup (QEMU count, 9x on this loop). Wall time is unmeasured.
candidates.exactness: Output pixels must be identical, including the first matching colour index when keys are duplicated: a hash insert must keep the FIRST occurrence. An inlined small-n memcmp must return the same sign and byte difference (*a-*b of the first mismatch) as musl.

candidates.name: strlen (the same row re-measured on every pixel)
candidates.where: musl strlen (not interposed; generic word loop). Call site: xstubs/xstubs.c:515, `if ((int)strlen(row) < (x + 1) * cpp)` inside the per-pixel loop of xpm_build's SHM path, which re-scans a 64- or 128-byte row 64 times.
candidates.apps: xfiles startup (all XPM icons)
candidates.heat: MEASURED (QEMU, same replica): 131,072 strlen calls per xfiles startup over 64-128 byte rows, about 9 MB of bytes scanned (INFERRED from the row lengths). Its instructions are inside the 32.3 M total above.
candidates.pathology: The row is loop-invariant, but strlen is re-evaluated for every pixel, so each row costs O(w^2) bytes scanned. musl strlen has no Zbb orc.b word test.
candidates.replacement: Fix at source: hoist `rowlen = strlen(row)` out of the x loop, as the fallback path at xstubs.c:573 already does, and clamp w to rowlen/cpp. That leaves one strlen per row (4,096 in total instead of 131,072).
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED about 97% of the strlen work in icon decode, 127k calls removed. The combined fix is included in the 9x measured for the first entry.
candidates.exactness: The break must still happen at the same x when a row is short (x+1)*cpp > rowlen.

candidates.name: strlen + memcmp in the Xrm quark intern linear scan
candidates.where: musl strlen (not interposed) and memcmp (via the s31str forwarder). Call site: xlite/xlite_xrm.c:44-47 intern(), which compares against every existing quark and calls strlen(qstr[i]) for each one. It is reached from split() for every component of every XrmGetResource name and class path (xlite_xrm.c:608-620), which xtlite/xtlite.c:145-162 res_get() calls about 15 times per widget.
candidates.apps: xcalc, xclock, oclock (anything on xtlite/libXt), plus any client that calls XrmGetResource or XrmStringToQuark through xlite
candidates.heat: MEASURED (QEMU, scratch xrmh.c): loading the upstream XCalc app-defaults (448 resource lines, 160 quarks) plus a modelled 40 buttons x 16 resources lookup pass takes 9,626 interns, 778,628 strlen calls (106,776 during load, 671,852 during lookups) and 38.3 M instructions. With an FNV hash table and a length-plus-NUL check (xrmf.c) the same work is 3.9 M instructions and 9,603 compares. The lookup pattern is INFERRED from xtlite.c:370-416; the counts are MEASURED for that model.
candidates.pathology: The scan is O(quarks) per intern, and it recomputes strlen of every quark string, so each resource lookup walks about 160 strings. The strlen calls are on 4-20 byte strings, so call overhead dominates.
candidates.replacement: Fix at source: hash the intern table, or at least store each quark's length alongside it. This is first-party code, and an interposer cannot beat simply not making 778k calls.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED 38.3 M to 3.9 M instructions (about 10x) for xcalc resource resolution at startup under the model. That is launch latency only; nothing per expose.
candidates.exactness: Quark numbering must remain first-come order: the same string must map to the same quark id, and ids must stay dense from 1.

candidates.name: snprintf used as strcpy ("%s", "%s%s", "%.*s")
candidates.where: musl snprintf -> vfprintf. Call sites: xtlite/xtlite.c:133-140 and 157 path_of()/res_get() (2*depth+3 calls per resource lookup), xtlite.c:940-941 run_actions() (2 per action on every click or keypress), xtlite.c:281/321/373 label copies, and xstubs/xstubs.c:371 in the XPM colour cache.
candidates.apps: xcalc (every button press and release), xclock/oclock (startup), xfiles (XPM colours)
candidates.heat: MEASURED (QEMU, act.c vs act2.c): run_actions on "set() notify() unset()" costs about 4.9 K instructions per invocation in snprintf, about 815 instructions per snprintf("%.*s"), against memcpy+NUL. Per xcalc click that is about 6 calls, roughly 5 K instructions, which is negligible per keypress. At startup, INFERRED about 640 lookups x ~13 snprintf, about 8.3 K calls, roughly 6.8 M instructions using the measured per-call cost.
candidates.pathology: vfprintf's two-pass format parse and its FILE-emulation setup do a 5-20 byte copy. This is the already-listed vfprintf cost; the new part is these call sites.
candidates.replacement: Fix at source: use memcpy plus a bounded NUL for %.*s, and a small bounded append helper in path_of. No interposition is needed.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED about 6 M instructions at xcalc startup. Per keypress it is about 5 K instructions, which is not worth doing for latency on its own.
candidates.exactness: Truncation must match snprintf semantics: at most n-1 bytes, always NUL-terminated. Any caller that uses the offset arithmetic (oi += ret) must see the untruncated length.

candidates.name: __divdi3 (64-bit signed division) in the client-side polygon tessellator
candidates.where: libgcc __divdi3 (already a listed routine; this is a new call site). xrlite/xrlite.c edge_x_at(), `(long long)(x2-x1)*(y-y1)/(y2-y1)`, called once per edge per band in XRenderCompositeDoublePoly.
candidates.apps: xclock in render mode (the dial ticks and hands are drawn entirely through XRenderCompositeDoublePoly, per xrlite.c comments), on every expose or tick
candidates.heat: INFERRED and unmeasured: up to (2n-1) bands x n edges divisions per polygon (MAXPT=64), and xclock draws 60 tick polygons plus 2-3 hands per full expose, so from hundreds to a few thousand __divdi3 calls per full redraw. The same routine also converts 4 doubles per vertex, twice per vertex, through XDoubleToFixed. Those are soft-double helpers and are EXCLUDED by this brief.
candidates.pathology: The divisor is a 32-bit XFixed span, but the 64-bit dividend forces a full __divdi3 call. It could be a 32-bit division whenever the product fits, or a single per-edge slope computed once instead of once per band.
candidates.replacement: Fix at source: compute each edge's slope once in 16.16 fixed point (one division per edge, not per band x edge), or check whether |dx*dy| fits in 32 bits and use the hardware div in that case. Converting XPointDouble once per vertex instead of twice (the k=i+1 duplicate) halves the excluded soft-double calls too.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED to be small: a few thousand soft calls per xclock redraw at most. Worth doing only alongside the double-conversion cleanup.
candidates.exactness: The trapezoid coordinates sent on the wire must be identical: the same truncation-toward-zero division result as the C 64-bit division.

result.coverage_notes:
I read xtlite/xtlite.c (res_get/path_of, the converters, dispatch/run_actions, draw, XtAppMainLoop), xtlite/xtclass.c (timers via gettimeofday, the GC cache memcmp, converters), xrlite/xrlite.c (whole file, including the DoublePoly tessellator), xftlite/xftlite.c (the function list and face_for), xstubs/xstubs.c (the XPM decoder, colour cache and FcPattern stubs), xlite/xlite_xrm.c (intern, split, the QGetResource path) and alsalite/README.md. alsalite is a design note only, with no code, so it pushes heat into no routine today. Findings:

- **xftlite** does no rasterisation, has no glyph cache and uses no float or double math. It maps every Xft call onto core-font XDrawString and XTextWidth, so glyph cost lands in xlite and the server, not in libc or libm.
- **strtof**: the one xtlite converter call (xtlite.c:251) runs at startup only.
- **sprintf %g**: xcalc's own display formatting is app code already covered by the fmt_fp entries.
- **xclock/oclock sin and cos**: app code in double libm, already listed.
- **xt_note**: it evaluates (double) casts even when tracing is off (xtlite.c:691), but only on resize, and they are excluded soft-double conversions.
- **The GC cache memcmp** in xtclass.c:474 compares a ~92-byte XGCValues, but only during XtGetGC at init.
- **xtlite timers** use gettimeofday, which the existing clock work already covers.

Measurement method: QEMU instruction counts only, on faithful replicas of the loops, compiled with s31-cc against the QEMU sysroot's upstream musl. That is not byte-identical to the board libc, and on the board memcmp also passes through the s31str forwarder. Nothing was timed, and there was no board.

Inputs fetched: the xfiles icons came from github phillbush/xfiles at the Buildroot-pinned c47a0d9, and the XCalc app-defaults from the gitlab xcalc master branch, not a pinned version. The xcalc lookup pattern of 40 buttons x 16 resources is a model derived from xtlite.c:370-416, not a trace.

All of the new heat found here is at first-party call sites (xstubs, xlite_xrm, xtlite, xrlite), and the fix belongs at source. The only interposer-level idea is inlining n<=8 in s31str memcmp before it forwards to libc.

Scratch files are in /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-litelibs/: xpmh*.c, xpmf*.c, xrmh.c, xrmf.c, act.c, act2.c.

candidates.name: memcmp / bcmp with n < 64 (ncurses CharEq cell compare in doupdate/TransformLine)
candidates.where: libncursesw.so (nnn, and any ncurses TUI) -> PLT -> rootfs/s31fp/v3/s31str.c:384 memcmp, which for !elig (n<64) forwards to l_memcmp = libc memcmp; libc memcmp (toolchain libc.so 0x105a0) takes the byte loop at 0x10612 for every n<64. Caller: ncurses-6.5 curses.priv.h:1404 CharEq = attr compare + memcmp(chars, CCHARW_MAX*4 = 20 bytes) (TransformLine, hashmap)
candidates.apps: nnn (BR2_PACKAGE_NNN=y, ncursesw), any ncursesw program on the board; memcmp<64 is also generic for Xorg/X libs
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU with a synthetic nnn-style redraw of 29 listing rows plus a status line on 80x30 xterm-256color, ncurses 6.5 widec built with s31-cc -Os and linked statically (build/cloud/probes/wide-term/nctest.c): 100 refreshes = 243,980,636 instructions, memcmp 109,077,650 (44.7%) in 804,035 calls (about 8,040 calls and 136 instructions per call per refresh), memcpy 57,946,705 (23.8%). On-board heat in nnn is unmeasured: every keystroke that moves the cursor runs erase() and a full-list redraw (nnn.c:6616 redraw, 6635 erase).
candidates.pathology: musl/xespv memcmp only runs the PIE block path for n>=64. Below that it compares byte by byte, about 7 instructions per byte, and on the board each call also pays the PLT and the s31str wrapper before reaching it. ncurses compares 20-byte wchar arrays per screen cell several times per refresh (about 3.3 calls per cell), always 4-byte aligned, and the arrays are usually equal, so every call runs the full 20 bytes.
candidates.replacement: In s31str memcmp/bcmp, send n<64 with ((a^b)&3)==0 straight to the existing sc_memcmp word loop (s31str.c:154: 2x32-bit compare per 8 bytes, byte fallback for the difference) instead of l_memcmp. Leave the rseq/PIE routing out of this path, since the n>=64 gate already keeps small calls off PIE. Measured by linking the same word loop into nctest: total 243.98M -> 168.69M instructions (-31%), memcmp 109.1M -> 33.8M (-69%), and byte-identical terminal output (12,107 bytes, cmp o1 o2).
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED -31% instructions per ncurses full refresh in QEMU (about 2.44M -> 1.69M instructions per 80x30 redraw). On the board the PLT and wrapper overhead per call adds to the win. Any wall-time figure is INFERRED; there is no timing model.
candidates.exactness: The sign and magnitude of the return value must match musl's: the first differing byte's *a - *b, as unsigned chars. sc_memcmp breaks out of the word loop on inequality and finishes byte by byte, so the result is exact. Loads are aligned only (the (a^b)&3 gate plus a scalar prefix), so no misaligned trap and no overread past n.

candidates.name: strcasestr (nnn type-to-filter)
candidates.where: libc.so strcasestr (musl src/string/strcasestr.c: strncasecmp at every haystack position, tolower per char, all libc-internal calls). Caller: nnn-5.0 src/nnn.c:2986 fnstrstr = &strcasestr, run over every directory entry on every filter keystroke
candidates.apps: nnn (dynamic); any dynamic program using strcasestr
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU (build/cloud/probes/wide-term/cs.c): 2,000 real file names x 7 progressive patterns (l..libxcb-) = 14,000 calls cost 7.60M instructions under musl (strncasecmp 4.57M + tolower 1.80M + strcasestr 1.23M), about 543 instructions per call. On-board call rate unmeasured: per keystroke it is 1 call per entry in the current directory.
candidates.pathology: musl's strcasestr is O(n*m). It calls strncasecmp at every haystack offset, which calls tolower() out of line twice per character. It uses no first-character scan and no Zbb. Because these are internal libc bindings, s31str's existing interposers cannot reach them.
candidates.replacement: Export strcasestr from s31fp as ASCII case folding ((c-'A')<26u ? c|32 : c; musl's tolower is ASCII-only in every locale). Scan for the folded first needle character in either case, then verify inline. The prototype fcasestr gave the same 2,275 hits on the same input for 1.17M instructions (+0.41M strlen), about 84 instructions per call. A Zbb orc.b word scan for the two first-byte candidates would go further.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED 6.5x fewer instructions per call (543 -> 84) in QEMU. With 2,000 entries that is about 1.1M -> 0.17M instructions per filter keystroke; wall time is INFERRED.
candidates.exactness: The returned pointer must be the leftmost match, the same as musl's: scan order is left to right, so it matches. An empty needle returns the haystack. Folding must be ASCII-only, as musl's tolower is, with no locale dependence.

candidates.name: musl regexec (TRE) on literal / literal-prefix patterns, including its per-byte mbtowc
candidates.where: musl src/regex/regexec.c (tre_tnfa_run_parallel plus GET_NEXT_WCHAR -> mbtowc per byte), statically linked into busybox (busybox_unstripped: regexec 0x945b2 size 0x13e0, regcomp 0x93318). Callers: busybox grep (findutils/grep.c:398/543), sed, and awk literal /re/ matches.
candidates.apps: static busybox grep/sed/awk (init scripts S05xip/S06s31-cgroup/S30clock/S04s31-swap, s31-deskmon, s31-play, s31-peripheral-test, board harness scripts); dynamic regexec users (nnn regex filter mode nnn.c:3016, archive_re nnn.c:7226)
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU with busybox 1.38.0 built by s31-cc (build/cloud/probes/ram-userspace/busybox-1.38.0/busybox_unstripped, board busybox config, minimal env). `grep MemAvailable` over 1,080 lines / 30,060 bytes of meminfo: regexec 3,453,940 of 7,569,809 instructions (45.6%), about 115 instructions per byte, plus mbtowc 387,036. `grep -F` of the same input spends 116,460 in twoway_strstr (3.9 per byte). sed 's/^MemAvailable:...//p': regexec 2,593,860 (41.5%). awk '/MemAvailable/' on a single 54-line meminfo: regexec 183,322 of 551,921 (33%). How often boards run these is unmeasured.
candidates.pathology: TRE runs a tagged-NFA simulation in wide-character mode for every byte, with an mbtowc call per byte, even when the pattern is a plain literal or an anchored literal (^MemAvailable:). It has no required-literal or first-byte prefilter, so the cost is about 30x a strstr. busybox is linked static (busybox.fragment CONFIG_STATIC=y), so an LD_PRELOAD interposer cannot reach this copy.
candidates.replacement: At regcomp, detect a pattern that is a pure literal, optionally with a leading ^, no REG_ICASE and no backrefs; ideally also record the required literal and first byte for general patterns. At regexec, answer pure literals with memchr/strstr (or a single anchored memcmp) and fill pmatch[0] directly. For other patterns, reject lines that lack the required literal before running the NFA. Reach: (1) the static busybox only gets it through a patched musl libc.a (the project already carries a musl patch set, toolchain/riscv32-esp-linux-musl/s31-patch-sha256.txt, docs/xespv-libc.md) followed by a busybox relink. There is no way in by preload, and a copy-patch would have to run offline over the busybox file, because s31fp is not loaded into static binaries. (2) Dynamic users (nnn) can get it by interposing regcomp/regexec/regfree in s31fp, keeping the literal side table keyed on regex_t's spare __padding[4] or a pointer map and delegating everything else to libc.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED from the MEASURED numbers: on literal patterns regexec drops from about 115 to under 5 instructions per byte (-40 to -45% of total grep/sed instructions on the measured inputs). Against a static exec cost of about 14 ms (busybox.fragment note, measured 2026-09-02), this matters only for multi-KB inputs or many lines.
candidates.exactness: Must keep POSIX leftmost-longest semantics: for a pure literal the leftmost occurrence is the unique match, so pmatch[0] is exact. Honour REG_NOTBOL for ^, REG_NEWLINE (a literal without '\n' is unaffected), REG_NOSUB and nmatch. Byte-mode matching of a literal equals TRE's wide-character result only when the pattern and subject treat bytes >=0x80 the same way. musl's C locale maps them to 0xDF80+b, which is one-to-one, so a byte compare is exact. Leave REG_ICASE to TRE.

candidates.name: busybox awk dynamic regex (`$0 ~ var`) recompiled on every record
candidates.where: busybox editors/awk.c:1973 as_regex(): any match against a non-literal re calls regcomp (and regfree) on every evaluation. Hit by overlay/usr/bin/s31-deskmon:32 field(), which runs `awk -v k="^$2:" '$0 ~ k {print $2; exit}'` 3x per sample
candidates.apps: s31-deskmon (the desktop memory/repaint sampler); any board script that uses awk with -v pattern matching
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU with board-sized env: field VmData on a /proc/PID/status sample costs 950,241 instructions with `$0 ~ k` against 264,455 with `index($0,k)==1` (3.6x). For VmSwap, 1,119,132 vs 304,880. Over 1,080 lines, `$0 ~ k` costs 46.47M instructions (regcomp/tre_add_tags/tre_stack_push/memset/malloc dominate) against 6.93M for the literal /^MemAvailable:/. How often deskmon runs is operator-driven (INTERVAL default 5 s).
candidates.pathology: TRE regcomp costs about 40k instructions plus a malloc/free storm per compile, and busybox repeats it for every record while scanning toward the key. The sampler is a measurement tool, so its own CPU cost perturbs what it measures, which CLAUDE.md already warns about for mjpegrec and shell-loop harnesses.
candidates.replacement: In s31-deskmon, use `index($0, k)==1` with k="$2:" (no regex), or fold the three field() calls into a single awk pass over /proc/PID/status printing VmData,VmRSS,VmSwap. Do the same for swap_used and the MemAvailable lookup, which can share one awk over /proc/meminfo. That removes 2 to 4 of about 13 execs per sample and each exec's roughly 14 ms static exec cost. It is a script-only change: no busybox rebuild and no s31fp.
candidates.est_gain: MEASURED 3.6x fewer instructions per field() call (about 0.95-1.12M -> 0.26-0.30M). Merging the awk calls also saves at least 2 fork+exec per sample, INFERRED at about 27 ms each from the spawnbench fork 13 ms + static exec 14 ms figures in busybox.fragment.
candidates.exactness: The ^key: anchored match must equal index($0,"key:")==1, which holds because the keys contain no regex metacharacters. Output text and columns stay unchanged.

candidates.name: st utf8decode / utf8validate (per input byte in twrite)
candidates.where: st 0.9.2 st.c:284 utf8decode and :309 utf8decodebyte (+ utf8validate), called once per byte from twrite (st.c:2511) before tputc; /usr/bin/st (BR2_PACKAGE_ST=y, lvdesk menu.conf:304 'Terminal = st')
candidates.apps: st (dynamic, X11/Xft), the desktop's menu terminal
candidates.heat: MEASURED in QEMU with the st 0.9.2 core (st.c with X stubs, s31-cc -Os like BR2_TARGET_OPTIMIZATION, build/cloud/probes/wide-term/st-0.9.2/stub.c) fed 20,298 bytes of `ls -l` output x10: 65.98M instructions, 325 per byte. utf8decode 6.50M + utf8validate 3.45M = 49 per byte (15%), both called 202,980 times (once per byte). How often st runs output-heavy commands on the board is unmeasured.
candidates.pathology: utf8decode is a generic loop through the utf8mask/utfbyte tables, with a stack frame, a call to utf8validate and a table search even for 7-bit ASCII, which is nearly all terminal traffic. At about 49 instructions per ASCII byte it is roughly 6x what an ASCII fast path costs. The function is pure (inputs are the pointer, length and out-pointer, with read-only tables), which makes it a clean full-body signature target.
candidates.replacement: Add an s31fp copy-patch signature for st's utf8decode: if clen>=1 and c[0]<0x80, set *u=c[0] and return 1; otherwise fall through to a copy of the original body. The same entry could also cover utf8validate for the ASCII case. The alternative, rebuilding st with -O2 as a per-package override, measured 49.80M vs 65.98M instructions (-24.5%) for the whole core, because -Os also emits a memcpy call for each 16-byte Glyph copy in tsetchar (200,019 memcpy calls, 7.8M instructions). On the board those calls go through the PLT and the s31str memcpy wrapper.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: about 49 -> about 8 instructions per ASCII byte, roughly -12% of st's terminal-core instructions (325 -> about 285 per byte). A per-package -O2 rebuild gives MEASURED -24.5%. Neither touches the Xft/XRender glyph drawing path, which is likely the larger cost and was not measured here.
candidates.exactness: Must return the same length and Rune as st's utf8decode for every input: invalid or overlong sequences go to UTF_INVALID (0xFFFD) through utf8validate, and a truncated multibyte sequence returns 0. The fast path covers only c[0]<0x80 with clen>=1; everything else runs the original bytes. The signature must full-body match the -Os build that ships.

candidates.name: hosted Wi-Fi RX: memcpy_fromio -> bounce frame -> byte-sum -> skb_put_data memcpy -> CHECKSUM_NONE -> stack software csum (do_csum)
candidates.where: patches/0048-esp32s31-hosted-hid/esp32s31-hosted-sram.c:1915 (memcpy_fromio of SRAM slot into the 'frame' bounce buffer), :876 (s31_frame_checksum over the frame), :889-898 (napi_alloc_skb + skb_put_data second copy, skb->ip_summed = CHECKSUM_NONE). Kernel #397 layout (artifacts/gl/glquake/kfast/base-nm.txt): s31_hosted_poll 2864 B FLASH, memcpy_fromio 108 B FLASH, memcpy 246 B FLASH, do_csum 82 B FLASH, skb_checksum 344 B FLASH, __skb_checksum_complete 126 B FLASH, tcp_rcv_established/tcp_v4_rcv FLASH
candidates.apps: anything receiving over wlan0: wget from a host HTTP server (docs deploy path), s31-record/s31-serve control traffic, wpa_supplicant, any network client
candidates.heat: UNMEASURED for Wi-Fi (no profile of a network workload exists; GLQuake capture has only 65 of 32,000 hart-1 samples in net/sock code, none of it Wi-Fi). Throughput context MEASURED: 191 KB/s and 575 KB/s wget (docs/lvgl-bringup.md:45-47), 915 KB/s s31-serve (docs/current-state.md:3524).
candidates.pathology: Every received byte is touched five times, all in flash-resident code: (1) memcpy_fromio SRAM->bounce, (2) byte-at-a-time 16-bit sum (s31_frame_checksum), (3) memcpy bounce->skb, (4) because the driver says CHECKSUM_NONE, TCP runs __skb_checksum_complete -> skb_checksum -> do_csum over the whole segment (the RISC-V Zbb csum path is compiled out under XIP since RISCV_ALTERNATIVE is off, so this is the generic C loop), (5) copy_to_user. Passes 1-4 are pure overhead on a core whose copy ceiling is ~13.6 MB/s (CLAUDE.md, PSRAM bandwidth).
candidates.replacement: In s31_hosted_poll/s31_process_frame: read the header from the slot, napi_alloc_skb first, then do ONE word-wise pass SRAM->skb->data that simultaneously accumulates (a) the transport byte-sum exactly (per 32-bit word: (w & 0x00ff00ff) + ((w >> 8) & 0x00ff00ff), folded, mod 2^16, with the checksum field treated as zero) and (b) the Internet one's-complement sum of the bytes after the 14-byte Ethernet header (the csum_partial_copy_nocheck shape, with Zbb rev8/andn not needed on little-endian). Drop the frame on byte-sum mismatch exactly as today; otherwise set skb->ip_summed = CHECKSUM_COMPLETE, skb->csum = (b). The stack then only folds skb->csum with the pseudo-header and skips the full skb_checksum pass. Put the fused loop (~200 B) in .text..fast. This is a first-party driver, so it is not a 'patch a mature driver' case.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: removes 2 of 3 extra copy passes and the stack's checksum pass - roughly 3 of 5 passes over each received byte. At the 13.6 MB/s PSRAM copy ceiling a single pass costs ~74 ms of CPU per MB, so at ~1 MB/s ingress that is on the order of 10-20% of a hart back; negligible when the link is idle.
candidates.exactness: Byte-sum must equal s31_frame_checksum bit-for-bit, including the header checksum field zeroed and odd trailing bytes; malformed-frame drop behaviour unchanged. CHECKSUM_COMPLETE value must be the unfolded 32-bit one's-complement sum starting at the L3 header (post eth_type_trans skb->data) - a wrong value makes the stack drop good packets, so validate on QEMU against csum_partial over random frames including odd lengths and VLAN-less/VLAN cases.

candidates.name: hosted Wi-Fi TX: no NETIF_F_HW_CSUM/SG -> skb_checksum_help pass + kmalloc(GFP_ATOMIC)+memcpy+byte-sum+memcpy_toio per packet
candidates.where: patches/0048-esp32s31-hosted-hid/esp32s31-hosted-sram.c:1971-1996 (s31_hosted_xmit -> s31_send_payload), :548-567 (kmalloc frame, memcpy payload), :501 (s31_frame_checksum), :517 (memcpy_toio into SRAM slot); net_device has no features set (probe, ~:2020). Flash: skb_checksum_help 342 B, csum_and_copy_from_iter_full 1200 B, memcpy_toio 104 B, memcpy, do_csum all FLASH in #397
candidates.apps: s31-serve / s31-record serve (board->host transfers), any TCP/UDP sender on wlan0, Bluetooth-over-hosted uses the same s31_send_payload_meta
candidates.heat: UNMEASURED CPU share; MEASURED throughput 915 KB/s for s31-serve over Wi-Fi (docs/current-state.md:3524), which is exactly this TX path.
candidates.pathology: Without NETIF_F_HW_CSUM the core computes the L4 checksum in software (skb_checksum_help or csum-and-copy from user, both flash-resident generic code without Zbb), then the driver kmallocs a GFP_ATOMIC bounce buffer per packet (slab churn on a 15.4 MB machine where slab is 28% of RAM), memcpy's the whole frame into it, byte-sums it, and memcpy_toio's it again: 4 passes plus an allocation per 1.5 KB frame.
candidates.replacement: Advertise NETIF_F_HW_CSUM | NETIF_F_SG (and set needed_headroom = sizeof(struct s31_esp_payload_header)). In xmit, under tx_lock, write the header straight into the SRAM slot and copy linear data + frags into the slot in one pass that accumulates both the transport byte-sum and, if skb->ip_summed == CHECKSUM_PARTIAL, the one's-complement sum from csum_start; store csum_fold at csum_start+csum_offset in the slot and correct the byte-sum for the two inserted bytes arithmetically. No kmalloc, no bounce, no separate csum pass. The loop (~250 B) goes in .text..fast.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: 4 passes + 1 slab alloc/free per frame become 1 pass; at ~1 MB/s egress that is again on the order of 10-20% of a hart by the 13.6 MB/s copy-ceiling arithmetic, and ~700 GFP_ATOMIC kmalloc/kfree pairs per second removed at 915 KB/s.
candidates.exactness: On-wire bytes must be identical to today's software-checksummed frames (compare frames from both paths in QEMU for TCP/UDP, odd lengths, fragmented skbs); byte-sum over the slot must match what hart0's IDF verifier computes; csum_offset insertion must respect the HW_CSUM contract (0 -> 0xffff for UDP is done by the stack before handing CHECKSUM_PARTIAL, verify).

candidates.name: esp32s31_lcd_cursor_paint CPU ARGB8888-over-RGB565 blend
candidates.where: patches/0071-esp32s31-lcd-fullscreen-present/esp32s31-lcd.c:3125-3265 (per-pixel loop :3214-3242; cursor_lift memcpy loop :3073-3122). #397: esp32s31_lcd_cursor_paint 774 B FLASH, esp32s31_lcd_cursor_lift 262 B FLASH, both calling flash memcpy
candidates.apps: every pointer move on lvdesk/Xorg desktops (the DRM cursor plane is composited by the CPU, docs/accel-plan.md:757-763)
candidates.heat: MEASURED: 2.5% of kernel-mode ticks in 60 s of windowed Doom on PROF=1 kernel #185, with kernel mode ~10% of wall (docs/frame-path-plan.md:131-138) => ~0.25% of wall; per-move cost is exported as dbg_paint_ns/dbg_paint_max but no captured value was found in the repo.
candidates.pathology: Runs from 80 MHz XIP flash (~6x RAM, docs/hot-text-plan.md); re-derives RGB565 from the ARGB sprite on every move although the sprite only changes on cursor_set; for each partially transparent pixel it does three integer divides by 255 plus 9 shifts/masks; per-pixel branch on alpha; lift is a per-row memcpy in flash memcpy.
candidates.replacement: At cursor_update (sprite change, rare) precompute per pixel: a 2-bit class (skip / opaque / blend), the opaque RGB565, and for blend pixels premultiplied sr*a, sg*a, sb*a and (255-a); also per-row runs of opaque pixels. Per move: memcpy opaque runs, skip transparent runs, and blend the few edge pixels with the exact divide (x*0x8081)>>23 (verified exact == x/255 for all x in [0,65025], build/cloud/probes/wide-kdrv). Place cursor_paint/cursor_lift (~1 KB) in .text..fast.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: paint cost 3-5x lower (mostly opaque/transparent pixels become run copies/skips, no divides, RAM-resident); ~0.2% of wall under pointer motion and a shorter per-move tail for cursor latency.
candidates.exactness: Output pixels must be bit-identical to the current formula ((s*a + d*(255-a))/255 then &0xf8/<<8 etc.); (x*0x8081)>>23 is exact over the full 0..65025 domain; the a==0 skip and a==0xff direct paths must stay as they are.

candidates.name: dw_mmc IDMAC descriptor ring: whole 4 KiB ring synced DMA_BIDIRECTIONAL on every request
candidates.where: patches/0066-dw-mmc-keepalive/dw_mmc.c:132 (DESC_RING_BUF_SZ = PAGE_SIZE), :358-363 (dw_mci_idmac_sync_for_device syncs the full ring), called at :1737 and :1825 (end of prepare_desc64/32, every request); per-descriptor sync_desc_for_cpu before OWN check :1689-1693/:1776-1780; streaming (cached) ring because Sv32 has no uncached coherent memory :4789-4801. dw_mci_* is in RAM (.text..fast), but the cache ops it calls are FLASH: arch_sync_dma_for_device 44 B, esp32s31_cache_range 184 B, esp32s31_cache_issue/wait_done/align_range, all FLASH and deliberately kept there (scripts/board/fastfn-pick.py:39-44)
candidates.apps: every SD read/write, dominated by swap-in faults (GLQuake runs with 13-14 MB swapped), app launches, file reads
candidates.heat: MEASURED: GLQuake 4 x 8,000 hart-1 PC samples (artifacts/gl/glquake/prof9 + kfast/prof10a-c, resolved against kfast/base-nm.txt by build/cloud/probes/wide-kdrv/res.py): esp32s31_cache_* + arch_sync_dma_* = 180 samples (0.56% of hart-1), all in flash; the mmc/dw_mci path total 634 samples (2.0%). What share of the cache samples comes from the ring sync vs set_pte/damage flushes is NOT separated.
candidates.pathology: A 4 KiB swap-in uses one 16-byte descriptor, but the driver writes back and invalidates the whole 4 KiB ring (BIDIRECTIONAL) per request, then does another cache op per descriptor while polling OWN; each op takes the IRQ-saving cache lock, issues the cache-controller command and spins in esp32s31_cache_wait_done, from flash.
candidates.replacement: Track [desc_first, desc_last] in prepare_desc32/64 and dma_sync_single_range_for_device only those bytes (rounded to cache lines), DMA_TO_DEVICE (the CPU wrote them; the device only writes back OWN, which the per-descriptor for_cpu sync already handles). In the OWN-check loop, skip the for_cpu sync for descriptors that were never handed to the device since the last init (the ring is re-zeroed only in dw_mci_idmac_init). Secondary, board-verify-only: whether the post-DMA invalidate of the 4 KiB data page is redundant with the pre-DMA one depends on whether the S31 D-cache can speculatively refill - do not assume.
candidates.est_gain: INFERRED: one 4 KiB writeback+invalidate becomes a 1-line (32/64 B) clean per request; if cache-op time scales with range this removes most of the ring's share of the 0.56% cache-op samples, i.e. a fraction of a percent of hart-1 in swap-heavy games plus a few us off each swap-in fault (faultlat p50 0.90-1.04 ms, patches/0069-esp32s31-fastfn-swap-path/README).
candidates.exactness: Device must see every descriptor field the CPU wrote (des0-des3/des4-5) before the DBADDR/poll-demand kick; untouched descriptors must be clean in cache (they are, after init's sync). A/B with sdlat/faultlat and the 0064 sdtrace for any IDMAC descriptor-unavailable/OWN-timeout errors.

candidates.name: HID report path (hid-core / hid-input / hidp / hosted-HID) still in XIP flash, and never profiled
candidates.where: #397 (artifacts/gl/glquake/kfast/base-nm.txt): hid_report_raw_event 826 B, hidinput_hid_event 926 B, hid_process_event 196 B, hid_field_extract 144 B, hid_input_array_field 168 B, hidinput_report_event 44 B, hid_input_report 12 B, hidp_input_report 420 B - all FLASH; downstream input_event/input_handle_event/evdev_events are RAM (patches/0007-esp32s31-fast-input-text.patch)

Closest MEASURED sibling: moving input.o + evdev.o (18 KB) into .text..fast gave +3.8% CoreMark under continuous pointer motion, ranges non-overlapping, with a cold-object control at -7.1% (docs/hot-text-plan.md 'What else was worth adding'). result.name: alsa-lib route plugin mono->stereo (snd_pcm_route_convert1_one) / plug-chain copies under s31route
result.tested:
The proposed replacement already exists and has shipped, so this candidate offers no new win on the codec path. Commit 27217c9 (2026-09-27) makes s31route open hw:0,0 directly for the codec sink and do the mono-to-stereo duplication itself. That code is s31rs_dup, rootfs/s31resample.h:299, called from rootfs/s31route.c:855, with CONV_DUP chosen at s31route.c:458. The shipped .so's dup loop is lh / addi / addi / sh / sh / bne, 6 instructions per frame (disassembly at 0x2450 in build/cloud/probes/wide-1/plugin.dis).

result.name: alsa-lib 'linear' rate converter (linear_expand/linear_shrink behind plug)
result.tested:
Everything is in /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-0/. No tracked files were changed and no make targets were run.
1) ORIGINAL: orig.c holds linear_expand_s16, linear_shrink_s16, input_frames/output_frames (with muldiv/muldiv_near) and linear_adjust_pitch, extracted verbatim by sed from alsa-lib 1.2.15.3 src/pcm/pcm_rate_linear.c and pcm_local.h. linear_init is the source logic with format selection reduced to S16. Fidelity check: `s31-cc -O2 -mtune=esp-base` gives linear_expand_s16 = 0x116 bytes, which matches the board libasound nm exactly (artifacts/gl/glquake/nm/libasound.so.2.0.0.nm: `000686da 00000116 t linear_expand_s16`). shrink_s16 is 0x128 against the board's 0x130.
2) REPLACEMENT (repl.c): a fused path for interleaved S16 with 1 or 2 channels. It computes the weight once per frame instead of once per channel, and rewrites old*ow+new*nw as (old<<16)+(new-old)*nw, which is identical modulo 2^32. The divu is either kept (R_MAGIC=0) or replaced by an exact reciprocal (R_MAGIC=1, M=ceil(2^48/d), exact for n<2^32 and d<2^16). The R_PACK variant writes each stereo frame with one 32-bit store. Any other layout or channel count falls back to the original.
3) Differential test (test.c): 14 directed board geometries x ch 1/2 x 3 layouts (interleaved, planar, swapped). Then 20,000 random cases: rates 4k-768k, random periods, ch 1-3, planar layouts, random offsets, short src_frames (the clamp path), random dst_frames (the shrink overflow/sanity path, hit 1,543 times), consecutive calls carrying old_sample, and checks of the output buffer with guards, the state and input_frames. Commands: `s31-qemu ./difft1 20000`, `./difft0 20000`, `./difftp 20000`, and `./difft1 3000 bad` for the negative control.
4) The magic divide was checked on the host (magicchk.c): every d in [1,65535] x 2000 numerators (edge values and random) = 131,070,000 checks.
5) End to end: alsa-lib 1.2.15.3 built static for QEMU (`./configure --host=riscv32-esp-linux-musl --enable-static --disable-shared ...`, CC=s31-cc). drive.c runs plug -> rate -> file -> null at 44100 S16 2ch, with an app period of 768 frames @36k / buffer x4, matching the board's slave 940/3764 (the board shows 941). Variant libraries swap in pcm_rate_linear.o with rate->func pointed at the replacement (libasound_r.a) or at the bad control (libasound_b.a). The output .raw files were compared with cmp.
6) Instruction counts: `s31-qemu -plugin /plugins/libinsn.so -d plugin`, taking the (101 calls - 1 call) difference with bench.c for the converter alone, and the (201 - 1 periods) difference with drive.c for the whole plug path.
result.exactness:
MEASURED: 0 mismatches in every variant. difft1 (magic), difft0 (divu) and difftp (packed) each ran 19,470 cases / 49,032 calls / 93,154,570 output samples. The magic divide had 0 bad in 131,070,000 host checks. End to end, the plug->rate->file output was byte-IDENTICAL for divu and magic at 36000 st/mono, 22050 st/mono, 12000 st, 11025 mono, 96000 st, 88200 mono and 64000 st (about 173 KB each).
Negative controls both fail as they should. A 1-LSB weight bug (w & ~1) gave 2,338,204 mismatches in 15.1 M samples in the unit test, and 14,321 differing bytes end to end.
Frame accounting (input_frames/output_frames/adjust_pitch) is unchanged by construction. The code is the same and plug's negotiation is untouched because the replacement stays behind the same `convert` op with no get_supported_formats.
Caveat: the source is alsa-lib 1.2.15.3, and the REPORT names 1.2.15. The expand function's size matches the board byte for byte.
result.icount:
Converter alone (bench.c, -O2 -mtune=esp-base), instructions per output frame:
| case | original | fused divu | fused magic | fused divu + packed store |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| 36000->44100 stereo | 37.91 | 31.56 | 39.57 | 31.57 |
| 36000->44100 mono | 18.98 | 22.28 | 30.28 | - |
| 22050->44100 stereo | 34.21 | 27.25 | 35.27 | 27.26 |
| 22050->44100 mono | 17.15 | 19.21 | 27.22 | - |
| 11025/12000 x4 stereo | 31.10 | 23.63 | 31.63 | - |
| 96000/88200->48000/44100 stereo (shrink) | 52.20 | 44.23 | 52.23 | - |
| same, mono | 26.15 | 33.20 | 41.20 | - |
The original inner loop (disassembled) has one divu, two mul and one sh per sample per channel. For stereo that is 2 divu and 2 sh per frame, in two separate passes over dst. The fused stereo version has 1 divu and 1 sw per frame.
Whole plug path per 44.1 kHz output frame (drive.c), original / fused-divu / fused-magic:
| case | original | fused divu | fused magic |
|---|---|---|---|
| 36000 stereo | 50.3 | 45.6 | 51.6 |
| 36000 mono | 46.9 | 50.2 | 58.2 |
| 22050 stereo | 45.7 | 40.5 | 46.5 |
| 12000 stereo | 42.3 | 36.8 | 42.8 |
| 96000 stereo | 73.6 | 71.4 | 77.4 |
| 44100 stereo direct, no rate plugin | 4.1 | - | - |
The whole alsa-lib rate path is about 46 instructions per output frame, not 590. The best exact replacement saves 5-7 instructions and 1 divu per stereo frame, and is worse for mono.
result.notes:
REFUTED for this board as it ships today, on three independent grounds.
(1) The stated pathology is wrong. Plug's rate plugin runs with S16 in and out (board log: "MMAP_INTERLEAVED format: S16_LE", raw/tone-h2-sinf.txt), so linear_init selects linear_expand_s16 or linear_shrink_s16 (pcm_rate_linear.c linear_init). The label-dispatched generic linear_expand/linear_shrink never run. The S16 loop is already tight: about 19 instructions per sample-channel (MEASURED).
(2) The heat is gone. The codec path no longer goes through plug or linear at all. Option 3 is SHIPPED (artifacts/audio/first-principles-2026-09-27/IMPLEMENT.md:96-118, commit 27217c9): s31route opens hw:0,0 directly and converts with its own float polyphase filter (203/302 cycles per frame mono/stereo). Kernel #401 / patches/0074 also made 22050, 24000 and 32000 native. The only remaining exposure to alsa-lib linear is: the Bluetooth loopback sink, which still goes through plug: (rootfs/s31route.c:368, 506-513) when the app rate differs from the rate s31-bt opened; S31ROUTE_PLUG=1; or apps that open plughw directly. No heat is measured for any of these.
(3) The gain estimate does not hold. The whole plug->rate->null path measures about 46 instructions per 44.1k output frame under QEMU. So the board's "~590 cycles/frame" (REPORT.md:85) cannot come from instruction count in this converter, and a rewrite of the arithmetic cannot recover "~7% of a core". INFERRED: the board cost is more likely per-write fixed overhead (REPORT.md:82 puts it at ~0.8-1 ms per write, and the 590 figure is a cross-geometry difference: 36k/512-callback against 44.1k/2048) plus stalls. The stall candidates are 2 divu per stereo frame (divider latency on the S31 is not recorded anywhere in the repo, so this is untestable here) and 16-bit stores straight into the uncached internal-SRAM DMA ring (esp32s31-i2s.c:5-9 and :264: "every store into that SRAM stalls on the bus"), written in two per-channel passes.
What would help, if the BT-loopback path ever gets heat: an external rate plugin (libasound_module_rate_*.so via defaults.pcm.rate_converter) with the fused bit-exact stereo path. It does 1 divu instead of 2 and one 32-bit store instead of two 16-bit stores per frame, and it is proven exact here (0 mismatches in 93 M samples, and byte-identical end to end). Its value depends entirely on the divu latency and the uncached-store cost, and only the board can price those.
The magic-reciprocal variant costs more instructions than divu (the 64-bit multiply). It is only worth having if divu is slower than about 8 cycles. Mono should keep the original loop.
Sources: pcm_rate.c:1411 lists default_rate_plugins as {"speexrate","linear"}, so each open also attempts a failing dlopen of speexrate. That is an open-time cost only.

label: probe:2:SDL2 ALSA hotplug thread: snd_device_name_hint() eve

result.name: SDL2 ALSA hotplug thread: cache snd_device_name_hint() behind a byte-exact validity key (dlsym interposition)
result.tested:
All work is under /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-2/. No tracked files were changed (git status is clean) and no make targets were run.

Sources, at the pinned versions (fetched):
- alsa-lib 1.2.15.3 (the version docs cite). The board's libasound uses 0x302 bytes for snd_device_name_hint (artifacts/gl/tyrquake/nm/libasound.so.2.0.0.nm). My s31-cc build uses 0x2dc, so it is the same source with different codegen.
- SDL2 2.32.10, matching the board's libSDL2-2.0.so.0.3200.10.

SDL source confirms the call path:
- SDL_alsa_audio.c:839-955 is the iteration; :972-985 runs it every 5 s; :30-31 hard-codes SDL_ALSA_HOTPLUG_THREAD=1 at compile time, so there is no runtime off switch.
- libasound is dlopen'd, and the board libSDL2 nm has no U snd_* symbols. Symbols are loaded with dlsym(handle, ...) (:103-110). musl only searches that handle's own dependencies, so a plain preload export is never seen. Interposing dlsym is required.

Builds (s31-cc, board ISA, no D):
- alsa-lib 1.2.15.3 as a shared library (configure --host=riscv32-esp-linux-musl CC=s31-cc).
- t/wide2hint.c + t/dlstub.S + t/resolve.c -> libwide2.so, the replacement:
  - An asm dlsym stub. RTLD_NEXT tail-jumps to the real dlsym with ra untouched, because musl's dlsym is `mv a2,ra; tail __dlsym`. I checked that shape in the toolchain libc.so.
  - Every other dlsym call goes through C. For the name snd_device_name_hint it returns s31_hint.
  - s31_hint returns a malloc'd deep copy of the last real result while a byte-exact key (memcmp, not a hash) is unchanged. The key is: card, iface, the whole environ, stat of each key path (dev/ino/mode/size/mtim/ctim, errno), stat of every directory entry, and the bytes of /proc/asound/cards.
  - The real snd_device_name_free_hint frees the copy correctly (it is per-string free() plus free() of the array; namehint.c:686-700), so free_hint needs no wrapper.
  - Real dlsym is found lazily through dl_iterate_phdr and a libc .dynsym walk.
- t/fakesnd.c -> libfakesnd.so, a fixture. It makes placeholder files behave like /dev/snd/controlC0 (S31Codec, 1 pcm device) and controlC1 (Loopback, 2 devices) by emulating the PVERSION, CARD_INFO, PCM_NEXT_DEVICE and PCM_INFO ioctls, so the card path runs under QEMU.
- t/hinttest.c, an SDL-shaped driver: dlopen, dlsym(handle), N x {hint(-1,"pcm"), SDL's NAME/IOID get_hint walk, free_hint}, with scripted mutations and dlsym edge-case probes.
- t/mkroot.sh builds the fixture root: the board's lean alsa.conf with its hook paths pointed into the root, plus the board's /etc/asound.conf.
- Run with t/run.sh {orig|cache|neg|ra} N MUT [qemu args]. Instruction counts use `-plugin /plugins/libinsn.so -d plugin`. Syscalls use `-strace`. Per-function profiles use t/libhb.so (hotblocks with no entry limit) and t/prof.py.
result.exactness:
MEASURED, QEMU, 16 iterations with 7 scripted mutations between calls:
1. Append a hinted pcm.foo to etc/asound.conf.
2. Remove card 1 (rename controlC1).
3. Restore card 1.
4. Same-size in-place edit Foo->Bar (same length, only mtime changes).
5. setenv ALSA_CARD=1.
6. Create a new file in etc/alsa/conf.d.
7. Same-size edit of that file.

Mutations 1-4, 6 and 7 changed the real output; setenv did not change it.

Results:
- Cache vs original, 2-card fixture: stdout is byte-identical (CACHE_IDENTICAL). That covers every hint string and its order, the count, rc, the errno value going into each call, the bad-iface path (-22) and the NULL-hints path (-22).
- Cache vs original, 1-card fixture: identical as well.
- NEGATIVE CONTROL 1 (libwide2neg.so, key check disabled): 104 differing lines (2 cards) and 76 (1 card). The stale list is caught at the first mutation.
- dlsym transparency: dlsym(h,"nosuch")=NULL, dlsym(RTLD_DEFAULT,"printf") and dlsym(h,"snd_device_name_get_hint") are unchanged. RTLD_NEXT from the executable resolves malloc to libc and open to libfakesnd, the same as without the preload. RTLD_NEXT issued from inside the preload (as s31clk.c does) resolves clock_gettime to libc. Both hold on the lazy first-dlsym path too.
- NEGATIVE CONTROL 2 (libwide2ra.so: RTLD_NEXT routed through C, so ra is lost): RTLD_NEXT "open" wrongly resolves to libc instead of libfakesnd. The harness catches the ra hazard.

Residual assumptions (INFERRED):
- The result depends only on the keyed state. On this board /usr/share/alsa is on the read-only XIP overlay, so only /etc, $HOME, /dev/snd and the environment can change at runtime, and all of them are keyed.
- A config @func that reads some other live state would not be tracked. None of the lean config's funcs do this: they are getenv, igetenv, refer and concat.
- On a cache hit, errno is preserved from entry, while the original may leave ENOENT behind. It was the same in every run here, and SDL never reads it.
result.icount:
MEASURED, QEMU libinsn. Per call = (N=21 minus N=11)/10. Totals include the SDL-shaped get_hint walk, which is tiny in both arms.

| Case | Instructions/call | Syscalls/call |
|---|---|---|
| 2 cards, original | 3,552,613 | 286 |
| 2 cards, cache hit | 52,339 (68x fewer) | 32 (8.9x fewer) |
| 1 card (board: /proc/asound/cards shows only the simple-card, current-state.md:8440), original | 2,951,072 | 226 |
| 1 card, cache hit | 48,331 (61x fewer) | 31 |

One-time costs of the preload: +155k instructions and +69 syscalls at N=1. That covers loading the library, resolving dlsym and the first miss (key + copy).

Where the original's instructions go (hotblocks):
- musl malloc/free/get_meta/alloc_slot/calloc: ~24%
- The config lexer/parser (get_char, get_string, get_char_skip_comments, parse_defs, getc): ~21%
- _snd_config_search/walk/add/copy/delete: ~12%
- memset/memcpy/strlen/strcmp: ~12%
- printf_core/__fwritex: ~4%

Cause: namehint.c:597 calls snd_config_update_r with a NULL config, which reparses every configuration file on every call. It then copies the tree (:600) and deletes both (:674-675).

Syscalls per original call, 2 cards:
- 45 x openat("libasound.so.2") + ~45 statx(fd) + 46 fcntl + close. alsa-lib dlopen()s its own path for every hook and @func evaluation (conf.c:4033 and :5186 go straight to snd_dlopen, bypassing the dlobj cache; dlmisc.c:131-155). musl answers a dlopen by path with open+fstat.
- 30 failed opens of controlC2..31 (snd_card_next probes all 32 slots).
- 8 opens of real controls.
- 14 mmap/munmap pairs (heap churn).
- About 12 config-file opens, stats and accesses.

Syscalls per cache hit: 13 statx, 4 getdents, 3 openat, 3 mmap/munmap, 2 close.

The hit is dominated by QEMU-sysroot musl's byte-wise memcmp of the key (35%). A hash pre-check or libs31fp's memcmp would shrink it further.
result.notes:
What the board has measured (cited, not measured here):
- One enumeration costs 0.35 s after the lean alsa.conf, down from 1.76 s, and runs every 5 s (perf-plan-2026-09-23.md:976-990).
- The hotplug thread measured 11% of CPU0 after the lean conf (same source), and 4.5% of CPU0 by tick accounting (audio-48k-plan-2026-09-25.md:214-222).
- The kernel profile named path_openat, link_path_walk and ovl_getattr. This run explains that: 45 of the ~50 opens per call are alsa-lib re-dlopening /usr/lib/libasound.so.2 through the XIP overlay, one per config @func or hook evaluation.

Estimate (INFERRED): the cache removes about 98% of the per-call user instructions and 89% of the syscalls. On a board it should recover most of the measured 4.5-11% of CPU0 on every SDL2 app, with residual cost of the order of 13 stats every 5 s. It also stops the whole-config allocate/free churn (14 mmap/munmap pairs) every 5 s, which matters on a machine short of RAM. Only the board can give the wall-time and CPU share; QEMU has no timing model.

Integration caveats for putting this in libs31fp:
1. libs31fp would EXPORT dlsym. That interposes every process running with the preload, but the asm stub keeps RTLD_NEXT semantics, which s31clk.c/s31str.c rely on; this was verified along with a negative control.
2. build-v3.sh's import allowlist would have to admit fstatat, openat, readdir, fdopendir, getenv, realloc, read and close, or the key would have to be built from raw syscalls.
3. The default board key list is in wide2hint.c (board_keys: /dev/snd, alsa.conf, /etc and /usr/etc asound.conf, three conf.d directories, $HOME/.asoundrc, and XDG asoundrc). S31_ALSA_KEYS overrides it; that override exists for the test only.
4. If the stock alsa.conf is ever restored, its /usr/share/alsa cards/pcm files sit on the read-only overlay and cannot change mid-process, so the key stays sound.
5. The lock is a non-blocking atomic flag: contention falls through to the uncached call, so there is no pthread import.

Simpler alternatives:
- SDL2 cannot switch hotplug off at runtime (compile-time macro), and patching SDL is outside the "off-the-shelf" rule.
- A separate, generic lever turned up: dlopen(path) of an already-loaded library costs open+fstat+fcntl+close in musl. It is left unexploited because a path-string match would not be exact if the file were replaced.

Binary caveat: the alsa-lib was built here from source. It is not the board's byte-identical libasound (function sizes differ: 0x2dc vs 0x302).

Files: t/wide2hint.c, t/dlstub.S, t/resolve.c, t/fakesnd.c, t/hinttest.c, t/mkroot.sh, t/run.sh, t/prof.py, and the outputs t/out-{orig,cache,neg}-mut.txt and t/o1-*.txt, all under /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-2/.

result.name: ALSA SYNC_PTR status/control mmap (kernel-fastpath) - wide-3
result.tested:
Everything is under /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-3/. No tracked files were modified and no make targets were run.

1. Kernel policy, read from source. Upstream sound/core/pcm_native.c was fetched at tag v7.1 and at master (pcm_native_v7.1.c and pcm_native_master.c); the mmap policy block is the same in both.
   - v7.1:3740-3869 allows the status and control page mmap only under `#if defined(CONFIG_X86) || defined(CONFIG_PPC) || defined(CONFIG_ALPHA)`. On every other architecture both pages return -ENXIO.
   - v7.1:3140-3183 is snd_pcm_sync_ptr(). It runs hwsync only when the HWSYNC flag is set. Otherwise it copies runtime->status and runtime->control under pcm_stream_lock_irq. So a SYNC_PTR without HWSYNC returns exactly what a mapped status page would show.
   - pcm.c v7.1:943/951: status and control are alloc_pages_exact() kernel pages that only hart1 touches.

2. Harness: the real alsa-lib 1.2.15.3 hw plugin run unmodified under QEMU.
   - It uses the existing static library ../wide-0/alsa-lib-1.2.15.3/src/.libs/libasound.a, built with s31-cc at -O2.
   - It is linked `-Wl,--wrap=ioctl,--wrap=mmap,--wrap=munmap,--wrap=poll` against mock.c, a mock of the kernel PCM that follows the v7.1 SYNC_PTR/WRITEI/HWSYNC semantics. The mock's pointer is period-granular, like the board's GDMA residue.
   - drive.c opens the device with snd1_pcm_hw_open_fd.
   - Build:
     - `s31-cc -O2 -I$AL/include/sound -c mock.c`
     - `s31-cc -O2 -I$AL/include -c drive.c`
     - `s31-cc -static -o drive drive.o mock.o $AL/src/.libs/libasound.a -Wl,--wrap=...`
   - Four arms:
     - A: both status and control mmap return ENXIO (the riscv behaviour today).
     - B: both pages mapped (x86 policy).
     - C: only a read-only status page mapped, which is the candidate's "own helper page" option.
     - N: negative control, B with a stale status page.
   - Two scenarios:
     - 1: hw direct, 1024-frame RW writei per period, the shape of SDL1/SDL2 blocking PlayDevice (SDL2 2.32.10 has SDL_ALSA_NON_BLOCKING 0).
     - 2: the rate(linear) plugin at 16 kHz over hw at 32 kHz, 512-frame app writes, the plug:rate shape.
   - Runs:
     - `s31-qemu ./drive <arm> <scen> 1000 [trace]` for syscall counts (counts.txt).
     - `s31-qemu -plugin /plugins/libinsn.so -d plugin ./drive <arm> <scen> {200,1200}`, taking the difference per 1000 periods (icount.txt).
   - With arm B, alsa-lib requested the NEW offsets 0x82000000/0x83000000. The musl sysroot defines __USE_TIME_BITS64 (bits/alltypes.h:45). So on the board the ENXIO comes purely from the arch #if; the 32-bit !CONFIG_64BIT refusal applies only to the OLD offsets.
result.exactness:
What the application sees was hashed after every write: the writei return, snd_pcm_state, avail_update, delay return and value, and snd_pcm_avail. 1000 periods per run:
- Scenario 1: arms A, B and C all give d0faf48d8dc9dde3.
- Scenario 2: arms A, B and C all give 77beab75feec0fe3.

The candidate is refuted as a worthwhile win, even though the mechanism and its exactness check out.
- **Mechanism confirmed.** Mapping both pages removes 50% of the kernel crossings in the direct-writei shape and 77% in the plug:rate shape, and the application sees bit-identical values.
- **Cost is too small.** The ceilings above bound it to about 0.05% (direct) to about 0.4% (plug:rate at 345/s) of a core. On today's shipping Quake path the function measures 0.03%. - Real per-call kernel cost (flash-resident entry path, lock contention).

result.tested:
Everything is under /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-5/. No tracked files were changed and no make targets were run.

ORIGINAL:
- musl 1.2.5 expf/logf/powf/hypotf plus their data files, copied from build/cloud/src/musl-1.2.5 into ref/. They are built for the host with a minimal libm.h shim, -O2 -ffp-contract=off (ref/libref_host.a), and used as the oracle for the exhaustive tests.
- Under QEMU, the reference is the QEMU sysroot libm, which is the same upstream musl.
- The toolchain libc (6041b2cd) contains all the same tables byte for byte (logf/powf/exp2f tabs, polys, InvLn2N; the python byte search found every one). Its own libc.a objects expf.o/logf.o/powf.o/hypotf.o were extracted, symbol-renamed and linked into tccmp. Their call census: expf 6 muldf3/4 adddf3/2 subdf3; logf 6/5/1; powf 14/10/3; hypotf 2 muldf3/1 adddf3 plus sqrtf.

REPLACEMENT (s31lm.h, tables generated by gen.py into consts.h):
- Each function re-evaluates musl's own formula (same k/i selection, same tables, same polynomial coefficients split into float hi+lo) in float-float arithmetic using fmadd.s.
- It returns RN_float of that value only when the value is more than M ulp from a rounding boundary (M = 2^-12 for expf/logf, 2^-16 for hypotf, 2^-10 for powf). In every other case it calls the original.
- It also delegates for: non-RNE frm (read with frrm); NaN, inf, zero, subnormal or negative inputs; |x| >= 87 in expf; |y| outside [2^-40, 2^20] in powf; |ylogx| between 125 and 128.5, or between -150.5 and -125; x after musl's scaling below 2^-26 in hypotf; and exact-tie risk on musl's k (|r| within 2^-26 or 2^-24 of 0.5).
- powf's clear overflow and underflow cases return musl's exact __math_oflowf/__math_uflowf expressions.
- Board build: s31lm_preload.c is an LD_PRELOAD shape with the fallback bound through dlsym(RTLD_NEXT). The shipping toolchain builds it as libs31lm-board.so (-O2 -fPIC): text 4,952 B (expf 624 B, logf 658 B, powf 1,158 B, hypotf 402 B, three 256 B tables). It contains 0 esp.* instructions and no soft-double or libm calls.

COMMANDS:
- Host oracle: gcc -O2 -mfma -ffp-contract=off -fopenmp host_exh.c ref/libref_host.a, then ./host_exh expf|logf (all 2^32 inputs), ./host_exh hypotf 4e8, ./host_exh powf 6e8, and MODE=0..5 ./host_exh powf 1e8 per domain.
- Host directed hypotf double-rounding search: hdr, 768 y values x 2^23 x, with a __float128 oracle.
- QEMU (board ISA, no D): s31-cc -O2 -ffp-contract=off -fno-builtin -fno-math-errno. Programs:
  - qtest: random inputs plus edge values, 25% random frm, comparing bits, fflags and errno.
  - qtest replaying host hard sets: hard_expf.bin, hard_logf.bin, hard_hypotf.keep, hard_powf_ziv.bin.
  - tccmp: toolchain libc.a objects vs upstream vs s31lm.
  - pchk: interposed through LD_PRELOAD vs dlopen'd libc.
- Instruction counts: qbench with /plugins/libinsn.so, computed as (count at N=1e5 minus count at N=0) / 1e5, with a null-call arm for loop overhead.
result.exactness:
MEASURED, 0 mismatches everywhere except the negative controls:
- expf, all 2^32 inputs on the host vs musl-1.2.5: 0 mismatches. 269,701 in-domain inputs took the Ziv/tie fallback (about 4.9e-4 of the fast domain).
- logf, all 2^32 inputs: 0 mismatches, 1,040,830 Ziv fallbacks.
- hypotf, 4e8 random (4 distributions): 0 mismatches, 9,806 Ziv fallbacks. The directed search found 6 genuine double-rounding pairs; all 6 fell back, 0 mismatches.
- powf, 6e8 random over 6 domains (any bits; |y| 2^-16..2^9; x near 1; half-integer y; |ylogx| near 120-130; x in [2^-5,32) with y in (0,200]): 0 mismatches.
- QEMU random, 20M cases (5M per function, random frm): 0 bit, 0 fflags and 0 errno mismatches.
- QEMU replay of the host hard sets: 0 mismatches for expf (269,701), logf (1,040,830), powf (26,938) and hypotf (6).

- Flags: injecting an underflow into the expf path (FLAGNEG) gives 123,927 of 1M flag mismatches.

- powf and hypotf are sampled, not exhaustive: 2^64 domain.
- The board's deployed libc 352e9417 was not available. Equivalence rests on toolchain libc 6041b2cd, whose tables and extracted objects match.

The replacement is about 140 single-precision instructions plus one frrm (25-30 ns CSR). That suggests 8-15x per call, but the fmadd.s latency on the S31 is unknown here.
result.notes:
Mechanism (B, interposition): export expf, logf, powf and hypotf from the preload.
- Fallback goes through dlsym(RTLD_NEXT), which pchk exercised.
- The float-float mirror of musl's own formula plus the Ziv test is what makes these bit-identical rather than merely accurate. This matters because musl logf and powf are not correctly rounded (0.82 ulp), so an "accurate" float libm would NOT match musl.

Remaining risks and next steps:

- powf and hypotf exactness is sampled, not proven. A rigorous error bound for the Ziv margins is not derived; the margins are empirical, with 2^4-2^8 headroom over the first observed failure.

label: probe:4:musl float libm evaluated in soft double: sinf/cosf/

result.name: musl float trig (sinf/cosf/sincosf/tanf) on the single-precision FPU, bit-identical to musl through a proven-rounding test with libc fallback
result.tested:
All work is in /home/user/esp32-s31-linux/build/cloud/probes/wide-4/. No tracked files were changed and no make targets were run.

REPLACEMENT: s31trig.c, compiled with -ffp-contract=off. It reproduces musl 1.2.5's own algorithm, not the true sin. It keeps the same branch thresholds (0x3f490fda, 0x4016cbe3, 0x407b53d1, 0x40afeddf, 0x40e231d5) and uses musl's exact double constants, split into 2 or 3 floats by gen.c into consts.h: s1..s4pio2, invpio2, pio2_1/pio2_1t, S1-S4, C0-C3 and T0-T5.
- Reduction is exact float-float using fmadd.s. For the medium path, n comes from fcvt.w.s with rne. It delegates when frac(x*2/pi) is more than 0.4999 away, so musl's rint cannot differ.
- musl's __sindf, __cosdf and __tandf polynomials are evaluated in float-float. tanf's -1/r is a float reciprocal plus one FMA Newton correction.
- Rounding test: fh+(fl+d) must equal fh+(fl-d) with d = 2^-34*|fh|. If not, it tail-calls libc.
- It also tail-calls libc when frrm != RNE, when |x| >= 2^23, and on the medium path when the sin kernel gets |y| < 2^-14 (to cover musl's rounding of fn*pio2_1t). Tiny inputs, Inf and NaN use musl's own FORCE_EVAL ops.
- Code size is 4,616 bytes of .text for all four functions.

ORIGINAL:
- musl 1.2.5 sources (build/cloud/src/musl-1.2.5/src/math) compiled on the host with a stub libm.h, symbols renamed with objcopy (ref/).
- Under QEMU: the QEMU sysroot's musl 1.2.5 libc.so, and the TOOLCHAIN libc.so 6041b2cd itself. tltest.c copies its PT_LOAD image into an RWX mapping and calls sinf at 0x3cd00, cosf at 0x2c348, sincosf at 0x3c7a2 and tanf at 0x3da66. I confirmed all their callees (__sindf, __cosdf, __tandf, __rem_pio2f, __rem_pio2_large, the libgcc df3 helpers, scalbn, floor) are direct jal calls with pc-relative data and no esp.* instructions.

COMMANDS:
- Host exhaustive (exh.c): `./exh {0,1,2,3}` over all 2^32 inputs, 4 threads, output in exhaustive-host.txt. The negative control is `exh_neg_eps0` (EPS=0).
- QEMU differential (qtest.c, sysroot libc): `s31-qemu ./qtest 200000` runs 4M calls over random bit patterns, 2^-12..2^23 magnitudes, points near k*pi/4, and every branch threshold, with both signs, in all 5 rounding modes, comparing values and fflags. `s31-qemu ./qtest 0x3f000000 0x3f800000 x` covers one exhaustive binade, run for both the real and the negative-control build. Output in qemu-diff.txt.
- Toolchain-libc differential (tltest.c):
  - binade [0.5,1) exhaustive in RNE, plus its negative control;
  - `0..0x80000000 step 4093` × both signs × 5 rounding modes, with fflags;
  - `0x39000000..0x4b100000 step 97` in RNE.
  Output in tl-diff.txt.
- Instruction counts: `s31-qemu -plugin /plugins/libinsn.so -d plugin ./icb <op> 20000 <kind>` minus the same run with 0 calls, divided by 20000. Output in icount.txt.
result.exactness:
MEASURED:
- Host, all 2^32 inputs against musl 1.2.5 source: 0 mismatches for each of sinf, cosf, tanf and sincosf (both outputs).
- Delegation: overall 41.18-41.21%, almost all of it |x| >= 2^23, which is 1,761,607,680 inputs and delegated by design. Inside the |x| < 2^23 domain (2,516,582,400 inputs) it delegates:
  - sinf: 7,271,490 (0.289%)
  - cosf: 7,339,978 (0.292%)
  - tanf: 7,192,914 (0.286%)
  - sincosf: 8,263,202 (0.328%)

NEGATIVE CONTROL: EPS=0, the same code without the rounding margin. Over all 2^32 inputs it gives 928 sinf, 888 cosf, 10 tanf and 1,816 sincosf mismatches (first bad inputs e.g. 0x3f14ba76 and 0x3f3375dc). So the harness does detect the rare misroundings, and the margin is what removes them.

QEMU cross-check against the sysroot musl, binade [0.5,1):
- 0 mismatches for the real build.
- The negative control gives 43 sinf, 49 cosf, 0 tanf and 92 sincosf, identical to the host counts for that binade. So the host simulation equals real rv32 codegen.
- Random + edge run: 4,000,000 calls, 0 value mismatches, 0 fflags mismatches, all 5 rounding modes (directed modes delegate through frrm).

Against the TOOLCHAIN libc 6041b2cd:
- Binade [0.5,1), both signs: 67,108,864 calls, 0 mismatches. The negative control gives 368 = 2×(43+49+0+92).
- Whole float range at step 4093, both signs, 5 rounding modes: 20,986,920 calls, 0 value and 0 flag mismatches.
- 2^-13..2^23 at step 97: 24,992,864 calls, 0 value and 0 flag mismatches.

result.icount:
QEMU libinsn, instructions per call, original libc (sysroot musl 1.2.5) → replacement. Counts include about 5 loop instructions, plus amortized delegation.

| Input set | sinf | cosf | sincosf | tanf |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| x = 0.7..20.7 (census input) | 2742 → 133 (20.6x) | 2751 → 132 | 4693 → 208 (22.6x) | 3494 → 242 (14.4x) |
| x over -pi..pi (direct branches) | 2044 → 107 (19.1x) | 2046 → 106 | 3988 → 177 (22.5x) | 2792 → 218 (12.8x) |
| x = 10..1000 (medium reduction) | 3064 → 140 (21.9x) | 3064 → 139 | 5010 → 214 (23.4x) | 3804 → 251 (15.2x) |

The earlier census figures (sinf 2104, cosf 2049, sincosf 4024, tanf 2789) sit inside these ranges.

The replacement's path is about 60-90 single-precision FP ops (mostly fmadd.s, fmul.s, fadd.s), one frrm CSR read, and for tanf one fdiv.s. It makes no calls on the fast path.
result.notes:
Why this is exact: it does not approximate sin. It estimates musl's own double value before rounding, to about 2^-40, using musl's own reduction constants and polynomials. It returns only when that value is at least 2^-34 relative away from a float rounding boundary, and otherwise tail-calls libc. The replicated constants matter: musl's s2pio2 differs from pi by about 2^-53, which is about 2^-29.6 relative at x = 3.14159274f, so a "truly accurate" FPU sin would NOT match musl there.

This answers the perf-review-2026-09-23.md:98-104 objection ("float trig is ≤1 ulp, not bit-identical"): a bit-identical version is feasible and verified exhaustively.

Mechanism: the replacement is interposition (B). tiopex-quake is a dynamic PIE and imports sincosf through its PLT: 12 sincosf@plt sites and 1 direct, MEASURED by objdump of rootfs/tiopex-quake. It also has 9 sin@plt call sites, which are double and out of scope. A v3-style s31trig.so would export sinf, cosf, sincosf and tanf and fall back through dlsym(RTLD_NEXT).

Cost of the frm guard: frrm on every call (board CSR cost 25-30 ns per the brief). A caller that sets FE_TOWARDZERO etc. always delegates, and that path was verified equal.

UNTESTABLE HERE:
- Cycles and ns per call: QEMU has no timing model, and the fmadd.s latency and the length of the serial FP dependency chain are unknown on the board.
- App-level gain: the only measured heat is the aggregate "libm bodies 0.91% of CPU0" plus 3.17% in soft-double helpers on software Quake (perf-review-2026-09-23.md:100), with no per-function caller counts. INFERRED gain is a large share of the sincosf part of that, but the call rate needs the counting shim that perf-review:106 proposes.
- Per-sample float synths would gain most: about 20x fewer instructions per call, INFERRED from the 9 us/sinf board figure cited in the candidate.

Remaining limits:
- Board libc 352e9417 is not verified. The next board step is an md5 dump comparison, like the roadmap's A5 plan.
- |x| >= 2^23 always delegates. The limit could be raised with more reduction-exactness analysis.
